FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM on off: only mirror files, do not back up the database.
LITESTREAM_SSE_C_KEY empty Optional: the storage provider encrypts the Litestream replica (SSE-C, 32 bytes base64, only over https and with providers that support SSE-C).
Details: Storage, S3 and backups.

en.heading: Encryption
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY empty 32 bytes, base64 (openssl rand -base64 32). Encrypts files in the bucket, scheduled backups, Markdown exports and the instance backup. Without a key nothing changes.
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE empty Instead of the variable: path to a file holding the key (Docker secret).
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS empty Earlier keys, comma-separated – only for reading after a key change.
Details: Encryption.

en.heading: Stored secrets
paragraphs: Flowplan stores AI provider keys, the keys of authenticator apps (two-factor sign-in) and the access tokens of the Git export of spaces only encrypted (AES-256-GCM, bound to their place). The key for this comes, in this order, from:
Source Meaning
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY If set, it also encrypts the stored secrets.
FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY / FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY_FILE A key just for this: 32 bytes, base64 or hex (openssl rand -base64 32), or the path to a file (Docker secret).
secrets.key in the data folder Without the two variables, Flowplan creates this file itself when first needed (readable only by its owner).

[!IMPORTANT] The instance backup deliberately leaves out secrets.key – it doesn't belong next to the data it protects. Back up the file separately or set the key as a variable. If it is missing after a restore, admins and users enter their AI keys again, and for two-factor sign-in recovery codes or a reset by an administrator help.

en.heading: E-mail (SMTP)
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
SMTP_HOST empty Turns on sending e-mail: invitations, address confirmations, password resets and digests of unread notifications.
SMTP_PORT 587 Port. With 465 Flowplan speaks TLS directly, STARTTLS otherwise.
SMTP_SECURE by port true/false forces TLS from the start of the connection.
SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASSWORD empty Sign-in at the mail server.
SMTP_FROM Flowplan Sender, e.g. Flowplan .
Check delivery under Administration → E-mail → Send test email.

en.heading: Inbound e-mail (IMAP)
paragraphs: For inbound e-mail via webhook (Mailgun, Postmark, SendGrid, Cloudflare) nothing needs to be set. A mailbox of your own is polled over IMAP every two minutes:
Variable Default Meaning
INBOUND_MAIL_DOMAIN empty Domain of the inbound addresses, e.g. mail.example.com. The settings then show inbox+@mail.example.com for each address.
INBOUND_IMAP_HOST empty Turns on IMAP polling (together with INBOUND_IMAP_USER).
INBOUND_IMAP_PORT 993 Port (143 when INBOUND_IMAP_TLS=false).
INBOUND_IMAP_USER / INBOUND_IMAP_PASSWORD empty Sign-in at the mailbox. The part before @ is also the part before + in the addresses.
INBOUND_IMAP_FOLDER INBOX Folder that is polled.
INBOUND_IMAP_TLS true false only for a mail server on the same host or network (unencrypted).

The mail server must support plus addressing (inbox+anything@… is delivered to inbox@…); Dovecot, Postfix, Gmail/Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 (switch it on there) do. Flowplan marks processed e-mails as read and deletes nothing.

en.heading: Integrations
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning

FLOWPLAN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true allows webhooks to internal addresses and http:// – such as Home Assistant or n8n in the same network. Without this variable only public HTTPS addresses are allowed.
SPACE_GIT_EXPORT empty true turns on the Git export of spaces: space owners push their space into a repository of their own, daily or weekly.
SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Allowed Git servers for it, comma-separated (e.g. git.example.org). Without it any public https:// server is allowed; internal addresses never.

SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a Forgejo on the same host that the container reaches via --add-host git.example.org:host-gateway. Only works together with the list; every other server stays limited to public addresses.

ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Own servers for the GitHub and GitLab issue sync, comma-separated (e.g. gitlab.example.org). github.com and gitlab.com are always allowed; other servers only when listed here.
ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a GitLab in the same network. Only works together with the list.

PLUGIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS empty HTTPS origins owners may register block extensions from, comma-separated (e.g. https://plugins.example.org). Without it only when the administration switches on Block extensions from any HTTPS address. The origins are also added to the frame-src of the Content Security Policy.

GIPHY_API_KEY / TENOR_API_KEY empty Key for the GIF search on whiteboards at GIPHY or Tenor (if both are set, GIPHY wins). Without a key the GIFs tab is hidden. Searches run through the server; chosen GIFs up to 8 MB are stored on the server.
EXPORT_GIT_* empty Deprecated: the Git export of the whole instance, see Push into a Git repository. Keeps working; the Git export of spaces is the better choice.

en.heading: Calendar sync
paragraphs: Two-way sync of database views with Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook / 365. Each person connects their own account; without a client ID that provider stays hidden. Flowplan asks for changes every ten minutes (the providers' push notifications are not used – they would need a publicly reachable HTTPS address verified with the provider).
Variable Default Meaning

GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET empty OAuth client (type “Web application”) from the Google Cloud Console, with the Google Calendar API enabled and the scope …/auth/calendar. Redirect URI: /api/calendar-sync/callback/google.

MS_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID / MS_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET empty App registration in Microsoft Entra ID (web platform) with the delegated permissions Calendars.ReadWrite and offline_access. Redirect URI: /api/calendar-sync/callback/microsoft.
MS_CALENDAR_TENANT common common (work and personal accounts), organizations or a tenant ID.
People's refresh tokens are stored sealed in the database (like all stored secrets).

en.heading: Legal and interface
paragraphs: Variable Default Meaning
IMPRINT_URL empty Link to the legal notice, e.g. https://example.com/imprint. Shown on the sign-in page, under shared pages and forms and in the account menu – only when set.
PRIVACY_URL empty Link to the privacy policy, in the same places and also only when set.

en.heading: Voice notes (Whisper)
paragraphs: Voice notes in the editor are always stored as audio. With a Whisper service in your own network, Flowplan also turns them into text; the recording never leaves your server.
Variable Default Meaning
WHISPER_URL empty Address of an OpenAI-compatible Whisper server (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions), e.g. http://whisper:8000. Turns transcription on.
WHISPER_MODEL Systran/faster-whisper-small The model name as the service expects it.
WHISPER_LANGUAGE de Language of the recordings (e.g. en).
WHISPER_API_KEY empty Only if the service requires a key.
WHISPER_MAX_MB 200 Largest recording in MB.
WHISPER_RESPONSE_FORMAT verbose_json Response format of speech recognition; falls back to json once.
WHISPER_DIARIZE empty on: ask for speaker separation (diarize=true), only for services that support it.
Example with speaches (formerly faster-whisper-server) in the same Compose project:
whisper:
image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cpu
volumes:
- whisper-models:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
restart: unless-stopped
Then set WHISPER_URL=http://whisper:8000 for Flowplan. Newer speaches versions do not download models by themselves; download it once, for example from the Flowplan container:
node -e "fetch('http://whisper:8000/v1/models/Systran/faster-whisper-small',{method:'POST'}).then(r=>console.log(r.status))"

small needs about 1 GB of memory and transcribes roughly in real time on a normal CPU; base is faster and less accurate, medium more accurate and considerably slower. Do not make the Whisper service publicly reachable – only Flowplan talks to it.

en.heading: AI
paragraphs: All optional; the values apply until an admin saves under Administration → AI. Details: AI.
Variable Default Meaning
FLOWPLAN_AI off on switches AI on.
FLOWPLAN_AI_PROVIDER empty ollama, openai (OpenAI-compatible), anthropic or gemini. If only OLLAMA_URL is set, Ollama is used.
OLLAMA_URL empty Address of Ollama, e.g. http://ollama:11434 with the Compose service.
FLOWPLAN_AI_BASE_URL per provider Address of the provider, e.g. https://api.mistral.ai/v1 for an OpenAI-compatible service.
FLOWPLAN_AI_MODEL empty Model, e.g. llama3.1 or gpt-4o-mini.
FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL empty Model for semantic search, e.g. nomic-embed-text (Ollama). Without it: full-text search only.
FLOWPLAN_AI_API_KEY / FLOWPLAN_AI_API_KEY_FILE empty The provider's key. Never stored in the database and only used for the provider from the variables.
FLOWPLAN_AI_ACCESS everyone selected: only people who were enabled.
FLOWPLAN_AI_GUESTS off on: guests may use AI too.
FLOWPLAN_AI_USER_PROVIDERS off on: people may add their own provider and key.
FLOWPLAN_AI_FEATURES all Allowed features, comma-separated: write, summarize, ask, database, actions, whiteboard.
FLOWPLAN_AI_DEVICE on off: no on-device AI in the apps for iPhone, iPad and Mac. Independent of FLOWPLAN_AI.
FLOWPLAN_AI_SEMANTIC_SEARCH off on: semantic search with the embedding model.
FLOWPLAN_AI_EMBED_PER_HOUR 5000 Maximum chunks embedded per hour for semantic search.
FLOWPLAN_AI_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR 300 Maximum AI requests per person and hour (plus 30 per minute, 3 at once).

en.heading: Push notifications
paragraphs: Variable Meaning
WEB_PUSH_SUBJECT Contact for the push services, e.g. mailto:admin@example.com.
WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY / WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY VAPID key pair. If not given, Flowplan creates one in FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR/web-push-keys.json.
MOBILE_PUSH Notifications to the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android. Nothing to set up; off turns them off altogether. Default: on.
PUSH_RELAY_URL The push relay notifications to the apps go through. An HTTPS origin only (http only for localhost), without a path. Default: https://push.flowplan.org.
PUSH_RELAY off: no relay. Apps then only get notifications if they have an Expo token (older app versions), through Expo's push service. Default: on.

MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT Whether the notification's text comes along – and with it the buttons Done and Tomorrow on due tasks and Reply on comments (Buttons on notifications); Mark as read is always there. Empty (default): only where it is end-to-end encrypted, i.e. through the relay; through Expo (older apps) only "something new in the inbox" as with Web Push, and Live Activities only with times, no titles. on: also through Expo and with titles in Live Activities – readable by Expo, Apple and Google. off: never, not even through the relay.
The VAPID keys must not change, otherwise all browsers lose their subscription. Outgoing HTTPS to the push services of Apple, Google and Mozilla (Web Push) and to the push relay must be possible.

en.heading: Push relay and end-to-end encryption
paragraphs: Notifications to the apps go through the Flowplan push relay (push.flowplan.org). Only the relay holds the credentials for Apple (APNs) and Google (Firebase); your instance needs none of its own – self-hosted instances, too, reach the apps from the App Store and Google Play this way.

– End-to-end encrypted: every app installation creates a key pair (X25519) per instance and gives the instance only the public key. The instance encrypts every notification with it (HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, a fresh one-time key per notification); only the app on the device decrypts it. The relay, Apple and Google only see ciphertext – plus the kind of message, which buttons it has, the number on the app icon and when it was sent. If a notification cannot be decrypted, the app shows "New notification".

– Signed: the instance has a signing key pair of its own (Ed25519), created on first use. The private key is stored only encrypted in the database (like stored secrets, see above); the public key is published at /.well-known/flowplan-push. The relay only accepts signed requests, and only for devices that registered for exactly this instance. For this, APP_URL must be the public HTTPS address, and /.well-known/flowplan-push must be reachable from outside.

– What is stored: per app installation the relay token (only encrypted) and the public key. Both go with signing out, removing the device under Signed-in devices, or when the relay reports that the device can no longer be reached. Neither tokens nor keys nor content are logged.

– Live Activities (iPhone) for the timer and focus are also updated by the instance through the relay when their state changes. iOS renders their content itself – it cannot be encrypted. By default it therefore holds only times and the phase, no titles (MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on sends the title along).
– Older app versions without the relay keep getting notifications through Expo's push service (exp.host), without text by default.

– Rotating the signing key: node --import tsx scripts/push-relay-key.mjs rotate in the repository, or as an administrator POST /api/admin/operations with {"action":"pushRelay.rotate"}. The new key is published at once and signs after a little more than an hour; the old one stays listed for 7 days (--grace-days or graceDays). For a key that may have leaked, --immediate or "immediate": true: the new one signs at once, all old ones are removed. {"action":"pushRelay.keys"} lists the keys (ids and dates only). Or under Administration → Push notifications → Rotate key ….
– Your own relay: only together with your own app build – see Running your own push relay.

– Checking it: Settings → Notifications → Send test notification sends at once through the relay, Expo and Web Push to your own devices and shows the result per device – for example that the relay could not verify the instance (/.well-known/flowplan-push not reachable) or cannot be reached. Administrators also see the relay address, whether /.well-known/flowplan-push is enabled and the APP_URL in use. See Test notification.

– State in the administration: Administration → Push notifications shows the relay in use (official or your own), whether it is on and otherwise why not, whether it is reachable right now (/healthz, with response time), whether the instance can fetch its own /.well-known/flowplan-push at APP_URL, the signing keys with Rotate key …, the deliveries of the last 24 hours per channel and the last error. See Administration → Push notifications.

For an instance's privacy policy, for example: "Push notifications to the Flowplan apps are delivered end-to-end encrypted through Flowplan's push service (push.flowplan.org) and the services of Apple (APNs) or Google (Firebase Cloud Messaging). These services receive a device token, the address of this instance, the time and the kind of the notification, but not its content." – extend it accordingly with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on or notifications through Expo.

en.heading: Running your own push relay
paragraphs: The relay is open source (github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan-push) and can be self-hosted. The apps from the App Store and Google Play don't need it – they only accept notifications through push.flowplan.org, because Apple and Google deliver to these apps only with Flowplan's keys. Your own relay makes sense if you build your own app version (own bundle ID, own Apple team) or want to reach instances in an internal network.

– Start the relay – as the Docker image ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-push:latest (or built from the repository), e.g. in Coolify at https://push.example.com, port 8080, a volume on /data. Environment variables:
Variable Value
RELAY_STORAGE_KEY openssl rand -base64 32 – encrypts the stored device tokens
RELAY_PUBLIC_URL the relay's public address without a path, e.g. https://push.example.com (otherwise https://push.flowplan.org applies)
APNS_KEY_ID, APNS_TEAM_ID, APNS_KEY your Apple team's APNs key (.p8): key ID, team ID and the file's contents (base64 also works)
ALLOWED_BUNDLE_IDS your app's bundle ID, e.g. com.example.notes
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT optional, your Firebase project's service-account JSON for Android
TRUST_PROXY 1 behind Coolify/Traefik

ALLOW_PRIVATE_INSTANCES true if instances in an internal network (private addresses, http://localhost) should send notifications – meant for development and closed networks only, as the relay's README says
https://push.example.com/healthz answers {"status":"ok"}; the start-up log says whether APNs and FCM are set up.

– Build the app – with your bundle ID and Apple team, PUSH_RELAY_URL=https://push.example.com (the app's build variable) and, for Android, your google-services.json. The app only registers with the relay it was built for.

– Configure the instance – PUSH_RELAY_URL=https://push.example.com. APP_URL must be the instance's HTTPS address and /.well-known/flowplan-push reachable for the relay. An instance can use one relay only: pointed at yours, it no longer reaches the store apps through the relay.
– Check – with the test notification.
Operations, key rotation, blocking abusive instances (node dist/src/cli.js block in the container) and backups are described in the relay's README.

en.heading: Do not set
paragraphs: The image sets NODE_ENV, PORT, HOSTNAME and NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED itself. FLOWPLAN_DIST_DIR is only meant for parallel development servers, OIDC_ALLOW_LOCAL_HTTP only for tests with a provider on http://localhost, FLOWPLAN_GIT_ALLOW_HTTP only for tests of the Git export with an http:// server (no effect in production). Version and commit (FLOWPLAN_VERSION, GIT_COMMIT, SOURCE_COMMIT) come from the build; FLOWPLAN_VERSION in .env only picks the image tag in compose.yaml.

en.heading: In the interface
paragraphs: In the Administration, administrators set (see Administering the instance):
– Instance: the instance name and whether the instance offers a public demo (running and total started demos are shown under Administration → Monitoring → Instance in numbers),

– Sign-in & SSO: whether anyone may sign up with e-mail and password, whether everyone may create workspaces of their own, after how many days without sign-in accounts are blocked, required two-factor sign-in,
– Limits & retention: the default storage quota, storage and own workspaces per person, the maximum upload size, how long versions are kept,
– Storage & backup: the daily or hourly database backup and how many copies are kept,
– Maintenance & notices: a notice banner for everyone and the maintenance notice,
– Extensions & domains: Custom domains for publications (off) and Block extensions from any HTTPS address (off) – see Coolify and reverse proxies and Block extensions,
– Monitoring → Statistics: whether usage statistics are collected (locked with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off).
Empty fields fall back to the environment variables.
Flowplan only needs an HTTPS proxy in front of it. WebSockets are not needed: collaboration runs over normal HTTP requests and server-sent events.

en.heading: Coolify
paragraphs: – Choose New resource → Docker Image (ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest) or Dockerfile from the Git repository.
– Ports Exposes: 3000.
– Enter the domain, e.g. https://flowplan.example.com. Coolify gets the certificate via Traefik.
– Persistent Storage: a volume with the target /app/data.
– Set the environment variables from the configuration.
– Deploy. After about 20 seconds the health check reports the container as healthy.

en.heading: Health check
paragraphs: The image comes with its own health check. If you set it up in Coolify:
Field Value
Check type HTTP request
Method / scheme / host GET / HTTP / localhost
Port 3000 – empty means 80, where nothing listens
Path /api/health
Expected code 200
Start period 30 seconds (with S3, Litestream restores the database on the first start)
Flowplan sends no X-Powered-By header. The health check only needs the status code; its details are not public without a token (see Health check).

en.heading: Volume permissions
paragraphs: The container runs as UID 1000. A new Docker volume gets the permissions automatically. A mounted host folder must belong to this UID:
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /path/to/flowplan-data

en.heading: Roll out automatically
paragraphs: Coolify does not watch the registry itself. The repositories' image workflows therefore trigger a deployment through the Coolify API after pushing a new image (POST /api/v1/deploy?uuid=… with an API token). Coolify's built-in GitHub webhook does not fit: it builds from source and fires on the push, before the image is ready.
– In Coolify, turn on API access under Settings (and allow the CI runner's address if needed).
– Under Keys & Tokens → API tokens, create a token with the deploy permission.
– In the resource under Webhooks, copy the Deploy Webhook address, e.g. https://coolify.example.com/api/v1/deploy?uuid=…&force=false.
– In the GitHub repository under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions, create two secrets: COOLIFY_WEBHOOK (the address) and COOLIFY_TOKEN (the token).
Repository Image in Coolify Rolled out on
flowplan ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:beta (or :latest without automation) every manual build (Actions → Docker image → Run workflow)
flowplan-website ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-website:latest every push to main
flowplan-docs ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan-docs:latest every push to main

Pull requests and Dependabot never deploy; without the secrets (in forks, for example) the step is skipped. If Coolify does not pull the new image on deploy, set pull_policy: always in the compose file.
[!WARNING] Keep the number of instances at 1 in Coolify. Several containers would write to the same SQLite file.

en.heading: Pangolin, Traefik and other proxies
paragraphs: – APP_URL must exactly match the address under which Flowplan appears in the browser.

– If TLS ends at the front proxy (such as Pangolin) and it passes on to Traefik, turn off TLS to the target there and set a custom host header with the Flowplan domain – otherwise Traefik finds no route and answers with 404.
– Large uploads: content archives can be up to 2 GB. Traefik does not limit the request size; nginx needs client_max_body_size, Cloudflare has its own limits.
– Timeouts: exporting and importing large archives can take minutes; raise proxy timeouts if needed.

– Server-sent events (live editing in documents, live cursors on whiteboards) must not be buffered; nginx: proxy_buffering off (see the example below). Flowplan also sends X-Accel-Buffering: no for this.

– Client address: the proxy must set X-Forwarded-For (Traefik and Caddy do so by default, nginx needs the line from the example). Only then does Flowplan limit sign-in attempts, demo starts and anonymous form answers per address. Without the header only the limits per account and per link apply, and the log shows a note on the first request. FLOWPLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES names the number of proxies (Configuration).

en.heading: nginx
paragraphs: server {
server_name flowplan.example.com;
client_max_body_size 2g;
location / {
proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 600s;

en.heading: Caddy
paragraphs: flowplan.example.com {
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
Never expose the internal port 3000 publicly as well.

en.heading: Custom domains for publications
paragraphs: With Custom domains for publications under Administration → Extensions & domains, owners show published pages under their domain (Sharing and publishing). Flowplan recognises the domain by the Host header and serves only the publication. The certificate stays the reverse proxy's job; it must pass requests for any host on to Flowplan and keep the Host unchanged.
Flowplan answers GET /api/domains/allowed?domain= with 200 for verified domains of active publications and with 404 otherwise – exactly the question Caddy asks before a new certificate.

en.heading: Caddy with on-demand TLS
paragraphs: on_demand_tls {
ask http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/domains/allowed
flowplan.example.com {
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
# Every other host: a certificate only when Flowplan knows the domain.
https:// {
tls {
on_demand
reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
Caddy fetches the certificate on the first request for the domain. Domains Flowplan has not verified get none – so nobody can trigger certificates for other people's names.

en.heading: Traefik
paragraphs: Traefik does not ask before issuing a certificate. Add a router per domain (file provider or labels) – after the domain is verified in Flowplan:
http:
routers:
flowplan-docs-example:
rule: Host(`docs.example.org`)
service: flowplan
tls:
certResolver: letsencrypt
services:
flowplan:
loadBalancer:
servers:
- url: http://flowplan:3000
With an HTTP-01 resolver the file check (/.well-known/flowplan-verify.txt) then works too; with DNS the order does not matter.

en.heading: Coolify
paragraphs: In Coolify add the extra domain to the Domains field of the Flowplan resource (comma-separated, e.g. https://flowplan.example.com,https://docs.example.org) and redeploy. Coolify creates the router and certificate for Traefik. APP_URL stays the address of the app.

en.heading: Security
paragraphs: – Under a custom domain Flowplan only answers the publication's read access, its files and the interface's static files. Sign-in, app and API answer with 404 – also when someone forges the Host header.
– Cookies and Authorization headers are dropped there, and Flowplan never sets a cookie.
– The pages carry frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY.
– An entry for the instance's own address is not possible.
A page made of tiles: metrics, charts and views of your databases, tasks due, your journal streak and notes – at a glance, and for everyone with exactly the data they may see.

en.heading: Creating a dashboard
paragraphs: New page → Dashboard (or > New dashboard in the quick search). A new dashboard is empty; Add the first tile opens the settings of the first tile.

en.heading: Tiles
paragraphs: Tile Shows
Database view A view of a database, as the linked database in a document shows it. With Records editable here records can be changed right on the dashboard, otherwise they are read-only.
Metric The number of records of a view (with its filters) or the sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number property. With a target a progress bar appears.
Chart Columns, bars, line or donut over a property – drawn like the chart view; a click on a record opens it.
Journal streak How many days in a row you have written in a journal, plus today's entry or Write today.
My due tasks Your tasks from My tasks that are due today or overdue.
Recently changed The most recently changed pages and the number of unread notifications in the inbox.
Text Free text in Markdown – for headings, notes or links.

en.heading: Arranging and sizing
paragraphs: Edit at the top right switches to edit mode:
– Add tile creates a new tile.
– Drag tiles to change their order – or use Move earlier/Move later in the tile menu (…).
– Choose the size in the tile menu: Small (a quarter), Medium (half), Large (two thirds) or Full width. On phones all tiles stack.
– Configure … changes source, title and values; Remove deletes the tile.
Done leaves edit mode. Every change is saved right away.

en.heading: Permissions
paragraphs: – People with edit rights on the page add and change tiles; readers only look at the dashboard.

– Every tile is calculated with the rights of the person looking: private records only count for those who may see them. A tile over a database or journal someone may not read (or that is locked with a PIN) shows that person only Not available – no title, no values.
– Sources must be in the same workspace.

en.heading: Copying, export and trash
paragraphs: – Duplicate copies the dashboard with all tiles; when a database is copied along, the tile in the copy points to the copy.
– The Markdown export contains a text overview of the tiles (title, type, source, texts), and so do PDF, Word and EPUB. The values themselves depend on who is looking and are therefore not exported.
– Deleted dashboards go to the trash like any page and come back with all their tiles.
– Through the API, the dashboard.save action stores the tiles of a dashboard page.
A database is a collection of records with properties. The same records can be shown as a table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, list, feed, chart or form.

en.heading: Create a database
paragraphs: New page → Database asks for the kind:
Kind Properties First view
Tasks Task, Status, Priority, Due, Assignee, Tags Table "All tasks", plus board, calendar, timeline …
Documents Title, Tags, Created, Edited List "All documents" (last edited first), gallery, table; records open as a full page, empty properties are hidden
Empty only a title Table

Below are Your templates: saved database templates, such as your own "Notes (PARA)" database with relations and views. The device remembers the last choice. Alternatively use a template, such as "Tasks" or "Projects", or import a CSV file (see Import, export and versions).

en.heading: Records
paragraphs: – New at the bottom of the table or at the top right creates a record and opens it with the title selected – just start typing, Enter saves.

– A click on the title opens the record as a page: the title at the top to edit directly, the properties below it, and below them a full document with the same editor as every other page – including comments, version history and editing together.

– At the top right of a record: how it opens (as a dialog, in the side panel or as a full page – the choice applies to you in this browser; the database's default is marked "default"), the star for favourites, Copy link for the record's address, the lock for the record's permissions and the sliders for the layout of all records. Icon and Cover appear when the pointer is over the title.

– Reading mode (book icon at the top of the record or ⌘ ⌥ E) opens a record's text for reading only, as for pages; the device remembers it per record. Opened as a full page, Full width uses the whole screen – the properties keep a readable width, the text gets the space.

– An open record has its own address (/#page=&row=) – whether it opens as a dialog, in the side panel or as a full page. It can be shared, bookmarked or linked in texts with @. Below the properties, Linked from shows which records refer to it through a relation and which pages and records link to it in their text.
– Record templates give new records properties and content. One template can be the default for new records.
– Select several records (checkboxes on the left) and edit, duplicate or delete them together – up to 500 at once. Flowplan saves a state beforehand that can be restored from the version history.

– Deleted records sit in the database's trash and can be brought back. Right after deleting it is quicker: Undo in the notice at the bottom (or ⌘ Z while it shows). A bulk edit of several records, a record dragged into another column, a removed date and a deleted property can be taken back the same way.

en.heading: Move a page into a database
paragraphs: Page actions → Move into database … turns a document page into a record of a database you may write to – for example to bring grown documentation into a notes database:
– Title, icon and cover become the record's title, icon and cover, the content its document; files and images stay the same files (they then belong to the database).
– Comments, text comments, tasks and versions come along; favourites become record favourites.
– Links to the page in all pages and records of the workspace then point to the record.
– Sub-pages stay pages and move up one level. Permissions for people set on the page keep applying to them – so they become visible to neither more nor fewer people.

– Sharing of only this page (permissions for people, share links, publication) ends – the dialog lists it first; the record follows the database's permissions. The database's default record template applies.
– The page itself goes to the trash.

en.heading: Turn a record into a page
paragraphs: The other way round, Turn into page … makes a record a document page again – in the … menu at the top of the open record or with a right-click on the record. You need edit access to the record and write access at the target location:
– Title, icon and cover become the page's title, icon and cover, the record's document its content; files and images stay the same files (they then belong to the page).
– The properties stay as a short "Property: value" list at the top of the page (readable in a Markdown export too); in the dialog you can drop them instead.
– Comments, text comments, tasks and versions come along; record favourites become page favourites.
– Links to the record in all pages and records of the workspace then point to the page – @ links and backlinks keep working.

– The page goes where the database is, or to another location of your choice, and follows its permissions. The record's own permissions and relations from other records to it end – the dialog lists them first.
– The record itself goes to the database's trash and can be brought back.

en.heading: Copy and move records
paragraphs: A right-click on a record – in a table, board, list, gallery, calendar or timeline – opens its menu: Open, Duplicate, Copy to …, Move to …, Turn into page … and Delete. When several records are selected, the menu applies to all of them; the selection bar also has Move / copy to ….
In the dialog you choose the target database in the same workspace:
– Copy creates new records – with properties, content, icon and cover. Files and images are copied too, so the copy does not depend on the source.
– Move takes the record itself: content, comments, version history, tracked time and Git links stay with it. In the new database it gets the next number (ticket ID).

– Properties are matched by name, the title always to the title. Compatible types are converted (text ↔ e-mail, select ↔ multi-select, number → text …); missing select options are added to the target. Create missing properties in the target adds properties the target does not have yet.
– Calculated values (formulas, rollups, progress, created/edited) are worked out again in the target.
With the mouse it is quicker: drag records by their handle onto a database in the sidebar to move them there; hold Alt to copy them instead. Flowplan saves a state of the source beforehand.

en.heading: Properties
paragraphs: Type Content
Text, number Numbers with a format: currency, percent, decimal places, thousands separators
Date With or without time and end date, time zone, personal reminders, recurrence
Select, multi-select Coloured options, e.g. for status or tags
Checkbox, checklist Tick off; checklists with several items and progress
URL, e-mail, phone Clickable
Person Members of the workspace; assigning someone notifies them
Files Attachments and images right on the record
Relation, rollup A link to records of another database and calculations over them
Formula A value calculated from other properties
Created time/by, edited time/by Maintained automatically
Relations, rollups and formulas are described under Properties, formulas and rollups.

en.heading: Large databases
paragraphs: Tables, lists and galleries first show 100 records; the next 100 follow as you scroll, and groups and board columns have Show more. Search, filters, sorting and column calculations still always apply to all records. This way even databases with thousands of records open in a fraction of a second.

en.heading: Filter, sort, group
paragraphs: Every view has its own settings:
– Filters with AND/OR groups; for date fields also relative periods ("this week", "last 30 days") that update themselves every day.
– Sorting by several properties.
– Grouping by almost any property (except files and checklists), with up to five levels in tables and lists; boards show the second level as rows (swimlanes).
– Search within the database, also in the text of the record documents.
– Column calculations below table columns: sum, average, median, minimum, maximum, percentages, earliest and latest dates and more.

en.heading: Recurring records
paragraphs: Date fields can repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly. Calendar and timeline show the occurrences; it remains a single record. If needed, a single occurrence can be detached as a record of its own.

en.heading: Repeating tasks
paragraphs: For tasks that are ticked off one by one each time (“monthly closing”, “server updates”), set a rhythm in the record under Repeating task: daily, weekly (optionally on certain weekdays, e.g. Mo, We, Fr), monthly or yearly, each every N days, weeks, months or years. With several date fields you choose which one moves on.

As soon as the record is done (status or checkbox, see When is a record done?), Flowplan creates the next record: a copy with the status it had before, the chosen date on the next occurrence and every other date field moved by as many days. The rhythm moves to the new record; reopening and completing the old one again creates nothing more.
– Month ends are clamped but the day is kept: 31 January → 28 February → 31 March.
– 29 February becomes the 28th in common years and the 29th again in leap years.
New records at fixed times – whether or not the last one is done – come from scheduled automations.

en.heading: Date reminders
paragraphs: In a record, everyone can set a personal reminder for every filled date field – for times at the appointment or 5 minutes to 1 week before, for all-day dates on the day or 1, 2 or 7 days before at 09:00. Reminders appear in the inbox and as a push notification and do not change the record.

en.heading: Permissions per record
paragraphs: The permissions icon at the top of a record restricts a record beyond the permissions of the database:
– Same as database: the default.
– Read-only record: only its managers (page owners and the person who created the record) and people it is explicitly shared with may change it.
– Private record: only its managers and people it is shared with see it – together with its comments, tasks and files (in the file list, search, media library, copies, templates and backups).
Shares with people or groups never go beyond their role on the database page.
A shortcut opens a small window above every app: a thought, a task, a link, a file, a screen region or a voice note – into the inbox, a database, today's journal entry or a page. Offline too.
Quick capture is part of the desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It saves straight to your instance with the active profile's sign-in; nothing goes to third parties.

en.heading: At a glance
paragraphs: Key What happens
Ctrl Shift Space (Mac: ⇧ ⌘ Space) opens the window above every app – also while Flowplan is minimised, hidden or (Mac, tray icon) closed
Enter saves
Shift Enter new line
Tab choose the target: typing filters, ↑ ↓ moves, Enter takes it
Alt ↑ / ↓ previous / next target without opening the list
⌘/Ctrl Shift V paste the clipboard – a link gets its title
hold ⌘/Ctrl Shift R record a voice note, release to stop
↓ in the empty field Recently captured
Esc closes an open list, otherwise the window – the text stays as a draft
The buttons in the window do the same: Paste, Attach…, Region, Hold to talk, Suggest and As a task for today. The first line becomes the title, the rest the text.

en.heading: Where it goes: targets
paragraphs: The top right shows where the capture goes. You can choose:
Target What is created
Inbox (default) a record in your capture database – the default chosen under Capture (see Capture into a database)
a database a new record; its default template applies, shorthand fills its properties
a journal appended to today's entry – if the day does not exist yet, Flowplan creates it
a page appended at the end of the page, as a new paragraph (or as a task)
The list only shows where you may write. Recently used targets come first; the app remembers them per profile and starts with the last target next time.

[!NOTE] End-to-end encrypted spaces are not in the list. The server cannot write into them, and the capture window – unlike the Flowplan window – has no keys. The list says how many pages are missing for that reason. For encrypted spaces, capture directly in the Flowplan window. Journals behind a PIN are left out too.

As a task for today turns the first line into an open task – due today or on the day from the text, assigned to you or to the person from the text. It shows up at once under My tasks and in the app's tray icon.

en.heading: Shorthand in the text
paragraphs: Flowplan reads what you type as you type and shows it as chips below the text – for example for “Write offer tomorrow 3pm #client @anna !high”:
Due: Tue, Oct 27, 3:00 PM · Tags: Client · Assignee: Anna Schmidt · Priority: High

What a chip takes over disappears from the title. The × on a chip keeps the text exactly as typed. Shorthand only fills properties the target has – otherwise the text stays, and the chip says “stays text”.
Shorthand Examples (German · English · French) Becomes
Days heute, morgen, übermorgen · today, tomorrow, day after tomorrow · aujourd'hui, demain, après-demain due date
Weekdays Freitag, nächsten Montag · friday, next monday · vendredi, lundi prochain the next such day
Spans in 3 Tagen, nächste Woche · in two weeks, next week · dans une semaine, la semaine prochaine a day (next week: its Monday)
Dates 24.12., 24.12.2026, 2026-12-24, 24. Dezember · 12/24, Dec 24th · 24/12, le 5 novembre that day (without a year: the next one)
Times 15 Uhr, um 15:30 · 3pm, at 3:30 pm · 15h, à 9h30 time of the date (alone: today)
Tag #client an option of a multi-select (“Tags” first), if it exists
Person @anna a person property (“Assignee” first) – first name, full name without spaces or e-mail name, when exactly one person matches
Priority !hoch, !niedrig · !high, !urgent, !low · !haute, !basse · !1–!4, !!!, !! an option of a “Priority” select (or one with priority options)
– The due date goes into the first date property (first one named “Due”, “Fällig”, “Échéance” …). A time counts in your computer's time zone, also when the record is only sent later from the queue.
– #27 is a number, not a tag; name@example.org stays an e-mail address; an exclamation mark at the end of a sentence stays one.
– Offline the window shows no chips; the shorthand is read when the capture is sent – with the day and time zone of capturing.
– The server reads the shorthand (one place for all apps). Older servers without this feature take only text into the inbox – the window says so.

en.heading: Clipboard and links
paragraphs: ⌘/Ctrl Shift V or Paste inserts the clipboard text. If it is a link (https://…), it appears as a link chip with title and provider – your instance fetches the preview (like link cards in the editor, protected against internal addresses), never the app itself. It is saved into the database's link property (otherwise into the text) and as a link card; with an empty text, the page's title becomes the title. Offline, the link is saved without a title.

en.heading: Files, screen regions and voice notes
paragraphs: – Files: drop images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, HEIC), PDFs, Markdown and text files on the window, or choose them with Attach…. They are checked as when dropping files on the main window: extension and content, images and PDFs up to 50 MB, text up to 5 MB (the instance may allow less), at most 10 attachments. The list below the text shows them, × removes one. Images and PDFs go into the database's files property and into the text; Markdown and text become text.

– Screen region: Region – the window steps aside and you drag a region; it is attached as a PNG. On the Mac this uses the system's screenshot tool (Space picks a window, Esc cancels); on Windows and Linux Flowplan shows the screen under the pointer, you drag the region, Enter takes the whole screen, Esc cancels. Temporary files sit only briefly in the app's data folder and are deleted right away.

– Voice note: press and hold Hold to talk (or ⌘/Ctrl Shift R), release to stop. If your instance has transcription (Whisper, see Configuration), the recording becomes text there and appears in the field – to check before saving. Without transcription, offline or if it fails, the recording is attached; the instance tries again when it is saved.

en.heading: Permissions per system
paragraphs: System Screen region Microphone

macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording → switch on Flowplan, then restart Flowplan. Without it the window says so and opens the page with Open System Settings. macOS asks the first time (“Flowplan uses the microphone for voice notes.”). Declined: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.
Windows no permission needed Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone must allow desktop apps
Linux X11: none. Wayland: the desktop asks (portal) and often offers a screen or a window – Flowplan takes what it hands over. depends on the desktop (PipeWire/PulseAudio)
Flowplan never uses the camera, and the capture window may only use the microphone – and only while you hold the button.

en.heading: Offline: the queue
paragraphs: If the instance cannot be reached, the capture goes into a queue – with text, target, shorthand, link and attachments. The window says “No connection to … – queued, sent automatically”, the top shows “1 queued”, and the tray icon and the settings show the number too.

– Sent by itself: as soon as the connection is back, the computer wakes up or is unlocked, otherwise with growing pauses (5 s, 15 s, 30 s … at most every 15 minutes). Send now (window, tray icon, settings) tries right away.

– Nothing twice: every capture has its own key (Idempotency-Key) from the first moment, and every attempt sends exactly the same request. If an answer gets lost after the instance has already saved it, the next attempt receives the stored answer instead of a second record.

– Nothing lost: if the instance refuses something for good (target deleted, file too large), it stays in the queue and the window shows it with Copy (back into the field) and Discard. While signed out, the capture waits until you are signed in again.

– Stored encrypted: the queue and “Recently captured” are kept per profile in the app's data folder (capture/), encrypted with the system's key store (macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI, Secret Service/KWallet on Linux). Without a key store on Linux they are stored unencrypted, readable only by your user account – the settings say which applies. Removing a profile deletes them.

en.heading: Undo and “Recently captured”
paragraphs: After saving, the window shows “✓ Saved to …” with Open (the record or page in the Flowplan window) and Undo – for ten seconds. Then the window goes away unless you started something new.

– Undo moves a captured record to the database's trash (restorable from there) and removes appended content from a page or the journal again – as long as it is still unchanged at the end. If someone has written on since, it stays, and the window says so. A capture still in the queue is simply not sent.

– Recently captured: ↓ in the empty field shows the profile's last 20 captures with target and time; Enter or Open opens one. The same list (the last 8) is in the menu bar or tray icon under Recently Captured; waiting ones are marked with ⏳.

en.heading: Quick actions
paragraphs: Under Settings → Quick actions you add more shortcuts that open the window ready for one thing:
Quick action Opens the window …
Task with As a task for today and the chosen target
Journal entry with the chosen journal – appended to today's entry
Bookmark with the link from the clipboard and its title
Meeting note with a chosen database and one of its templates (default, or e.g. “Meeting”), the text starting with “Meeting: ”
Note with a fixed target, optionally as a task

Each has a name, a target, a shortcut (Change, Off), Try it and Remove. None is active without a shortcut – after the update only the main shortcut is on. If another app already holds a shortcut, the action says so; a shortcut always belongs to one action only and never also to the main shortcut. At most eight quick actions.

en.heading: AI suggestion (optional)
paragraphs: Suggest asks an AI where the text belongs: database, a short title and properties the text clearly names. The result appears as chips with ✓ (accept) and × (ignore) – nothing is applied by itself. Every suggestion is checked on the server: only databases you may write to, only existing options, only real people and days.

– Where the AI runs: through your instance's AI (the AI actions feature, see AI) – or on a Mac with macOS 26 and Apple Intelligence switched on, on the Mac itself (On-device AI): the instance only builds the question, the Mac answers it, and the text reaches no AI on the server. Which is preferred follows your setting for on-device AI.
– What the AI sees: the text in the window and the names of the databases, their properties and options – no content. Databases closed to the AI are left out.
– Off: the button is missing when the administration or you switched off AI (or AI actions).

en.heading: Setup and the one-time hint
paragraphs: After the first sign-in the app shows one more step: How Flowplan should run on this computer – Turn on quick capture (with the shortcut, Change, Try it now; a taken shortcut is reported), Icon in the menu bar / notification area, Start when you sign in to the computer and Start minimized / in the background (only together with starting at sign-in). The switches start with your system's defaults (icon: on for Mac, off for Windows and Linux), everything can be skipped and changed later under Settings – they are the same settings.

People who had the app before and never captured see “New: quick capture with …” once in the lower left of the window, with Try it and Settings. After closing it, a click or the first capture, the hint never comes back.

en.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: – Captures are only stored on your instance, with the profile's sign-in and its origin check. Link previews, transcription and AI run through the instance (or on the Mac); the app itself fetches no other addresses.

– The computer only keeps the queue and “Recently captured” (encrypted, see above), the recently used targets (identifiers only) and, briefly, screen regions. The window has a session of its own without cookies or storage.
– End-to-end encrypted spaces are never a target.

en.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: The desktop app after 1.2.0 and a Flowplan server newer than 0.7.0. With an older server the window takes text (and As a task for today) into the inbox and says that targets, shorthand, links and attachments need a server update. Voice notes as text need transcription on the server; the AI suggestion needs AI actions switched on, or Apple Intelligence on the Mac.
The editor works with blocks: every paragraph, list, table or embed is a block you can insert, format, indent and move. Everything is saved continuously, even without a connection.

en.heading: The block menu with /
paragraphs: At the start of a line or after a space, / opens the block menu right at the cursor. Keep typing to filter: /h2, /todo, /code, /tab. Arrow keys choose, Enter or Tab inserts, Esc closes.
[!TIP] To type a plain slash, type a space after / or close the menu with Esc. In code blocks / is always an ordinary character.
Block Shortcut in the menu What for
Text /text A normal paragraph
Heading 1–3 /h1, /h2, /h3 Structure; they appear in the table of contents
Task list /todo Tasks to tick off
Bulleted list, numbered list /ul, /ol Lists, nested as deep as you like
Quote /quote A highlighted quotation
Note, Tip, Important, Warning, Caution /note, /tip, /important, /warning, /caution A coloured box with icon and title – the five kinds of GitHub alerts
Toggle /toggle Content that folds in and out
Code /code Syntax highlighting for 192 languages
Table /table A simple table in the text
Image or file /image, /file Upload or pick from the media library
Mermaid diagram /mermaid Flowcharts, sequence and class diagrams as text
Formula, inline formula /math, /inlinemath LaTeX, rendered with KaTeX
Mention a page, record or person /mention or @ A reference to a page, database record or person
Whiteboard /board Embed a whiteboard in the document
Draw /draw, /sketch, /handwriting Handwriting and sketches with a pen or finger (Handwriting in documents)
Linked database /db A view of an existing database
Two columns /columns Content side by side
Embed /embed Players for YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma, CodePen; a link card otherwise
Spoiler /spoiler Hidden text, revealed by a click
Voice note /voice Record (up to two hours) and insert as audio, optionally also as a transcript
Synced block /sync Content that stays the same on several pages
Insert synced block /sync Show an existing synced block
Divider /hr A horizontal line
AI /ai, /ki Let the AI write (when switched on)
Footnote /footnote, /fußnote Numbered note at the end of the page (Footnotes)
Citation /cite, /zitat Cite a source – DOI, BibTeX or Zotero (Citations)
Bibliography /bibliography, /references All cited works as a list

en.heading: Voice notes and meetings
paragraphs: /voice opens the recorder: tap the microphone, speak, Stop recording – up to two hours, enough for a meeting. You can listen to the recording or discard it; Insert puts it into the page as audio (within the instance's upload limit). If speech recognition is set up, the spoken words follow below as text; otherwise the dialog only offers the audio.
– Long recordings go to the server in parts; it puts them together and sends them to speech recognition. WHISPER_MAX_MB limits the size (default 200).

– Transcript with timestamps: if speech recognition returns segments with times (OpenAI-compatible verbose_json, e.g. faster-whisper-server, speaches or whisper.cpp), a collapsible Transcript · duration block appears with one paragraph per passage and its timestamp (00:04, 1:02:05).

– Speakers: only when the service itself separates speakers (diarization, switched on with WHISPER_DIARIZE=on for servers that know diarize) and returns a speaker per segment, each passage starts with Speaker 1, Speaker 2 … Flowplan never guesses speakers from pauses. If the service only knows plain JSON, the text is inserted as paragraphs as before.
– Then summarise with AI summarises the transcript (Summaries).
– In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android the app records; iPhone and iPad turn the words into text on the device, without speech recognition on the server (Voice notes in pages).

– Generate tasks and summary (when AI actions are on for you): the AI proposes a summary with decisions and a task list with assignees and dates – as a preview with checkboxes; only Run adds them to the page.

en.heading: Table of contents
paragraphs: The list icon at the top right of a document opens the table of contents beside the text – in every document, journal days and database records included. It is built from the headings and grows while you write, marks the section you are reading and jumps to a heading on click. Whether it is open is remembered in this browser for all documents. On a phone a round button at the bottom right opens it.

en.heading: Pasting answers from ChatGPT
paragraphs: Text copied from ChatGPT or another assistant is formatted when pasted: LaTeX formulas (\[ … \], \( … \), $$ … $$) become formula blocks and inline formulas, Markdown (headings, bold, lists, tables) is applied, lines with tabs become a table, ☐ a task list, and each line becomes its own paragraph. Formulas already rendered on a copied web page stay formulas. This also applies when copying straight from the ChatGPT web page. If formulas are already in the document as text (such as \[ A(3;2;1) \]), select them – or everything with ⌘/Ctrl+A – and choose Turn into formulas in the text menu. Ordinary text is pasted as before.

en.heading: Callouts
paragraphs: Callouts come in five kinds, as on GitHub, Forgejo and Obsidian: Note (blue), Tip (green), Important (purple), Warning (yellow) and Caution (red). Each kind has its icon and a title in the reader's language. With the cursor in a callout, /tip, /warning etc. change its kind; so does Manage blocks → Callout type.

Markdown export writes callouts as GitHub alerts (> [!WARNING]). Import (Markdown, ZIP, Notion) turns > [!NOTE] to > [!CAUTION] back into callouts of that kind; Obsidian's further kinds map to the nearest one (e.g. danger → Caution, hint → Tip), and a custom title (> [!WARNING] Read first) becomes a bold first line.

en.heading: Reading mode
paragraphs: The book icon in the top bar (or ⌘ ⌥ E, quick search → > reading) opens a document for reading only: nothing changes by accident, handles and the block menu disappear – handy on the phone and when reading aloud or presenting. The pencil switches back to editing. The device remembers the mode per page; permissions stay the same, and others keep their own mode. Database records have the same book icon at the top of the record (see Databases).

en.heading: Focus mode
paragraphs: Focus mode (quick search → > focus) hides the sidebar, toolbar and page margins; the top bar only appears on hover. At the bottom, a bar counts the words of the page and those added in this session. With a goal (e.g. 500 words) a bar shows the progress; the device remembers the goal per page. Esc ends the mode.

en.heading: Present
paragraphs: Present in the … menu at the top right (or ⌘ ⌥ P, quick search → > present) shows a document as full-screen slides – without rebuilding it:
– Each heading 1 starts a new slide. If the document has none, each heading 2 does. A divider (---) always starts a new slide.
– Whatever comes before the first heading becomes a title slide with the page title.
– Images, tables, code, formulas and diagrams are scaled down so the whole slide fits on the screen.
Key Effect
→, ↓, Space, Page Down Next slide
←, ↑, Page Up Previous slide
Home / End First / last slide
Esc End the presentation

A click into the right two thirds of the slide moves on, into the left third back. At the bottom, a counter and a bar show where you are; the bar of buttons fades out while the mouse rests. It also switches between light and dark slides. If “Reduce motion” is set on your system, slides change without a fade.

en.heading: Speaker notes and presenter view
paragraphs: A callout (/callout, kind “Note”) as the last block of a slide holds the speaker notes: it does not appear on the slide. Presenter view (notepad icon in the bar) opens a second window with the current and the next slide, the notes and the elapsed time – handy on the laptop while the projector shows the slides. Both windows stay in step: you can move on in either of them.

en.heading: Slides as PDF
paragraphs: The printer icon in the bar prints the slides – each on its own page in landscape. Choose Save as PDF in the print dialog to pass the slides on.

en.heading: Synced blocks
paragraphs: A synced block (/sync → Synced block) is content that is the same in several places – such as contact details, a checklist or a status notice. Insert synced block shows it on another page. You can edit it everywhere; the change appears on all pages, live on pages that are open.
– An orange frame marks the block; at the top it shows the number of pages and the page it was created on.
– The trash icon in the frame removes the block only in this place; it stays in the others.
– Permissions come from the page the block was created on: whoever may not read that page sees a notice instead of the content.
– The search finds the text on the original page. The block does not appear on published pages.

en.heading: Tasks with assignee and date
paragraphs: A task (/todo or [] + space) with a mention such as @Anna is assigned to Anna: she gets a notification and finds the task under My tasks in the sidebar. You set a date while the cursor is in the task, with the calendar button in the toolbar or through the text menu (select text or right-click → Due date). The date appears as a chip at the right of the line (highlighted today, red when overdue); a click on it changes the date or removes it with Remove date. A new task made with Enter starts without a date.

My tasks collects all tasks given to you, your own tasks with a date and all tasks from your journals (even without @name and without a date) – grouped into Overdue, Today, Next 7 days, Later and No date. Below, From other workspaces lists your tasks from your other workspaces, per workspace; clicking the page switches there. Ticking off and changing the date take effect right in the document, also for others who have it open. On the due date a reminder arrives in the morning; the number next to "My tasks" shows how many are due today or overdue.

en.heading: Markdown shortcuts
paragraphs: While you type, the editor converts:
Type Result
#, ##, ### + space Heading 1–3
- or * + space Bulleted list
1. + space Numbered list
[] + space Task
> + space Quote
` Code block
--- Divider
bold, italic, ` code , ~~strike~~` Formatting in the text

en.heading: Format text
paragraphs: Selecting text – or right-clicking it – opens the text menu: reactions for the paragraph, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, code, link, Comment and Copy, in tasks also Due date. The toolbar above the text adds headings, colour and background colour, superscript and subscript, inline formulas and Hide (spoiler).
– Formatting only applies to the current line. After Enter the new line starts as normal text – only lists and tasks continue with a new item, and a heading is followed by a paragraph.

– Turn into: in the text menu (also on right-click in a line) a line changes its type without losing its text – text, heading 1–3, bulleted list, numbered list, task, quote or code block. The current type is highlighted.

en.heading: Spoiler
paragraphs: Hidden text stays hidden while you write. A click on the area reveals it, another one hides it again. ⌘ ⌥ H hides the selection. Sticky notes and text on whiteboards can be hidden too.

en.heading: Indent
paragraphs: – Tab at the start of a paragraph or heading indents it (up to eight levels), ⇧ Tab outdents it.
– Backspace at the start of an indented line first removes one level.
– In lists Tab nests the item below the previous one; in code blocks it inserts two spaces.

en.heading: Move blocks
paragraphs: A handle (⋮⋮) appears to the left of every block on hover. Dragging shows an insertion line in the middle of the gap between two blocks; when you let go, the block glides to its new place. A click on the handle opens Manage blocks: move – also into callouts or columns –, duplicate or delete, one block or several neighbouring ones.

List items and tasks stay what they are when moved: outside their list they form a list of the same kind of their own, and a numbered item keeps its number. Right next to a matching list they become part of it; in another kind of list they adapt.
⌘ ⇧ ↑/↓ moves the current block past its neighbour. Every block action can be undone on its own.

en.heading: Images, files and embeds
paragraphs: – Pasting from the clipboard (⌘ V) or dragging in uploads images and files. Images can be resized at their edges.

– Photos are scaled down before uploading: at most 2560 px on the longer side, stored as WebP. The camera rotation is kept, metadata such as the location is removed. GIFs, SVGs and files that would hardly get smaller stay unchanged. Attachments in file properties and forms are stored as they are.

– PDFs appear as a card with a preview of the first page. A click opens the PDF viewer with all pages, zoom (also ⌘ +/−) and Download; Esc closes it. The same applies to PDFs in the media library, in files properties of databases and on published pages. In editable text, ⌘-click a link to a PDF to open the viewer. In the viewer you can write on the PDF – see Annotate PDFs.

– Mark up images: double-click an image (or the pen in the toolbar while the image is selected) to open it for editing – with pen, highlighter, arrow, rectangle, circle and text, seven colours and three line widths, undo with ⌘ Z. Save creates a new image with the markings; the original and the markings stay with the image, so you can change or remove them later.
– Media in the sidebar collects all uploads of the workspace for reuse.
– Embed (/embed) takes an address: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma and CodePen appear as players with an adjustable width, other sites as a link card with title and preview image.
– Links to pages and mentions of people show a preview on hover.
– The administrators set the maximum file size (10 MB by default).

en.heading: Annotate PDFs
paragraphs: If you may edit the page a PDF belongs to, the PDF viewer shows Annotate (not in encrypted spaces and on locked pages). A toolbar appears below it: Pen (with the Apple Pencil or another tablet pen, the line width follows the pressure), Highlighter (translucent, stays under the text and the ink), Eraser (Whole strokes or Partial – then only what is under the eraser goes), Lasso, Text and Laser pointer (points at something without staying). Plus colours, three widths, undo and redo (⌘ Z, ⇧ ⌘ Z).
– Favourite pens: the three pens next to the tools remember colour and width; change them while one is chosen and the favourite changes with it. They apply on this device.

– Shapes: hold the pen still for a moment at the end of a stroke – a drawn line becomes straight, a rectangle, circle, triangle or diamond becomes the clean shape. Switch this off in the Pen settings (gear).
– Lasso: draw around strokes and text to move them, resize them with the handle at the bottom right, recolour, copy (⌘ C, paste with ⌘ V – also on another page), duplicate or delete them.
– Text is placed with a tap on the page; a tap on existing text changes it. On the iPad, Scribble writes into it with the pen.

– Draw with the pen only: once you have written with the pen on a device, only the pen writes – fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks. PDFs, whiteboards and images share the setting; switch it off in the Pen settings, then a finger writes too, and two fingers scroll and zoom.

– Apple Pencil: the eraser end of a pen erases. In the iPad app, double-tap or squeeze switches to the eraser and back – as set in the iPad settings, or in the Pen settings always to the eraser, the last tool or nothing.

The annotations belong to the page of the PDF, not to the screen: they stay in place at any zoom and apply to everyone who opens the PDF – readers see them but cannot change them. The PDF itself stays unchanged. Done (or ⌘ S) saves; every save is a version you can load again from the clock icon. If someone else saved the annotations in the meantime, your version wins and a notice says who; theirs is kept as a version. Search finds text you write on a PDF – in the app for iPhone and iPad also the handwriting itself, and Convert to text turns selected handwriting into typed text (see Recognising handwriting).
To turn a PDF into a notebook you write in page by page and add sheets to, open it as a notebook: every PDF page becomes a sheet.

Download still downloads the original. Download with annotations (next to it once there are annotations) creates a new PDF with the same pages and the annotations on top as vector graphics – they stay sharp when zooming in. Protected (encrypted) PDFs can only be downloaded without annotations; text appears in Helvetica, characters outside the Western European character set as “?”.

en.heading: Formulas, diagrams and code
paragraphs: – Formulas in LaTeX: as a block with /math, inside the text with /inlinemath. The preview appears while you type. Building blocks such as fraction, root, superscript, subscript, vector, cross product, ±, π and sum sit above the input.
– Mermaid diagrams: a click or Enter opens the source and preview. Up to 20,000 characters and 500 edges.
– Code blocks: choose the language in the header; Line wrap and Copy are at hand. Tab indents by two spaces.
– Fractions: /Fraction (or /Bruch) inserts a formula inside the sentence.

en.heading: Calculating in text
paragraphs: Flowplan only calculates when you want it to – exactly, with fractions, in German or English notation (2,5 or 2.5, ×, ², √, €):
– Hint after "=": type a calculation followed by =, such as 12 × 2,400 € = or 3/4 + 1/6 =, and the result appears greyed out behind it. Tab accepts it, Esc or typing on dismisses it.
– Selected text: select a calculation, a term or an equation; the text menu (also on right-click) shows what is possible under Calculate and inserts the result after it with one click:
– Result and Reduce as an exact fraction, plus As a decimal – 12/18 = 2/3
– Expand, including the binomial formulas – (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

– Factor – x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)², 6x² + 9x = 3x(2x + 3), also with several variables: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), x² + 2xy + y² − 1 = (x + y − 1)(x + y + 1), by grouping ax + ay + bx + by = (x + y)(a + b); Factor with roots splits further into real factors: x² − 2 = (x − √2)(x + √2)
– Simplify algebraic fractions – (x² − 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1, 1/x + 1/(x + 1) = (2x + 1)/(x(x + 1))

– Solve for x – linear and quadratic equations exactly (x² + 2x − 4 = 0 ⇒ x = −1 ± √5), higher degrees exactly where possible (x³ = 2 ⇒ x = ∛2, x⁴ − 5x² + 6 = 0 ⇒ x = ±√2, ±√3), otherwise as rounded decimals (x³ + x − 1 = 0 ⇒ x ≈ 0.682328); with several variables, for each one that appears linearly. Equations with x in a denominator are solved with the common denominator; values that would make a denominator 0 are excluded and named (x/(x − 1) = 1/(x − 1) ⇒ no solution (x = 1 excluded)).

– Function graph: select a term in x, such as x² − 2 or f(x) = 2x + 1, and choose Draw graph in the text menu – a graph with axes, grid and marked zeros appears below. /Function graph inserts one too. The functions are edited below the graph: it changes while you type, + Function adds up to six functions in their own colours (sin(x), cos, tan, exp, ln, abs, √ and π work). Dragging moves the view, +/− or ⌘/Ctrl + scrolling zoom, ⟲ resets the view. On published pages the graph can be moved and zoomed but not changed.

– Vectors: write vectors as (1 2 3), (1; 2; 3) or (1, 2, 3). Flowplan calculates sums and multiples (2 · (1; −2) − (3; 1) = (−1; −5)), the dot product with · including the angle ((1, 0) · (0, 1) = 0 ⇒ ∠ = 90°), the cross product with × ((1 0 0) × (0 1 0) = (0 0 1)) and the magnitude with … ( (1, 1) = √2). A vector selected on its own shows its magnitude and unit vector ((3, 4) ⇒ v⁰ = (3/5, 4/5)). Draw vectors in the text menu shows vectors in the plane as arrows in a coordinate system – for (1, 2) + (3, 1) both vectors and their sum. More vectors such as (3, 2) can be entered in the graph next to functions. Vectors in space such as (1, 2, 3) – cross products too – are drawn in a 3D coordinate system with x, y and z axes, a floor grid and dashed guides to the floor; dragging turns the view, and the view is saved with the page. The formula editor has the building blocks Vector (column vector), Vector arrow and Cross product; column vectors in formulas are calculated the same way.
– In formulas: the formula editor shows the same options under Calculate and appends the result in LaTeX, such as \frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{12}.

en.heading: Dashboards and metrics
paragraphs: /Metric inserts a card with a number from a database, /Dashboard three side by side. With the gear you choose:
– the database (every database in the workspace you can read),
– optionally a view – then only the records its filters show count, such as “Open tickets”,
– the calculation: number of records, sum, average, minimum or maximum of a number, formula or rollup property,
– a label.

The server calculates the number for the person looking at the page and refreshes it every minute; private records only count for people allowed to see them. On published pages, visitors without access see a dash. Add charts by inserting a linked database below the metrics and choosing a chart view there – that makes a dashboard from several databases.

en.heading: Page links and mentions
paragraphs: @ searches pages, database records and people – keep typing to narrow the list. Journal days come after the other pages. @today, @yesterday (also @heute, @gestern) or a date such as @2026-10-27 offer a link to that day of the journal under Journal. Records appear with their database, such as "Heating – maintenance · Notes"; only records you may read are offered. Mentioning a person notifies them in the inbox.

Links to pages and records stay valid even if they are renamed or moved. A link that shows the old title gets the new one on a rename – in all documents and records you may edit; a link with its own text keeps it. The target lists all links to it under Linked from – including records whose text contains the link. Records and pages you may not read do not appear there.

en.heading: Footnotes
paragraphs: /footnote, ⌘ ⌥ F (Ctrl Alt F) or Footnote in the text menu inserts a footnote at the cursor and opens its text.
– The notes appear numbered under Footnotes at the end of the page. Numbers follow the order in the text and update by themselves when you move, copy or delete markers.
– Clicking a number jumps to its note, ↩ jumps back. Double-click the number (or press ⌘ ⌥ F with a footnote selected) to edit or remove it.
– Notes are plain text; web addresses in them become links.
– Footnotes also show on shared and published pages, in print and in the HTML export, and search finds their text.
– In the Markdown export they become [^1] with [^1]: text at the end; the import reads them back – including Obsidian's short form ^[text].

en.heading: Citations and bibliography
paragraphs: For papers, theses and research notes you cite sources right in the text:
– /cite (or /zitat) opens the workspace's bibliography.
– Search a title, paste a DOI (e.g. 10.1000/xyz123 – Flowplan fetches authors, title and year from Crossref and other DOI services) or bring in a whole list via Import BibTeX or CSL-JSON (Zotero) ….
– Optionally add a page and insert.

The text then reads "(Müller 2021)", "(Müller & Schmidt 2021, p. 12)" or "(Müller et al. 2021)"; hovering shows the full reference. /bibliography inserts a bibliography: all works cited on the page in an APA-like style, updating itself as you cite – also on shared and published pages.
– The bibliography belongs to the workspace; guests don't see it. Each citation carries its details along, so copies, exports and shared pages are complete without the list.
– Zotero: export a collection from Zotero as BibTeX or CSL JSON and import it in the dialog.
– In the Markdown export citations become Pandoc citations ([@key], [@key, p. 12]) and the bibliography a section of its own – so a text can be processed further with Pandoc.

en.heading: Show authors
paragraphs: Show authors (in the toolbar or the page menu …) colours the text by the person who wrote it – each person always in the same colour. A legend shows names and shares; Hide authors turns the colouring off again.
– The content itself doesn't change; the colouring is just a view.
– Recording starts with this feature: older, imported or restored text appears as "earlier", and so does text written by guests through links with their own permissions.
– Images, mentions and other embedded objects are not coloured.
– Only people who may read the page see names.

en.heading: Edit as Markdown
paragraphs: Page menu … → Edit as Markdown shows the whole page as Markdown text with line numbers – handy for big rearrangements, find and replace, or if you prefer writing Markdown.
– Apply (⌘ Enter) saves a version first and replaces the content in one step; Undo takes the change back.

– Blocks without a Markdown form – embeds, whiteboards, linked databases, synced blocks, columns, tables with merged cells or widths, sized images, function graphs, metrics and bibliographies – appear as a marker ``. You can move or delete them but not change them; they come back unchanged. If one is deleted, Flowplan asks before applying.
– Formatting without a Markdown form (colours, superscript, spoilers, mentions, citations) is kept as HTML in the text.
– Alignment, indent, text direction and reactions are lost when applying; the view says beforehand what is affected.
– If someone changes the page while you write in Markdown, a notice appears; Apply anyway then overwrites their changes.
– People who may only read – also on locked pages and in reading mode – see View as Markdown without Apply.

en.heading: Text direction
paragraphs: Paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, callouts and table cells in Arabic, Hebrew or Persian run right to left automatically: the direction follows the block's first letter. Bullets, checkboxes, quote bars, callout icons and block handles are then on the right.

Under Manage blocks (click the handle ⋮⋮) → Text direction you set Automatic, Left to right or Right to left for a block and everything inside it. The direction is kept in the HTML export; Markdown has no place for it.

en.heading: More blocks
paragraphs: – Table of contents: lists the headings of the page and jumps there on click.
– Two columns: blocks side by side; stacked on a phone.
– Linked database: a view of an existing database with its own filters and sorting; changes to records go to the source. See Views.
– Whiteboard: a whiteboard right in the document; the button at the top right opens it large.
– Draw (/draw): a block for handwriting across the full width, blank, lined or grid, with a height you drag; several people draw at once without overwriting each other. See Handwriting in documents.

An encrypted space is meant for journals, passwords and other confidential notes. Content, files and – if you choose – titles are encrypted and decrypted in your browser. The server – and with it the operators, backups and the storage provider – only sees ciphertext.

en.heading: What is protected – and what is not
paragraphs: Encrypted
Text of the documents yes
Files and images in the documents yes, including file name and type
Page titles only with Encrypt titles when creating the space
Page structure, icons, times, sizes no
Name of the space and who is a member no

The encryption protects against reading along on the server and in backups. It does not protect against a server that deliberately serves modified program code: a web app runs the code the server sends. If you do not trust the operator of an instance at all, do not edit confidential data on that instance.

en.heading: Set up your keys
paragraphs: With your first encrypted space – or under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption – you set up your keys:
– Choose a passphrase (at least 10 characters, ideally a whole sentence). It is not your sign-in password and never leaves your browser.
– Keep the recovery key safe: 52 characters in groups of four, to Download or Print. Setup only completes once you confirm you have stored it safely.
