Important: whoever loses the passphrase and the recovery key loses access to their encrypted data. Neither the administrators nor the operator can restore it – the server never saw the keys.

Under Settings → Account & security → End-to-end encryption you can change the passphrase and create a new recovery key (the old one stops working). Only if both are lost: Reset keys … at the very bottom, in the Danger zone. Afterwards a member has to give you access to each encrypted space again.

en.heading: Unlock and automatic locking
paragraphs: Encrypted pages first show Unlock. With the passphrase (or the recovery key plus a new passphrase) you decrypt your keys – only in this browser tab and only in memory. Reloading, Lock now or a period without activity (15 minutes by default, adjustable to 5, 15, 30 or 60) locks again. No readable copy stays on the device; that is why encrypted pages cannot be edited offline.

en.heading: Create a space
paragraphs: Add space → name → tick Encrypted space, optionally Encrypt titles → Create space. An encrypted space is always private. In the sidebar it carries a green lock.
Encrypted spaces hold documents only. Databases, whiteboards, dashboards and journals are not possible here (yet) – write a journal as documents, e.g. one page per month.

en.heading: Members
paragraphs: The lock next to the space name (or Members on a page) opens Members and keys:

– Add: owners of the space or of the workspace give a member the key (Give key). This works only while unlocked, and only for people who have already set up their own keys. New members also read all older content.

– Remove or Leave space: the space gets a new key right away; the removed person cannot read new content. What they could decrypt before, they may have kept – old content is not re-encrypted. Whoever is removed from the workspace loses the keys as well.

en.heading: What does not work in encrypted spaces
paragraphs: Everything that would need the server to read the content is switched off here and refused by the server:
– Search, AI, previews, "Related pages" and unlinked mentions
– Comments and text comments, mentions with notifications
– Share links, sharing single pages and publishing
– Version history, templates, duplicating, moving to other spaces (in or out)
– Export as PDF, DOCX, EPUB, server-side Markdown, Git export
– Webhooks only receive the page ID, MCP clients only metadata

en.heading: Export and backup
paragraphs: The editor offers two ways:
– Markdown (decrypted): the browser turns the page into Markdown and saves the file – the plaintext does not pass through the server.
– Encrypted archive: all pages of the space as ciphertext, plus your encrypted space keys and your key secured with passphrase and recovery key. Without passphrase or recovery key it is unreadable.
Regular instance backups also contain encrypted spaces only as ciphertext.

en.heading: Technical details
paragraphs: X25519 key pairs, AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations for the passphrase, all through the browser's WebCrypto interface (current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari). The full design with the threat model is in docs/e2ee-design.md.
From signing in for the first time to your first own page: what you do with Flowplan in the first ten minutes.

en.heading: Sign in or sign up
paragraphs: You sign in with your e-mail and password, with a passkey (fingerprint, face or device PIN) or – if your organisation has set it up – with Sign in with SSO through your organisation's login (OpenID Connect, such as Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel or Entra ID). You create an account with Create account, provided the instance allows sign-ups or you have been invited. Afterwards you set up passkeys under Settings → Account & security. Everything else is described under Sign-in.

When you sign in for the first time, Flowplan creates a private workspace with example pages. With single sign-on, your name, e-mail address and – if available – your profile picture come from the login provider.

[!TIP] If the instance offers a demo, you can try Flowplan without an account. The demo gets its own example workspace and is deleted completely when you end it, sign out or after 45 minutes without activity.

Language: Flowplan follows your browser's language. Under Settings → Appearance & language → Language you pick German 🇩🇪, English 🇬🇧 or French 🇫🇷 from the list – it then applies on all devices, also to e-mails and push notifications. Further languages can be added: Languages and translations.

en.heading: The introduction
paragraphs: After creating an account, Flowplan walks you through the essentials once. Every step can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in the settings:
– Welcome: language and appearance (automatic, light or dark).
– What would you like to start with? Set the workspace's name (as its owner) and, if you like, create pages right away: a Tasks database, a Notes database, a Journal or a Whiteboard.
– What Flowplan does: a short tour of pages and blocks, databases, whiteboards, the journal, collaboration, sharing, search and offline – each with a tip and a link into this documentation.
– Notifications: e-mail summaries (when the instance sends e-mail) and push on this device.
– All set: the created pages to open and the most important shortcuts.

Later, Settings → Appearance & language → Start introduction (or "introduction" in the search with ⌘/Ctrl + K) opens it again. Accounts that existed before the introduction was added do not see it automatically.

The settings open with an overview: one tile per section, grouped into Personal, Connections and Workspace. The search at the top (“Search settings …”) helps – “passkeys” finds Account & security, for example –, and every section has its own link, e.g. /#settings/notifications.

en.heading: The interface
paragraphs: – Sidebar on the left: workspace switcher, search, home, inbox, your spaces with the page tree, and below them templates, media, trash and settings.
– Home: recently edited pages, quick starts for a new idea or project, and all pages of your workspace – customizable with widgets (see Customize your home page).
– Header of a page: path, share, comments, favourite and the Page actions menu (…).

On a computer, drag the sidebar's right edge to make it wider or narrower (200 to 480 pixels); a double click on the edge restores the original width. Flowplan remembers the width per device. On a phone the sidebar folds away; the menu icon at the top left opens it.

Short animations show what just moved: cards and rows glide into their new place, bars that move along in the timeline visibly follow, and the target of a jump – from the table of contents, search or a notification – lights up briefly. Moving to another page briefly cross-fades the content area; when you open a page in the page tree, its icon and title fly to their place, and a card from a board or gallery grows into its record (on a phone the record comes up as a sheet). A tap or a key ends such a transition at once, and clicking quickly from one page to the next goes without one. While uploaded images load, they show a blurred preview in their final size and then fade in – nothing below them moves. The animations follow the system setting Reduce motion: when it is on, everything moves to its target without motion, and jump targets are only highlighted briefly and still.

en.heading: Customize your home page
paragraphs: The home page is yours: Customize at the top right (or “Customize home page” in quick search) lets you arrange it from widgets the way you work. On phones everything sits in one column, on tablets in two, on large screens in three or four – the iPhone, iPad and Android apps and the desktop app show the same home page.
While customizing:

– Widget opens the gallery: greeting, recently edited or viewed, favourites, the workspace's pages, my tasks, inbox, journal today, agenda, database view, pinned page, quick capture, focus & time, habits, counter, scratchpad, activity, this week, links and – for administrators – the instance status.
– Move: drag the handle, use the up/down arrows, or the keyboard – focus the handle, then the arrow keys, Home and End.
– Size: small (one column), medium (two), large (three) or full width. A widget never gets wider than the space there is.

– Settings (gear): a heading of your own and what the widget shows – for My tasks “Due today and overdue”, “Due today”, “Overdue” or “All open”, from your tasks or the open records of a database view; for the Agenda the period (today, 3 or 7 days) and which calendar and timeline views count (also those connected to Google, Microsoft 365 or CalDAV).
– Appearance: a header with a colour, a gradient or a page's cover image, an emoji as icon, comfortable or compact spacing, a subtle background (dots, grid, tinted) and a normal or wide page.
– Done saves, Cancel discards. In the … menu you save the home page for all your workspaces (otherwise it applies to this one only) or reset it.

You tick off tasks right in the widget, habits too; the journal widget adds a few lines to today's entry, and the scratchpad holds whatever fits nowhere else – it saves as you type and is the same on all devices.
Widgets only show what you may see anyway: pages of other workspaces do not appear, journals behind a PIN only show their name, and the home page sees no content of end-to-end encrypted spaces.
[!TIP] Workspace owners can use … → Set as default for members to choose the home page new members (and everyone without their own) see. Personal notes are not passed on.

en.heading: Your first page
paragraphs: – Click + next to a space in the sidebar or choose New page on the home screen.
– Choose the type: Document, Database, Whiteboard or Journal.
– Enter a title and start writing. Everything is saved automatically, even without a connection.
In a document, / opens the block menu: type /h2, /todo or /table and press Enter to insert. How the editor works in detail is explained under Documents and the editor.

en.heading: Find instead of search
paragraphs: ⌘ K (Windows/Linux: Ctrl K) opens the quick search across titles, text, database records, comments and even the content of uploaded PDFs and Office files. More under Search, inbox and push.

en.heading: Where to go next
paragraphs: – Pages and spaces: page tree, favourites, moving and trash.
– Databases: tables, boards, calendars and more from the same records.
– Collaboration and comments: write together, comment, mention.

en.heading: Help and community
paragraphs: Questions, ideas or just saying hello: in the Flowplan Discord users and admins help each other. Bugs and feature requests are best filed as GitHub issues, so nothing gets lost.
A form view collects answers directly as records in the database – from members or, if enabled, from anyone with the link.

en.heading: Design a form
paragraphs: – Create a view of the type Form in the database.
– Design form opens the editor:
– title, description and the label of the submit button,
– questions: order, hide, required, help text per question,
– question type: short or long text, radio buttons instead of a list, a linear scale 1–10 for numbers,
– Only show if … per question (see Conditions and pages),
– Text block before, Text block at the end and New page from here for explanations and several pages,
– title after submitting and confirmation text,
– what happens after sending (see Settings).
– Save form.
Flowplan checks required fields and input types in the browser and on the server. Files properties allow uploads in the form.

en.heading: Conditions and pages
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – for example “Kind is Bug”, “Topics includes Billing”, “Subject contains the text invoice”, “Importance is greater than 7” or “E-mail is answered”. A hidden page break hides its whole page.
– Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved – not even when they are sent anyway. The server checks the same rules as the browser.
– A question that depends on a hidden question stays hidden as well.
– With several pages a progress bar shows how far along you are (can be switched off); Back and Next change the page, and required questions are checked per page.

en.heading: Settings
paragraphs: Under After sending, Confirmation by e-mail and Notify the team – in the form editor as well as in a survey's settings:
– Then redirect to: an address with https:// that the thank-you page leads to after a few seconds (0–60, default 3).

– Placeholders: {Name of the question} inserts the answer to that question – in the title and text after submitting, in the redirect (there only after the domain name, e.g. https://example.com/thanks?name={Name}) and in the e-mail. Unknown names stay as they are; people, relations and files are not inserted.

– Confirmation by e-mail to the people answering: subject and text are up to you. The e-mail contains the text and the answered questions as a list – without hidden and internal properties – and, with the customer portal, the link to the request (then only this one e-mail is sent). It goes to the first answered e-mail question; in forms that are not anonymous, otherwise to the signed-in account's address. Anonymous forms only write when the person types their address. E-mail must be set up (Configuration); at most 5 e-mails per hour go to an address, 10 per sender and 300 per form.
– Notify the team: the chosen members get a notification of the kind “Guest comments and guest records” for each new answer – if they may see the record.

en.heading: Continue later
paragraphs: In forms and surveys that are not anonymous, Save and continue later keeps your answers so far as a draft for you (without files). When you open the link again, you continue on the same page; after sending, the draft is gone. Drafts unchanged for half a year are deleted.

en.heading: Share a form
paragraphs: Under Share form, switch the form on and copy the link.
– Members only: answering requires signing in; the answer carries the person's name.

– Anonymous: anyone with the link can answer, without an account and without a name. Files from anonymous answers count against a daily budget: 200 MB per form and FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB for the whole instance (Configuration); each form also accepts at most 1000 answers per hour.
Person and relation questions only exist in forms for members, because they would reveal members and records.
[!NOTE] Copied or imported forms start switched off and for members only. In the demo, forms can be designed but not made public, and confirmation e-mails cannot be switched on.

en.heading: Answers
paragraphs: Every answer is a normal record: it appears in all views and can be filtered, assigned and commented on.

en.heading: Surveys
paragraphs: Turn into a survey makes a form a survey – or create a new page from the Survey template. The builder has five tabs: Questions, Preview, Settings, Share and Results.

On the left is the flow with numbered questions, text blocks and page breaks; on the right you edit the selected item. Add question shows the question types grouped into choice, rating, and text and details. Everything is saved automatically shortly after you stop typing – the dot at the top right shows the state. If something is still missing (a question without text, an empty answer, a redirect without https://), saving waits and says why.

en.heading: Question types
paragraphs: Surveys have {{facts.questionTypes}} question types:
– Text: short answer, long text, e-mail, phone, website, number, date, time
– Choice: single choice, multiple choice, dropdown, yes / no – optionally with “Other” and a text field, a random order and a minimum or maximum number
– Rating: stars (3 to 10), Net Promoter Score (0–10), a scale with labels at both ends, a slider
– Matrix (Likert): several statements with the same answers
– Ranking: put items in order
– File upload
– Also text blocks for explanations and page breaks for several pages.
Pasting several lines into an answer field adds several answers at once.

en.heading: Conditions
paragraphs: Every question, text block and page break can Only show if … an earlier answer matches – with the same comparisons as in forms. Example: “What should we improve?” only appears for a recommendation score up to 6. Hidden questions are not required, and their answers are not saved.

en.heading: Survey settings
paragraphs: – a welcome page, a progress bar for several pages, a thank-you text with placeholders
– redirect, confirmation e-mail and team notification as for forms
– Closes on and At most this many answers – after that the survey takes no more answers
– One answer per person – signed-in people by their account, anonymous ones by their connection
– an accent colour

en.heading: Sharing and results
paragraphs: Share opens the survey. It can be public, so anyone with the link can take part, and anonymous, so without signing in and without names.
Every answer is a record of the database. Each question is a property, a matrix one property per row. So you can filter and sort answers, export them as CSV and process them with automations.
Results shows:
– the answers per day,
– per question the count and share of every answer,
– averages, minimum and maximum,
– the NPS score with promoters, passives and detractors,
– matrix tables, the average places of rankings and the latest text answers.
[!NOTE] Renaming a question keeps its answers. Changing the type so that the stored kind changes (e.g. from text to number) creates a new property – earlier answers stay in the old one.

en.heading: Customer portal
paragraphs: The customer portal turns a form into a service desk: whoever sends it can follow their request afterwards.
– Under Share form, switch on the customer portal.

– Choose which properties are visible in the portal – for example Status or a due date. A select property named “Status” is preselected when you switch it on. People, relations and files always stay internal.

After sending, the person sees a private link to their request. If they answered an e-mail question and e-mail is set up, the link also arrives by e-mail – in their language; with the confirmation e-mail switched on, it is part of that one e-mail. The page shows the status, their answers and a conversation with the team.

The team replies in the record under Customer request. Replies go to the person by e-mail; when they write back, the people on the record, everyone who already replied and whoever created the database get a notification. Copy customer link passes the link on when there is no e-mail address.
[!NOTE] The link is the key: anyone who has it sees the request and can reply. Switching off the customer portal or the form stops all links from working; switching it back on restores them.
Content comes in as Markdown, CSV or an archive and goes out again as Markdown, PDF or a complete archive. The version history brings back earlier states.

en.heading: Export
paragraphs: Page actions → Export:
Format Content
Markdown (.md) One file with the page content; databases with an overview, properties and the documents of all records.

Markdown with files (.zip) index.md, sub-pages under pages/, the days of a journal in its folder under 2026/10/2026-10-27.md (see below), record documents under records/, databases also as CSV under tables/, attachments under assets/ – all linked relatively. Every record under records/ starts with its properties as YAML frontmatter (see below). With Include comments and earlier versions, .comments.md and .versions/ come along.
As Word (DOCX) A Word document of the page – see Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book.
As PDF (with sub-pages) The page with its sub-pages as one document with a cover and a table of contents, which the print dialog saves as PDF.
As e-book (EPUB) The page with its sub-pages as an e-book for e-readers and e-book apps.
HTML / JSON The older format for documents and databases.

Print / PDF opens the browser's print view; save as PDF there. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad cannot print themselves: they open the page in Safari under a secret address for 15 minutes. This print view shows content only – no form fields, buttons or scripts – and at the top who created it.
The export respects read permissions and contains all records regardless of view filters. Formulas and Mermaid are kept as source.

Whiteboards come along in the ZIP as SVG images under assets/: a whiteboard page shows its image, and a whiteboard embedded in a document becomes the image with a link to the board in Flowplan. The image is cropped like Export as SVG in the board; pictures on the board sit next to it under assets/. Covered items stay covered, comment pins are not included; an empty board gives a short note instead of an image. Since SVG is text, Git shows changes to a board as a readable diff. The board cannot be edited outside Flowplan.

Journal days sort by path in the ZIP, in their journal's folder: 2026/10/2026-10-27.md next to the index.md of an exported journal, for a journal below another page under pages/-/2026/10/…. The heading is the day's title in the export's language ("Tuesday, 27 October 2026"; a renamed day keeps its title), the frontmatter names id and date (flowplan: id, date). This applies to the page and space export, the scheduled export and Git. The ZIP import turns them back into a journal with its days, without folder pages "2026" or "10"; a second file of the same date does not become a second day.
Limits per export: 500 pages, 5,000 records, 250 MB of content.

en.heading: Word, PDF with sub-pages and e-book
paragraphs: Three more formats for handbooks, reports and everything that is read or edited outside Flowplan. All three start from the same cleaned page content as the Markdown export and respect read permissions in the same way: they contain only what you may read – other people's private records, PIN-locked journals and pictures from pages you may not open stay out (a note stands in for such a picture, and a link to an inaccessible page becomes plain text).

As Word (DOCX) – Page actions → Export → As Word (DOCX), for a database also via Export in the toolbar, for a single record via the … menu in the record's header. The file is written by Flowplan itself, without a Word library, and opens in Word, LibreOffice and Pages:
– Headings (as Word heading styles, so the navigation pane works), paragraphs with alignment, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, highlights, text colour, superscript and subscript, links.
– Bulleted and numbered lists, also nested, tasks with ☐/☑ and their due date.
– Tables with merged cells and a shaded header row.
– Pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) embedded and scaled to the text width; the page's cover image at the top.

– Callouts (note, tip, important, warning, caution) as shaded paragraphs, quotes with a side line, code blocks, formulas and Mermaid diagrams in a monospace style, toggles with their title, columns one after another.
– Footnotes as real Word footnotes, citations and the bibliography as text.
– A database becomes a table of all records followed by every record's document; a single record starts with its properties as a table.
– Not included: whiteboards, embedded videos, audio, PDFs, link cards and linked databases (they stay links to Flowplan), function plots and metrics (a note), comments and versions.

As PDF (with sub-pages) – Page actions → Export → As PDF (with sub-pages): the page with all accessible sub-pages (can be turned off) becomes a print view with a cover, a table of contents and every page as a numbered chapter on a new page; links between the pages jump within the document. As with Print / PDF, the browser's print dialog opens – save as PDF there. Home screen apps on iPhone and iPad open the view in Safari as usual. Whiteboards come along as pictures, databases as a table with the records' documents. Page numbers in the table of contents and the footer appear only in renderers that know target-counter (Prince, Paged.js); browsers leave them out. For scripts: GET /api/export/pdf?page=&children=1 returns the HTML of the print view.

As e-book (EPUB) – Page actions → Export → As e-book (EPUB): the page with its sub-pages as EPUB 3 – every page a chapter, the table of contents nested like the page tree, pictures and whiteboards as resources, links between the pages within the book, footnotes at the end of each chapter. Suitable for Apple Books, Kindle (after conversion), Calibre, Thorium and other readers. For scripts: GET /api/export/epub?page=&children=1.
Limits: 200 pages per PDF or EPUB export, 5,000 records, 100 MB of attachments (files over 25 MB are left out). Database tables with more than 200 columns cannot be exported to Word.

en.heading: Export a whole space
paragraphs: The download icon next to a space's name in the sidebar (or Settings → Import & export → Export → One space) opens the space export. Besides the Markdown ZIP it offers Space as PDF (a print view of all pages of the space with a cover and a table of contents, see above) and Space as e-book (EPUB) – each with everything you may read, up to 200 pages (GET /api/export/pdf?space= or /api/export/epub?space=). The Markdown ZIP downloads the whole space as one archive – to archive, read offline or put into your own Git repository:
– Every top-level page is in a folder of its own, -/, with everything below it – the same layout as the scheduled Markdown export. Inside, the format of Markdown with files (.zip) applies.
– index.md at the top lists the space's pages; links between pages of the space are relative, links into other spaces keep pointing to Flowplan.

– Anyone who can read the space may export it, no administrator needed. It contains only what that person may read: other people's private records and PIN-locked journals stay out, and other people's private spaces cannot be exported.
– Include comments and earlier versions works as for the page export; the same limits apply, for the whole space.
– For scripts with a read token: {"spaceId":"…","format":"zip","history":true} to /api/markdown-export (see API tokens). The space's id is shown in the export dialog.
– Regularly into a Git repository, without a script of your own: the Git export of a space, set up by the owner of the space.

en.heading: Print and PDF
paragraphs: Page actions → Print (or > print in the quick search) prints the page as a clean A4 document – in the print dialog it can also be saved as PDF. The sidebar, toolbars, handles, comment bars and notices disappear; colours are always light, blocks are not split in the middle of a page, long code lines wrap and external links are written out with their address.

en.heading: Import
paragraphs: All imports are under Settings → Import & export → Import; at the top you choose the Target space once for all of them.
– Markdown, text or HTML: Markdown, text or HTML files. Headings, lists, tasks, tables, code (also mermaid) and formulas become blocks.

– Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export: Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export (ZIP) accepts a ZIP with Markdown and CSV files. Markdown becomes pages, CSV databases, days of a Flowplan journal (…/2026/10/2026-10-27.md below the journal) days of that journal again, Excalidraw and draw.io files whiteboards, folders sub-pages; linked images and files are uploaded, and Notion record pages are matched to their records. Up to 100 MB, 500 pages and 5,000 records per table; you choose the target space beforehand.
– Jira or Trello: Jira or Trello – see Projects, tickets and sprints.
– CSV: in a database, choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick a CSV file; the rows become records.
– Markdown with frontmatter into a database (such as notes from Obsidian): in the database, choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick one or more .md files or a ZIP – see below.
– Content archive (see below).

en.heading: Frontmatter: records as Markdown files
paragraphs: Notes from Obsidian, Logseq, Jekyll or Hugo carry their properties as YAML frontmatter at the top of the file:
para: Resource
area: House
tags: [heating, maintenance]
# Heating – maintenance

Import into a database: every file becomes a record. The title comes from title:, otherwise from the first # heading or the file name; the rest of the text becomes the record's document, linked images and files from the ZIP are uploaded, and links between the imported files become links to the new records. Keys are matched to properties of the same name (case does not matter):
– select and multi-select take the values and add unknown ones as new options (so tags: lands in Tags);
– relations find the linked record by its title (also as [[Title]]), people by name or e-mail;
– dates are read as ISO dates, true/false as checkboxes, numbers as numbers;

– aliases: (a list or one text, separated by commas) and alias: together fill the property of type Aliases, whatever its name; if there is none, Create missing properties adds one. A database without an aliases property but with a property named "aliases" gets the values there, as before;
– computed properties (formulas, rollups, timestamps) are not overwritten.

Before the import, a preview shows which properties match and which are missing. Create missing properties adds them with a fitting type: list → multi-select, ISO date → date, true/false → checkbox, number → number, address → URL, a few recurring values → select, otherwise text. Up to 5,000 files and 100 MB per import.

Export: in the ZIP export, every record under records/ starts with title: and its properties: select as text, multi-select and relations (titles of the linked records) as lists, dates as ISO dates. Aliases are written under Obsidian's key aliases: as a list, so they survive a trip to Obsidian and back. Computed values and the record's id are below flowplan: and are skipped on import. When a record exported this way is imported into the same database again, the preview offers update instead of adding: the record with the same id gets the file's properties and text, and the previous state stays as a version. Without this choice it is added as a new record.

Pages: when a page has aliases, its Markdown file (single page, space export and scheduled export) starts with frontmatter that only holds aliases:; pages without aliases keep no frontmatter. The ZIP import under Settings → Import & export reads a note's aliases:/alias: as the aliases of the new page; frontmatter holding nothing but aliases is removed from the text, other frontmatter stays in the text as before. The Git export reads aliases of changed pages back as well.

Where to export: in a database's toolbar, Export opens a menu with CSV (current view), Markdown with files (.zip), Markdown (.md) and As Word (DOCX). A single record is exported from the … menu in its header: Export as Markdown (.md) (with frontmatter), Markdown with files (.zip), As Word (DOCX) (properties as a table, then the document) or Print / PDF.

From Obsidian: links in the text are read as standard Markdown links. Convert wikilinks ([[…]], ![[…]]) first – in Obsidian, Settings → Files and links, turn off “Use [[Wikilinks]]” and choose relative paths.

en.heading: Content archive
paragraphs: Under Settings → Import & export → Export → Workspace as ZIP you download a ZIP of your workspace. To bring it back – also into another Flowplan instance – use Backups → Restore a Flowplan archive: the archive is created as a copy in new private spaces.

Backing up the whole instance (with accounts and permissions) is up to the administration: Administration → Storage & backup. The card Trash & retention leads to the trash and says how long things are kept: deleted pages and spaces until someone deletes them permanently, deleted database records 30 days; how long earlier versions stay is set by the administration.

It contains: accessible pages including the trash, databases with views and records, document content, relations, templates, comments, versions, favourites and form options, plus all files with checksums. Also the settings of databases (done rule, workflow, automations, sprints, story points – never the Git token), time entries and the status history behind burndown charts, the settings and trackers of journals with each day's values and place, handwriting on PDFs and your home page (applied only when the person importing has none of their own yet).

The archive only holds what you may see yourself: other people's private records with their comments and files are left out, as are journals behind a PIN you have not unlocked right now. Versions of a database are included only for owners, because they contain every record.
– Importing creates new IDs; internal links and relations are rewritten – embedded whiteboards, synced blocks, metrics, drawing blocks and records on whiteboard cards too.
– If the archive comes from someone else, their assignments and mentions become yours; tasks in documents show under My tasks right away.
– Older archives import as before; older servers skip what they do not know.
– Imported spaces and templates are private, shares and forms are not active.
– A failed import is rolled back completely.
– Limits: 2 GB ZIP, 500 pages, 20,000 files, 5,000 records per database.
Accounts, sessions and sign-in are not part of it – operations back them up every day with the whole instance.

en.heading: Version history
paragraphs: Page actions → Version history:
– Documents save automatically at most every five minutes, databases before the first change after ten quiet minutes.
– Save current version creates a state at any time; manually saved versions are kept permanently.
– Changes compares a version with the current state or with any other version (Compare with): added and removed text, for databases new, changed and removed records and properties.

– The comparison in detail: it walks the document block by block – headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells, quotes and code stay recognisable as such – and marks the single words inside a changed block: additions green, deletions red and struck through; unchanged blocks are dimmed. A summary states how many words came and went (for example "+120 words · −35 words"), and the arrows jump from change to change, also by keyboard. The same applies to the versions of a record document. Very long documents (more than 60,000 words on both sides together) or versions that differ in too many places are reported as too large to compare; they can still be restored.

– Bring back single paragraphs: compared with the current state, every removed or changed paragraph has a Restore button. The paragraph returns to its old place with its formatting; the rest of the page stays as it is.
– Restore sets the page back to that state. The authors view then starts over; the restored text appears as "earlier".
Automatic versions are thinned out to one per day after seven days and deleted after 180 days (adjustable in the administration).
Flowplan runs as a single container with SQLite and a data directory. Postgres, Redis or a separate search service are not needed.

en.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: – A server with Docker and a persistent volume. Text recognition for scanned PDFs briefly needs noticeable CPU when uploading.
– A domain with HTTPS behind a reverse proxy (Traefik, Caddy, nginx, Coolify, Pangolin …).
– Optionally an OpenID Connect provider for single sign-on. Without one, people sign in with e-mail and password or a passkey, see Sign-in.
– Optionally an S3-compatible storage for files and the continuous database backup, see Storage, S3 and backups.

en.heading: With Docker Compose
paragraphs: Flowplan is open source (AGPL-3.0). The ready-made image is in the GitHub Container Registry, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64:
Tag Content
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest The latest version (release)
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:0.7.0 A fixed version (currently 0.7.0), also as :0.7 and :0
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:beta The latest manually built development state – for trying out, not for production
Download the Compose file and the example configuration:
mkdir flowplan && cd flowplan
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/compose.yaml
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/.env.example
In .env, set at least the public address:
APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com

For single sign-on also set OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP (see Sign-in); for e-mails (invitations, forgotten passwords) the SMTP_* values from the configuration.
docker compose up -d

The container listens on port 3000 (bound to 127.0.0.1 only in the Compose file, so that the proxy sits in front of it). The volume flowplan-data on /app/data holds all content independently of the container. Choose a fixed version with FLOWPLAN_VERSION=0.7.0 in .env.
[!NOTE] An instance opens with the sign-in page. The website flowplan.org and this documentation are separate projects; the hosted instance runs at app.flowplan.org.

en.heading: Build the image yourself
paragraphs: From the source code (github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan):
git clone https://github.com/yannicschuller/flowplan.git && cd flowplan
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d --build
Or without Compose:
docker build -t flowplan:latest .
docker run -d --name flowplan \
-v flowplan-data:/app/data \
--env-file .env \
flowplan:latest
The image contains Node, Litestream for the S3 backup and curl for the health check. It runs as the user node (UID 1000).

en.heading: First start
paragraphs: – Open https://flowplan.example.com/api/health – the answer is 200 with "status":"ok".

– Open the address in the browser: a new instance offers Create account. This first account administers the instance. (With single sign-on: Sign in with SSO; administrators are the members of the group in OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.)
– In the sidebar under Administration, set the instance name, upload limit, sign-ups and the other settings.

[!WARNING] Flowplan is built for exactly one running instance. Several replicas would write to the same SQLite file. Do not scale horizontally; when updating, stop the old container before the new one.

en.heading: Update
paragraphs: When a newer release exists, the administration shows a notice with the new version number and a link to the changes (turn off with FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_CHECK=false, see Configuration). With the image tag :latest, this is all it takes:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
With a self-built image, use git pull and docker compose up -d --build instead.
On start, Flowplan migrates the database itself. Make a backup beforehand (see Storage, S3 and backups); going back to an older version after a migration is not supported.

en.heading: Upgrading to 0.7.0
paragraphs: Nothing to do by hand; Flowplan creates the new tables (for idempotency keys and the push relay, among others) on start. What changes for operations:
– API description only when signed in: /api/openapi.json and /api/docs need a sign-in or an API token. Public as before with FLOWPLAN_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true (see OpenAPI and SDKs).
– A shorter health check: without a token, /api/health only answers {"service":"flowplan","status":"ok"}; the details come with FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN (see Health check).

– Push to the apps through the push relay: notifications to the apps go end-to-end encrypted through push.flowplan.org. APP_URL must be the public HTTPS address and outgoing HTTPS to the relay possible – see Push relay.
– Usage statistics: monitoring counts requests, active people and storage – numbers only. Switch it off with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off or in the administration (see Statistics).

en.heading: Kubernetes (Helm)
paragraphs: The chart lives in the repository at deploy/helm/flowplan. Flowplan runs as exactly one pod (SQLite) with a volume for /app/data; updates replace the pod with a short downtime (strategy Recreate). The chart (version 0.1.0) installs Flowplan 0.7.0 (appVersion); choose another version with --set image.tag=….
kubectl create namespace flowplan
kubectl -n flowplan create secret generic flowplan-env \
--from-literal=FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
helm install flowplan deploy/helm/flowplan -n flowplan \
--set appUrl=https://flowplan.example.org \
--set existingSecret=flowplan-env \
--set ingress.enabled=true \
--set ingress.hosts[0].host=flowplan.example.org
– Set OIDC, SMTP and S3 via oidc., smtp. and s3.*; secrets preferably in existingSecret (keys are the names of the environment variables). Further variables via env.
– appUrl is required (or taken from the first ingress host).
– Use a block or local volume, not NFS (SQLite).
– Health checks use /api/health; the pod runs as user 1000 without extra privileges. helm test flowplan checks that it answers.
– The volume is kept on uninstall.
– To update: git pull in the repository, then helm upgrade flowplan deploy/helm/flowplan -n flowplan --reuse-values.
The chart's README explains every value.

en.heading: Without Docker
paragraphs: Node.js 22.13 or newer (the image uses Node 26):
npm ci
npm run build
FLOWPLAN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/flowplan npm start
For local development, npm run dev is enough. Development mode also offers Open local workspace, a shared example account; production mode has no such access.

en.heading: Next
paragraphs: – Configuration: all environment variables.
– Coolify and reverse proxies: running behind Traefik, Coolify or Pangolin.
A journal is a page with one sub-page per day. In the morning today's page is ready, with yesterday's open tasks already on it.

en.heading: Create a journal
paragraphs: New page → Journal. The page shows Today at the top and the past days below it with relative labels such as "Yesterday". The day pages are named after the date automatically, such as "Saturday, 26 September 2026".

en.heading: How a day comes about
paragraphs: – When a new day is opened for the first time, Flowplan creates its page. The day starts at midnight in your time zone.
– Open tasks from the last day move over – including nested sub-tasks. A small ↻ at the corner of the checkbox shows that a task was carried over from an earlier day.
– Completed tasks and the rest of the text stay on their day.
– Empty days disappear: if a day got nothing of its own besides carried-over tasks, it is removed again on the next day. This way the journal only contains days on which something happened.

en.heading: Create the day's page: automatically or on the first write
paragraphs: Under Set up journal → Days you decide when today's page is created:
– Automatically (default): as described above, as soon as the day starts and the journal or the app is opened.

– On the first write: Today first shows a draft with the template and the tasks that would be carried over from the last day. Nothing is saved yet – the top bar says "Draft – created when you start writing". Only the first keystroke, a ticked task, a tracker value, a place or a file creates the page. Until then carried-over tasks stay on their day, and the draft appears neither in the sidebar nor in search, graph or export.

The draft is the same on every device: if two devices start writing at the same time, exactly one page is created and both texts end up in it. If what the day starts with changed in the meantime (for example because a task was ticked yesterday on another device), Flowplan opens the stored page and says so. Text typed offline stays on the device and creates the page as soon as the connection is back.
Every day remembers which version of the template it was created from. A day that only holds that template counts as empty even if the template was changed later.

en.heading: Remove empty days
paragraphs: Set up journal → Days → Find empty days lists old days on which nothing was written: only the template, no open tasks of its own, no tracker values or places, no files, comments, sub-pages, favourites, shares or links from other pages, title and icon unchanged (upper/lower case or spaces do not count as a change). Today always stays. You untick what should stay and move the rest with Move … days to the trash – days can be restored from there. Flowplan never removes or merges old days on its own.

en.heading: Daily template
paragraphs: Set up journal (gear on the journal page) → Template: every new day starts with this content, such as "Grateful for", "Focus today" and "Evening review". Ready-made templates are available (gratitude & focus, 5-minute journal, work log, daily review); Use today makes the current day the template. Tasks from the template come back every day and are not carried over in addition. A day that only holds the template counts as empty and disappears like any empty day.

en.heading: Trackers, place and appointments
paragraphs: Above every day there is a bar:
– Trackers: mood (😞 to 😄), scales from 1 to 5, numbers with a unit (e.g. sleep in hours) or yes/no (e.g. sport). You decide which ones exist under Set up journal → Trackers.
– Place: enter freely; Location also stores the device's coordinates with a link to the map.

– Appointments: records of all databases with a date that you may see, including recurrences. Under Set up journal → Calendar you can also add a calendar via an iCal link (Google, Apple, Outlook, Nextcloud …).
In the settings under Day bar, place and appointments can be switched off for the whole journal.

en.heading: Meeting notes
paragraphs: Next to every appointment there is Create meeting note. Flowplan creates a page below the journal – with the title and date of the appointment, the Attendees, an Agenda, Notes and Tasks – and opens it. Afterwards the appointment shows Open note.

– Attendees: from the connected Google or Outlook calendar, from the iCal link and from person properties of the record. Whoever is a member of the workspace with that e-mail address is mentioned; others are listed with name and address.
– Tasks with @person show up for that person in My tasks right away.
– For records of a database the note links the record. A PIN lock of the journal also covers its meeting notes.
– The same outline is available as the template Meeting note under Templates → Meetings.

en.heading: In the sidebar
paragraphs: Even after years with thousands of days, the journal stays short in the sidebar. Below the journal you find:
– Today – also when today's page has not been created yet; a click opens the day,
– the last 7 days,
– All days … with the number of all days: opens the journal page at its list or calendar.
Other sub-pages of the journal (such as meeting notes or monthly summaries) follow below as usual.
Under Set up journal → Days you choose for each journal which days appear in the sidebar:
– None
– Last 7 days (the default)

– Grouped by year and month: as above, older days in addition in folders by year and month, such as "October 2026 · 18". The folders only exist in the sidebar, they are not pages – you cannot drag anything into them.
– All: every single day, as before.

When a day is open, the sidebar always shows it – also when it is older than 7 days; in the grouped view its year and month unfold. Days can still be dragged, and the arrow keys work in the folders too (→ opens, ← closes or jumps to the folder above).

en.heading: From day to day
paragraphs: Above every day page there is a bar:
– ← Previous day and Next day → jump to the previous or next day with an entry – gaps are skipped.
– Today opens today's day.
– The month (such as "October 2026") opens a small calendar: days with an entry are highlighted and can be opened. The arrow keys move by a day or a week, Page ↑/Page ↓ by a month; Esc closes it.

From anywhere, ⌘ ⌥ Y (Windows/Linux: Ctrl Alt Y) or the command Journal: Today in the quick search (⌘ K) takes you to today – of the journal used last. With several journals the quick search offers one entry per journal. The shortcut can be changed (see Keyboard shortcuts).

en.heading: Overview on the journal page
paragraphs: – Streak: how many days in a row you have written, plus the longest streak, entries and words.
– Heatmap: the last year as squares, the darker the more you wrote. A click opens the day.
– On this day: entries from a week, a month, half a year and whole years ago.
– Last 30 days: the course of every tracker.
– List or calendar: the list shows an excerpt, place, mood and the first photo of each day; the calendar shows a month with photos as backgrounds.

en.heading: Review
paragraphs: Review sums up a week or a month: days, words, completed and still open tasks, tracker averages, places and photos. Copy as Markdown takes the summary along, for example into a weekly report.

en.heading: Monthly summary
paragraphs: In the review of a month, Create monthly summary creates a normal sub-page of the journal – not a day – and opens it, such as "Monthly summary October 2026". It holds:
– days, words, completed and still open tasks in numbers,
– Highlights: tracker averages, places, photos and the completed tasks with a link to their day,
– Still open: tasks from this month that are still open today, with a link to the day they are on now,
– Days: every day as a link with the beginning of its text.

The page is built from your entries alone, without AI, and can be edited freely afterwards. If the month already has a summary, the review offers Open monthly summary; Create a new one anyway deliberately adds another one.

en.heading: PIN lock
paragraphs: Under Set up journal → Lock, a PIN of 6 to 8 digits protects the journal (shorter PINs set earlier keep working): days, search, previews and images stay hidden until the PIN is entered. After 15 minutes or with the lock button it locks itself again. After five wrong attempts there is a five-minute pause, after twenty in one day it is over until the next day – across server restarts too. When another person enters a wrong PIN five times, the person who created the journal gets a notification. Changing or removing it requires the current PIN. The lock also covers sub-pages of days as well as export, the content archive, comments, share links and duplicating – unlock first for those. It protects against glances but is no encryption: whoever has access to the server's backups sees the content.

en.heading: If today's page was deleted
paragraphs: If today's page is in the trash, the journal says so and offers Create again (a fresh page for today; with On the first write a new draft) or Restore from trash.

en.heading: Days in lists, search, graph and export
paragraphs: A journal soon has hundreds of days. So that they do not crowd out other pages:
– Search and @ mentions: days come after all other hits. The filter Without journal days in the quick search leaves them out completely (it stays on for the next search).

– @heute, @gestern and @2026-10-27 (also @today, @yesterday) insert a link to that day of the journal while writing – the journal in the page's space, otherwise the one written in last. Today works as when opening the journal: the page is created or, with On the first write, the link goes to the draft. Days without an entry cannot be linked.
– Graph: under Journal days the graph hides the days, shows one dot per month (default) or each day.
– Counting: the home page, space settings and administration count days separately, such as "120 pages · 340 journal days".
– Export: in the Markdown ZIP, the scheduled export and Git, days sort by path in their journal's folder under 2026/10/2026-10-27.md – see Import, export and versions.
Journals behind a PIN you have not entered appear in none of these – not even in the numbers.

en.heading: Tips
paragraphs: – /todo or [] + space creates tasks that move along. They also appear under My tasks, without any @mention.
– Day pages are normal documents: headings, tables, images, mentions – everything works.
– Journals can be shared like any page. Whoever may only read sees the days but does not create any.
– The quick search finds entries across all days; Without journal days hides them.
All shortcuts at a glance. On Windows and Linux, Ctrl stands for ⌘ and Alt for ⌥.

⇧ ⌘ Space / Ctrl Shift Space Desktop app: quick capture from any app (Quick capture (desktop))

In the desktop app, ⌘ ⇧ P or Ctrl Shift P switches to the next profile once more than one is saved.

en.heading: Your own shortcuts
paragraphs: ? (outside text fields), ⌘ /, the ? at the bottom of the sidebar or Show keyboard shortcuts under Settings → Appearance & language open the overview. Under Everywhere, every action has a Change button: press the new combination after it – Esc cancels. The combination applies at once and for your account on all devices and browsers.

– The overview shows conflicts: if the combination already belongs to another action, it asks (Use it anyway takes it away from the other action). If it collides with an editor shortcut (such as ⌘ B for bold) or the browser usually keeps it for itself (such as ⌘ W), a note appears below it.
– The arrow resets an action to its default, × removes its shortcut altogether, Reset all restores every default. Your own shortcuts are marked Custom.
– Combinations without ⌘, Ctrl or ⌥ (like ?) only work outside text fields and the editor.
– The shortcuts of the editor, the page tree, presentations and the split view are fixed; the overview lists them for reference.
In the iPad app with a hardware keyboard, holding ⌘ lists the shortcuts with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ – your own combinations included – in the iPad's overlay.
The overview names the keys as your device does: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Through the API, the command shortcuts.save stores the same settings (see API and webhooks).
