Flowplan is available in {{facts.languages word}} languages: German, English and French. Further languages can be added without changing the app's code – with any translation tool that understands JSON files.

en.heading: Choosing a language
paragraphs: Flowplan follows your browser's language; languages Flowplan does not know show English. Under Settings → Appearance & language → Language you pick a language (with its flag) from the list – it then applies on all devices, also to e-mails and push notifications; Automatic (follows the browser) undoes the choice. On the sign-in page the small button at the bottom right (e.g. 🇬🇧 EN) opens a menu with all languages.
Dates, times and numbers follow the language (French: fr-FR, e.g. “15 oct. 2026” and “2 400,5”). Calculations in notes use the decimal comma in French as well.
What you create yourself – pages, databases, properties – stays in the language it was made in. Templates and example content exist in German and English; French accounts get the English ones.

en.heading: How translation works
paragraphs: German and English sit side by side in the code. Every further language is a catalogue in the app's locales/ folder that maps the English text to its translation:
"Sign in": "Se connecter",
"{0} commented on “{1}”": "{0} a commenté « {1} »"
– locales/en.json lists every text of the app (more than 3,500) and is the source for translation tools. It is generated, not edited by hand.
– {0}, {1} … stand for values such as names or numbers. They have to appear in the translation; their order may change.
– An empty or missing entry shows the English text – so a language can grow step by step, and new texts in the app never break anything.

en.heading: Adding a language
paragraphs: – Create the catalogue, e.g. for Italian:
``sh npm run i18n -- --add it ``
This creates locales/it.json with every text and empty translations.

– Translate – by hand or with a tool such as Weblate, Crowdin, POEditor or Lokalise (format “JSON key-value” or “i18next JSON”, source file locales/en.json). Machine translation (e.g. DeepL) works as a draft; please keep placeholders and HTML tags unchanged.
– Register the language: in lib/i18n.ts under LANGUAGES with its name and date format (it: { name: "Italiano", tag: "it-IT" }), and import the catalogue in lib/i18n-catalogs.ts.
– Check:
``sh npm run i18n -- --check # progress and wrong placeholders npm run i18n -- --check --missing # what is still missing, with the place in the code ``
The language then appears in the choice on the sign-in page and in the profile, and browsers in that language get it automatically.

en.heading: Keeping catalogues up to date
paragraphs: After texts change in the code, npm run i18n collects all texts again: new ones are added empty to every catalogue, unused ones drop out, existing translations stay. The tests only report missing translations; wrong placeholders make them fail.

In the code, texts are t("Deutsch", "English") in components, tr() outside of them and ct() for content the server creates. Tables of text pairs get a marker so npm run i18n finds them, e.g. // i18n-table: 1 for [German, English] pairs.

en.heading: Text recognition
paragraphs: Text recognition for scanned PDFs and images is separate: it reads German and English, and French with FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS=fra,eng (see Configuration).
Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI assistants to your Flowplan using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). They search, read and write with exactly your permissions, nothing more.
Besides the optional built-in AI, MCP connects the assistant you choose. It works with your pages, databases and tasks. It sees only what you can see in Flowplan.

en.heading: Set up
paragraphs: – Under Settings → API & AI assistants, create a personal API token for the assistant. Choose Read only if the assistant should only search and read. Choose Read and write if it should also create pages and records.
– Copy the address shown under AI assistants (MCP). It is your Flowplan address followed by /api/mcp, for example https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp.
– Enter both in your client (examples below). The settings page has a ready-made configuration for each client and fills in a token you have just created.
Use a separate token for each assistant. That way you can see when each one was last used, and you can revoke one without affecting the others.

en.heading: Claude Code
paragraphs: claude mcp add --transport http flowplan https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp \
--header "Authorization: Bearer fp_…"
With --scope user the connection is available in all your projects. In Claude Code, /mcp shows the connection and its tools.

en.heading: Claude Desktop
paragraphs: Claude Desktop connects to remote MCP servers that use a token through the small mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js. Open Settings → Developer → Edit config, add the following to claude_desktop_config.json, and restart Claude:
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${FLOWPLAN_AUTH}"],
"env": { "FLOWPLAN_AUTH": "Bearer fp_…" }
The token goes in env, not in args: that way it does not appear in the process list.

en.heading: ChatGPT
paragraphs: In ChatGPT, custom MCP connectors are available in developer mode, depending on your plan and workspace settings. Under Settings → Apps & Connectors, create a new connector with the address https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp. If ChatGPT offers token or API key authentication, enter fp_… there.

If your ChatGPT version only offers OAuth or "No authentication", ChatGPT cannot connect to Flowplan yet. Flowplan currently signs in only with personal tokens (see What is supported). Never put the token into the address as a workaround: addresses end up in logs.

en.heading: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and others
paragraphs: Clients that speak Streamable HTTP and accept their own headers use this configuration (the exact file depends on the client, e.g. .cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json):
"mcpServers": {
"flowplan": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://flowplan.example.com/api/mcp",
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer fp_…" }

en.heading: Tools
paragraphs: Tool What it does Token
list_workspaces Your workspaces with your role and the spaces you can see Read
list_pages Pages in a workspace, optionally in one space or below one page Read
search Full-text search across pages, records, comments and file contents Read
read_page A page as Markdown; databases with their records Read
query_database Records with properties by name, property definitions, views; text filter, a saved view, paging Read
get_record One record with all properties and its record document Read
my_tasks Your tasks from documents and records, with due dates Read
create_page New document, database or whiteboard; documents can start with Markdown content Write
append_to_page Appends Markdown to the end of a document Write
create_record New record; properties by name Write
update_record Changes individual properties of a record Write

Properties are named by their name (or ID). Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD, options by their name, people by e-mail address or name, and relations as a list of record IDs. update_record accepts the version from get_record: if someone changed the record in the meantime, the change is refused instead of being overwritten.
In addition, each page is available as a resource flowplan://page/ (your favourites are listed). There are two prompts: Summarize a page and Plan my day.

en.heading: Permissions
paragraphs: – Every call acts as the person who owns the token, with exactly their rights. The same checks apply as in the browser: workspace membership and guest access, private spaces, page and group permissions, private records, and journals locked with a PIN.
– Read tokens only offer read tools. A write call with a read token is refused.

– Write tools run the same actions as the interface. That means automatic versions, mentions and task notifications, followers, the activity log and webhooks all work as usual. Locked pages stay locked.
– Tokens never have administrator rights and cannot create or revoke tokens.
– The public demo has no MCP access: demo accounts cannot create tokens, and browser sessions are not accepted by /api/mcp.

en.heading: Security notes
paragraphs: – Treat the token like a password. Anyone who has it can read (and with a write token change) everything you can. Revoke a token under Settings → API & AI assistants if you no longer need it or it might have leaked; the connection stops immediately.

– AI assistants can be misled by content they read (prompt injection), for example by text on a page shared with you. Give an assistant a read token if it does not need to write. With a write token, use the client's confirmation prompts for tool calls.
– Answers can contain anything you can read in Flowplan. That content goes to the provider of your assistant, so check its privacy terms first.
– /api/mcp accepts only tokens, not the sign-in cookie, so another website cannot use your browser session. Requests from a foreign Origin are refused.
– Limits: 120 requests per minute per person, 2 MB per request, and answers are cut after 200,000 characters. Write tools have the same size limits as the interface.

en.heading: What is supported
paragraphs: – Transport: Streamable HTTP (POST /api/mcp, JSON answers, no session). Protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05.
– Sign-in: personal API tokens as Authorization: Bearer fp_…. OAuth sign-in (for clients that only support OAuth) is not available yet.
– Not included: deleting content, administration, files and uploads, whiteboard contents.

en.heading: Examples
paragraphs: – "Search Flowplan for the offer for Müller and summarize the open points."
– "Read the page Team meeting and add a section Decisions with today's results."
– "Show my overdue tasks and make a plan for today."
– "Create a record in the Bugs database: title Login on iPad hangs, status Open, assigned to anna@example.com."

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
paragraphs: Flowplan is an open-source alternative to Notion, Confluence and AppFlowy under the AGPL-3.0. This is how you bring over pages, databases, images and files from the tool you use now.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs and Obsidian
paragraphs: Under Settings → Import & export → Import choose the target space at the top and, at Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs or Obsidian, the source (or let it be detected) and whether you want a page tree or a new database. Then choose the file:

– Flowplan uploads the file (with a progress bar) and shows a preview: how many pages, folders, files (with their size) and tags will be imported, and what will not work – such as encrypted text, unsupported macros or images missing from the export.
– Import creates everything in one step. If something fails, nothing is left half imported.
For all sources:
– End-to-end encrypted spaces cannot be targets (the server sees no plaintext there).
– You need write access to the target space; the workspace's storage quota and your personal limit are checked first (the preview already warns).
– Limits per import: 100 MB, 500 pages (as a database: 5,000 records), 10 MB per file in the ZIP.
– The content is cleaned like when pasting: scripts, forms and embedded foreign pages are dropped. File names are cleaned; files a browser could run (HTML, SVG) are only stored for download.
– Links between imported pages point to the new pages. Images and attachments are uploaded – every file once, even if several pages show it.

– As a new database, every note becomes a record with the properties Tags, Created, Updated, Folder (the folder path) and – where present – Source. As pages, tags appear as #tag at the top of the page.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From Notion
paragraphs: – In Notion: Settings → Export (for the whole workspace) or Export in a page's … menu. Choose the format Markdown & CSV and turn on Include subpages.
– In Flowplan: Settings → Import & export → Import, choose the target space at the top and the ZIP at Notion, AppFlowy or Markdown export (ZIP).
– Done – the import runs in one step. If it fails, nothing is left half imported.
What it turns into:
– Every Markdown file becomes a page, every folder named like a page holds its sub-pages. The IDs Notion appends to file and folder names are dropped.
– Every CSV file becomes a database. When both versions are there, Flowplan takes Name_all.csv (all records) instead of the current view.
– Columns get a fitting type: numbers, checkboxes, dates (also in Notion's format "September 24, 2026") and selects with their options; the rest stays text.
– Record pages are matched to their records as their document.
– Images and files the pages refer to are uploaded.
– Large exports that Notion splits into several ZIP files inside the ZIP are recognised.
Limits per import: 100 MB, 500 pages and 5,000 records per table. Export larger workspaces in parts, for instance page by page.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From AppFlowy
paragraphs: – In AppFlowy, export pages as Markdown and databases as CSV.
– Put the files into one folder – sub-folders become sub-pages – and make a ZIP of it.
– Import it in Flowplan under Settings → Import & export → Import.
Markdown becomes pages, CSV becomes databases; linked images and files come along.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From Confluence
paragraphs: – In Confluence: Space settings → Export (Confluence Cloud: Space settings → Export space). Choose HTML or XML, each with all pages.
– Import the ZIP in Flowplan as above (source Confluence or automatic).
What it turns into:
– The space's page tree becomes the page tree in Flowplan (from index.html or the parent pages in entities.xml; where a page is missing there, the breadcrumbs help).
– Info, tip, note and warning macros become callouts (info → note, tip → tip, note → warning, warning → caution), code macros code blocks, expand toggles, task lists tasks with their status.
– Images and attachments are uploaded; attachments the text does not show are listed as links at the end of the page. Links to other pages of the space point to the imported pages.
– In the XML export only the current version of each page counts; older versions and blog posts are skipped. Creation and modification dates are kept.
– Macros without a counterpart (such as table of contents or Jira queries) are dropped; the preview names them.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From Evernote
paragraphs: – In Evernote, save a notebook via … → Export notebook as ENEX. Put several notebooks into one ZIP.
– Import the .enex file or the ZIP in Flowplan.
What it turns into:
– Every note becomes a page; with several notebooks, every notebook becomes a page with its notes below.
– The note text (ENML) becomes normal text with formatting, lists and tables; checkboxes become tasks.
– Images and attachments (embedded in the ENEX file) are uploaded and shown where they were in the text; PDFs and other files as links. Attachments without a place in the text go to the end.
– Tags, created/updated and the source address are kept – best import as a new database, then they are properties to filter and sort by.
– Encrypted text cannot be imported; the preview warns.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From Google Docs
paragraphs: – At takeout.google.com choose Drive and set the format for documents to HTML (recommended) or Microsoft Word. Single documents also work via File → Download → Web page (.html, zipped) or Microsoft Word (.docx).
– Import the Takeout ZIP, the web page ZIP or the .docx file in Flowplan (source Google Docs).
What it turns into:
– Every document becomes a page, Drive folders become parent pages.
– Headings, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, nested lists, tables and links come along; Google's redirect links point straight to their target again.
– Images are uploaded – including the ones embedded in the HTML.
– Word files: paragraphs, headings, lists (numbered and bulleted, also nested), tables (with merged columns), links and images. Comments, footnotes and headers/footers are dropped.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: From Obsidian and other Markdown folders
paragraphs: – A vault as pages: make a ZIP of the vault folder (with its .obsidian folder) and import it under Settings → Import & export → Import – via Confluence, Evernote, Google Docs or Obsidian with a preview, or via the Notion/Markdown import, which recognises a vault as well.
– Folders become pages with their notes below. A folder note (Projects/Projects.md or Projects.md next to the folder) becomes the folder's page itself.

– Wikilinks [[Page]], [[Page text]], [[Folder/Page]] and [[Page#Heading]] become links to the imported pages – resolved like Obsidian does, by path or file name. Links to notes that do not exist stay text.
– Embedded files ![[image.png]] become images, ![[file.pdf]] file links; embedded notes ![[Note]] become links.
– Callouts such as > [!note] or > [!warning] Title become callouts of the matching kind.

– Tags from the frontmatter (tags:) and in the text (#tag, not in code) are collected: on pages as #tag at the top, in a new database in the Tags property – together with Folder for where a note came from.
– Notes with frontmatter into an existing database: in a database choose Import CSV or Markdown and pick the .md files or a ZIP. The YAML properties become columns – see Frontmatter.

– Aliases: aliases: [PAC, Pompe à chaleur] (or alias:) in the frontmatter becomes the page's aliases or the record's Aliases property. @ mentions, search and unlinked mentions then also find "Chauffage" by "PAC", and the Markdown export writes them back as aliases:.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: After the move
paragraphs: – Check links: links between imported pages point to the new pages; links to pages outside the export still point to the old tool.
– Set up views: an import creates one table per database. Add board, calendar, gallery or timeline afterwards – see Views.
– Sharing: permissions are not carried over. Invite members or share single pages – see Sharing and publishing.
– Your data stays portable: Flowplan exports again at any time as Markdown with frontmatter, CSV and ZIP, scheduled and pushed to Git if you like – see Import, export and versions.

en.page: Moving from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Confluence, Evernote and Google Docs
en.heading: Why move?
paragraphs: – Completely open source: all of the source code is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 – with no closed enterprise edition and no features behind a licence.
– Your data, your server: hosted on flowplan.org in Germany or as one Docker container on your own server – see Installation.
– No tracking.

A notebook is a page of sheets to write on – with the Apple Pencil, another tablet pen, a mouse or a finger, like a paper notebook. The sheets sit one below the other and you scroll through them. Each sheet has its paper (lined, grid, dotted, Cornell, music staff …) or a page of a PDF as its background. There is also handwriting in documents: a drawing block in the middle of the text.

en.heading: Creating a notebook
paragraphs: New page → Notebook (or New notebook in the command palette). A new notebook starts with one sheet of lined A4 paper.

From a PDF: in the same dialog, choose a file under Open a PDF as the notebook. Every page of the PDF becomes a sheet with that page as its background – lecture slides, worksheets or forms are then written on as if printed. ⋯ → Import PDF … adds more PDF pages to an existing notebook, after the current sheet. Up to 500 pages per import and 1000 sheets per notebook.

en.heading: Paper
paragraphs: Template Looks like
Blank no lines
Lined (college) lines 7.1 mm apart (college ruled) with a margin
Lined (wide) lines 8.7 mm apart (wide ruled) with a margin
Grid (5 mm) squared paper
Dotted dots every 5 mm
Cornell notes title band, cue column on the left, summary at the bottom
Music staff 12 staves (8 in landscape)
Plus A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape, and light or dark. On dark paper, black ink shows light and the highlighter glows.
The lines icon in the toolbar (or Change paper … in a sheet's menu) opens the choice. Apply to:
– This sheet – only the current sheet gets its own paper;
– Notebook default – for all sheets without their own paper and for new sheets;
– All sheets – sets the default and removes every sheet's own paper.
Sheets from a PDF keep their PDF page and its size.

en.heading: Writing
paragraphs: Whoever may edit the page writes right away – there is no "Annotate" step as in the PDF viewer. At the top is the toolbar: Pen (with pressure), Highlighter, Eraser (whole strokes or partial), Lasso (move, resize, recolour, copy, duplicate, delete), Text and Laser pointer, three favourite pens, colours, widths and the pen settings. They work as when annotating PDFs: only the pen writes once you have used it, fingers scroll and zoom, a resting hand leaves no marks; holding still at the end of a stroke straightens it into a line, rectangle, ellipse …

Everything is saved as you write (on the right of the toolbar: Saved). Every change of a sheet is a version. When two people write on the same sheet at the same time, both keep their strokes; a notice says that someone wrote along. What others write appears after a few seconds.
Readers of the page see all sheets, zoom and export, but no tools.

en.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
paragraphs: Key Does
P H E L T K Pen, highlighter, eraser, lasso, text, laser pointer
⌘ Z / ⇧ ⌘ Z Undo / redo
⌘ C, ⌘ V, ⌘ D, Delete Copy, paste, duplicate, delete the selection
⌘ + / ⌘ − / ⌘ 0 Zoom in, zoom out, fit to width
⇧ ⌘ ↵ New sheet after the current one
⌥ ↓ / ⌥ ↑ Next / previous sheet
⌘ S Save now
On Windows and Linux use Ctrl instead of ⌘ and Alt instead of ⌥. On an iPad with a keyboard the same shortcuts apply.

en.heading: Page overview
paragraphs: The sidebar icon on the left of the toolbar shows all sheets as previews; a tap jumps to the sheet. With ⋯ on a preview: New sheet after, Duplicate (with everything on it), Change paper …, Move up, Move down and Delete. You also change the order by dragging a preview or with ⌥ ↑/↓ on the focused preview. + in the toolbar adds a sheet after the current sheet or at the end, as does Add sheet below the last sheet.

en.heading: Exporting as PDF
paragraphs: ⋯ → Export as PDF downloads the notebook as a PDF: one page per sheet in the sheet's size, paper and handwriting as vectors (sharp at any zoom), PDF sheets with their original page including its text. The Markdown export puts the notebook into the ZIP as a PDF as well and writes a short Markdown file with a link to it and the recognised text. The PDF, Word and EPUB exports show the sheets as pictures (Word: only their text). Published and shared notebooks are read-only.

en.heading: Handwriting in documents
paragraphs: Type /draw in a document (also /zeichnen, /dessin, /handwriting or /sketch): a drawing block across the full width appears. With a pen you write on it right away; with a mouse or finger after a tap into the block (or on Draw) – so a finger keeps scrolling the document. Then the toolbar appears with the block's paper (Blank, Lined, Grid) and Done. Drag the bottom edge to change the height (or use the arrow keys on the handle).

The handwriting belongs to the block and is saved as you draw. For working together this means: when several people draw in the same block at once, their strokes are merged instead of overwritten; the text around it you edit together as always. Copied or duplicated blocks (also into another document) take their drawing along and are independent afterwards. Permissions, locking and the trash work as for the document; on published pages, in share links and in exports the block shows as a picture.

en.heading: Recognising handwriting (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: In the Flowplan app for iPhone and iPad the device itself recognises what you write – the strokes do not leave the device for this:

– Search: shortly after saving, the handwriting of a sheet, a drawing block or a PDF page is recognised and its text saved along. Search then also finds notebooks, documents and PDFs by what is handwritten.

– Convert to text: select handwriting with the lasso and choose Convert to text (the Aa icon) in the selection's bar. In a notebook and on PDFs, typed text replaces the strokes in their place; in a drawing block the text becomes a paragraph below the block. Undo brings the strokes back.
In the browser and the desktop app there is no recognition; Convert to text does not appear there. Text typed on sheets, in drawing blocks and on PDFs is searchable everywhere.

en.heading: Limits
paragraphs: – Encrypted spaces have no notebooks and no drawing blocks.
– Locked pages show the handwriting; it can be changed after unlocking.
– A notebook's page versions only hold its appearance; each sheet has its own versions of the handwriting.
– Drawing blocks exist in documents and journal days, not in the documents of database records.
Flowplan runs in the browser, can be installed as an app and keeps working without a connection.

en.heading: Work without a connection
paragraphs: Flowplan always saves documents locally in the browser first (IndexedDB) and syncs them with the server as soon as it can be reached. If the connection drops, you simply keep writing; other people's changes are merged when you reconnect.

en.heading: Turn on offline use
paragraphs: Under Settings → Offline & devices, the device also stores the app, the workspace, all readable pages and the records and files you open later. Then you can open pages, read documents and databases and edit text even without a connection.
– Online, the current state always comes from the server; the copy only serves without a connection.
– If the sign-in has expired, Flowplan shows the sign-in page online – without a connection, the stored copy still opens.
– The copies contain private content. They are removed when you sign out, when you turn the feature off and when another person signs in.
The whole app on the device

The copy holds the whole app – not only the parts you already opened online. The editor, calendar, timeline and gallery views, dashboards, charts, whiteboards, notebooks, math, Mermaid diagrams and the PDF viewer then load without a connection as well.
– Storage: about 18 MB on the device (around 5 MB to download), once per version. Flowplan only stores the app's files when the device has enough space.

– New version: after an update, Flowplan loads the new version's files with the next refresh; files that did not change are taken over instead of downloaded again. As soon as the new version is stored completely, the old one is removed.
– Settings → Offline & devices shows a line like “The app is stored for offline use (version 0.7.0) · 18 MB” – or how many files are still missing.

– If a part is missing without a connection after all, Flowplan shows “Not available offline – try again when you're online” with Try again in its place; the rest of the app keeps working, and the part loads by itself once the connection is back. A record whose content is not in the copy shows “This record is not available offline.”
The copy stays current

While Flowplan is open, it keeps the copy up to date on its own: at start, when the connection comes back, when you bring the app back to the foreground, and every 6 hours. It only loads what changed since the last update – usually two small requests.
– New pages are added; changed pages, records and documents are loaded again.
– Deleted pages and pages you may no longer read (including a journal behind a PIN) leave the copy together with their records and files.
– When an update takes a moment, Updating offline copy … shows briefly in the bottom left corner.
– When the sign-in has expired, Flowplan does not update – the existing copy stays as it is.
Settings → Offline & devices shows the state, for example “Offline copy updated 2 h ago · 312 pages · 85 MB”. Update now loads every page again.

Also store record contents and files also stores the documents of all database records and the files of the pages, even ones you have never opened – at most 200 MB and only while the device has enough space. Without it, only records and files you opened once are kept. Turning it off removes the records and files stored in addition.
Without a connection, Flowplan shows the date of the copy below the offline notice when it is older than 7 days (“Offline copy from Oct 12”).

[!NOTE] Installed as an app (Chrome, Edge, Android), Flowplan also updates the copy in the background while the app is closed, when the browser allows it (Periodic Background Sync). The browser decides whether and how often – usually only for apps used often. Records and files never opened are loaded only by the open app.

en.heading: Database records offline
paragraphs: Changes to records without a connection appear in the views right away and are collected on the device. As soon as the connection is back, they go to the server one after another. If someone changed the same record in the meantime, Flowplan merges the changes field by field; if the same field was changed on both sides or the record was deleted, you decide in the conflict dialog.
[!NOTE] A database's schema – properties and views – can only be changed with a connection.

en.heading: Offline in the app for iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: The app for iPhone and iPad keeps the offline copy itself – for every instance, self-hosted ones included. (iOS gives apps no service worker for addresses of your choice; in Safari and in the Android app, Flowplan works offline as in the browser.)

– Turn it on as everywhere under Settings → Offline & devices – per profile of the app. It also says “Stored in the Flowplan app”; state, size, version, Update now, Also store record contents and files and Remove offline copies work as in the browser.

– Without a connection – at start or when the instance cannot be reached – the app opens the stored copy: the same page you were on, with the notice “Offline – you see the last saved state”. Pages, databases, records, calendars, dashboards and the editor run from the copy. The app shows its “No connection” screen only when there is no copy for the profile.

– Changes offline: text in documents and changes to records are collected on the device as in the browser and synced as soon as the instance answers again. Then the app switches to the current page by itself – once you are not typing.
– Kept current: as in the browser while the app is open, and also every time it comes to the foreground; only what changed is loaded.

– Where it is stored: in the app's container, encrypted until the first unlock after a restart and not in backups. The copy belongs to the profile: Sign out in Flowplan and Sign out and remove the profile in the app's settings delete it; another profile never sees it.

– Limits: files over 25 MB, the PDF viewer and text recognition (OCR) need a connection in the app; at most 2 GB per profile, and the app always leaves 300 MB free. The copy needs a Flowplan server with this offline support (0.7.0 or newer); with older servers the app shows its “No connection” screen without a connection, as before.

en.heading: Install as an app
paragraphs: – Chrome, Edge: the install icon in the address bar.
– Safari on the Mac: File → Add to Dock.
– iPhone, iPad: Share → Add to Home Screen. Only this way are push notifications possible there.
– Android: menu → Install app.
The installed app opens in its own window without browser bars.

en.heading: Share to Flowplan
paragraphs: When Flowplan is installed as an app on Android (Chrome), it appears in the Share menu of other apps. Shared text and links land in a preview; Save as page creates a page from it in the chosen space. Without being signed in, you first go to the sign-in and then back to the preview. iOS does not offer this menu to web apps.

The preview asks whether to save as a page, as a record in a database or – for links – as a bookmark. As a record, title, text and link (or the article text) go into the record; the link lands in the database's first URL property, otherwise in the text, and the database's default record template applies. If there is a default capture database (see below), as a record is preselected with it. Include article text loads the web page on the server and keeps its main text without navigation, ads and scripts (public addresses only).

en.heading: Web clipper in the browser
paragraphs: Under Settings → Web clipper you find the button Save to Flowplan. Dragged into the bookmarks bar, it opens a small window on any web page with the title, address and selected text – the same preview as when sharing. After saving, the window closes.

en.heading: Capture into a database
paragraphs: For an inbox, e.g. with PARA: Quick capture on the start page, ⌘ ⌥ N, > capture in the quick search or – with the installed app – a long press on the app icon → its capture shortcut open a small window with title and text. It is saved as a record in the chosen database; without a connection it waits on the device and is created once the connection is back.

Use as default for capturing (in the window) or Settings → Web clipper → Capture sets the database that share, the web clipper and quick capture preselect – per person and workspace. The database's default record template applies, so new records land e.g. straight in the "Inbox" view.

en.heading: Bookmarks
paragraphs: Bookmarks land in the Bookmarks database of the chosen space; it is created the first time, with link, website, folder, note, date and "read" as well as the views All, Cards and Unread. The article text that was taken along is in the record. Choose bookmarks file imports the HTML file that Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari create when exporting bookmarks – including folders and dates; links that already exist are skipped.

en.heading: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
paragraphs: A slim desktop app wraps your Flowplan instance. On first start it asks for the address and suggests https://app.flowplan.org – for your own instance enter its address instead (e.g. https://flowplan.example.com). More instances are added as profiles.
– All data stays on the server.

– The app remembers the window size and position and opens external links in the default browser. Right-click menu with spelling suggestions, quick capture from anywhere, an icon in the menu bar or notification area, pages in windows of their own and more: see More from the desktop app.

– Offline use works in the desktop app too: turn on Settings → Offline & devices in the app – it keeps its own offline copies, separate from the browser or the installed web app. Without a connection it then opens the stored copy; its own offline page (Try again, Profiles) only appears when there is no copy on the device.
– Notifications: the app shows new inbox notifications as system notifications and the unread count on the app icon – also with the window minimised or hidden. See Notifications in the desktop app.
– It only accepts real Flowplan instances – an address running something else or redirecting to another site is refused.

– Handoff (Mac): the page open in the window appears on your iPad and iPhone (same Apple Account, Handoff on) and opens there in the Flowplan app – or in the browser without the app. A page open in the iPad or iPhone app appears in the Mac's Dock and opens in the desktop app, in the profile of its instance. See iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff.

– Sign in with a passkey and Sign in with SSO open the sign-in in the default browser, where passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Windows Hello, password managers) are available. After Sign in to the app the app takes over the sign-in; e-mail and password work directly in the app. This needs Flowplan 0.3.3 or newer.

The apps for macOS, Windows and Linux are at flowplan.org/download – the page detects your system. Updates install themselves (macOS, Windows installer, Linux AppImage). The Mac app is signed and notarized; with 1.0.5 or older, download the current version once – after that it updates itself. Windows shows SmartScreen. More under Operations and troubleshooting.

[!NOTE] The environment variable FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_URL exists twice: on the computer running the desktop app it names another source for app updates (see Updates); on the server, the variable of the same name points the instance's release check at a mirror (see Configuration). They mean different things and belong in different places.

en.heading: Several instances (profiles)
paragraphs: If you work with more than one Flowplan instance, say Work – flowplan.company.com and Private – notes.example, the desktop app keeps each one as a profile:
– Add: menu Profiles → Add Profile…, enter the address and, if you like, a name (without one the app shows the address). The address is checked as on first start.

– Switch: in the Profiles menu (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu), with Next Profile (⌘ ⇧ P or Ctrl Shift P), from the Dock icon on the Mac and from the taskbar jump list on Windows.

– Rename and remove: Profiles → Manage Profiles… (also reachable from the offline page). Removing asks first, signs the profile out and deletes what it stored on this computer. Your data stays on the server.

Every profile has its own sign-in, its own offline copy and its own cookies – also two profiles on the same instance, for example for two accounts. Only the active profile's instance opens in the window; links to another instance go to the browser. With more than one profile, the window title names the active one.
If you had set up an address before, it becomes the first profile after the update – still signed in and with its offline copy.

en.heading: Notifications in the desktop app
paragraphs: Browsers receive notifications through Web Push, which the desktop app does not have. It therefore asks your instance itself, about once a minute while it runs:

– What appears: each new unread notification once, with the inbox line as title and the record below it (with several profiles also the profile name). Your notification kinds under Settings → Notifications apply: only kinds with push switched on pop up. More than three at once become one notification that opens the inbox.
– Click: brings the window to the front, switches to the right profile if needed and opens the page.
– Count on the icon: the unread notifications – on the Dock (macOS), in the launcher (Linux, where the desktop shows counts) and as a red dot on the taskbar button (Windows).

– Settings: in the Notifications menu (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu): Show Notifications, Do Not Disturb for an hour or until tomorrow morning, and All Profiles (otherwise only the active profile). In the app, Settings → Notifications shows the same switch instead of Web Push.
Nothing pops up for the window in front – its inbox is in view anyway. What was there at the first start is not shown again, not even after a restart.

On a Mac the app keeps running in the Dock after closing the window and keeps notifying. On Windows and Linux closing the window quits the app; notifications arrive while it runs (minimised is enough) – or, with the notification area icon, also without a window.
This needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer and desktop app 1.0.7 or newer. The app only asks the profile's own instance, with its sign-in; nothing is stored on the server for it.

en.heading: More from the desktop app
paragraphs: From desktop app 1.1.0 there is more around the window. Its switches are under Settings… (macOS: in the Flowplan menu, Windows and Linux: in the File menu).

– Right-click and spelling: a right click in fields, on links and images shows a system menu – suggestions for a misspelled word, Add to Dictionary, cut, copy, paste, Paste as Plain Text, open a link in the browser or in a new window, copy or save an image, Look Up on a Mac. In the editor Flowplan's own text menu stays; the app's suggestions appear at its top (needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer). Choose the spell checker's languages – German, English, French – under Spelling in the right-click menu, in the Edit menu or in the settings.

– Quick capture from anywhere: Ctrl Shift Space (Mac: ⇧ ⌘ Space) opens a small window above every app – into the inbox, a database, today's journal entry or a page, with shorthand like tomorrow 3pm #client @anna !high, links from the clipboard, files, screen regions and voice notes, Undo and Recently captured, quick actions with shortcuts of their own and an optional AI suggestion. Offline, the capture waits encrypted in a queue and is sent later without arriving twice. Everything about it: Quick capture (desktop).

– Icon in the menu bar (Mac) or notification area (Windows, Linux): Quick Capture, the tasks due today or overdue from My tasks, the unread notifications, open Flowplan, the profiles and quit. On by default on a Mac, switched on in the settings on Windows and Linux; the app then keeps running in the notification area after its window is closed.

– Open pages from links: links like flowplan://open?instance=…&page=… open the page in the app, in the profile of its instance. In a browser on a computer, a page's actions (… at the top right) offer Open in desktop app. For an instance without a profile the app asks first whether to add it.

– Pages in windows of their own: Open Page in New Window (⌘ ⇧ N or Ctrl Shift N), a Shift- or middle-click on a link, or Open in new window in a page's menu. The app remembers these windows with their size and place and opens them again on the next start.

– Drop files: drop PDFs, images, Markdown and text files on the Dock icon, open them with Open With → Flowplan, or drop them on the window where Flowplan does not take them itself. The app asks where to: Into the Inbox (one record per file) or As New Pages (Markdown becomes a real page). Images and PDFs up to 50 MB, text up to 5 MB, at most 10 files at once.
– Open at login: in the settings, optionally Start without a window.
– Print and PDF: Print… shows a preview and prints through the system's dialog, Save as PDF… saves the page as a PDF – both without sidebar and tools, as when printing from the browser.

– Updates without interruptions: a new update downloads in the background; a small notice at the bottom of the window shows progress, size and speed, and the progress also shows on the app icon. Once it is ready the notice (and the menu) offer Restart; otherwise it installs when you quit. No dialog interrupts your typing.

en.heading: Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
paragraphs: [!NOTE] As of today the apps are in preparation and not yet available in the App Store or on Google Play. Until then, Flowplan can be installed as a web app as described above.
Requirements: iPhone and iPad with iOS/iPadOS 16.4 or later (the share sheet and the configurable widgets from iOS 17), Android 8.0 or later.
Like the desktop app, the mobile apps show your Flowplan instance; all data stays on the server and new features arrive without an app update. On top comes what only an app can do:

– Notifications: mentions, comments, tasks and reminders arrive as notifications, the number of unread ones shows on the app icon. The app asks for permission once after the first sign-in; a tap opens the page concerned. Which kinds arrive is set as in the browser under Settings → Notifications; there, Send test notification checks whether notifications reach all your devices and otherwise says why (more). Buttons tick off a task, postpone it to tomorrow, answer a comment or mark it read – without opening the app.

– Widgets for the home screen (on the iPhone also for the lock screen), each with settings of its own – tasks to check off, appointments, counters, time tracking and more; plus widgets for administrators.
– Live Activities: the timer, focus, the meeting, imports/exports and voice memos on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, or as an ongoing notification.
– Capture, Siri, Control Center: notes, tasks, voice memos and photos from widgets, Siri, Control Center, the app icon and Android tiles; ask Siri what is due, open a page or search.
– Focus filters (iPhone, iPad): one profile or workspace per Focus, optionally without notifications from the others.
– Share from other apps: text, links, photos and PDFs from any app straight into the inbox, a database or onto a page.
– Scanner and Spotlight (iPhone, iPad): documents scanned into searchable PDFs, your pages and tasks in the phone's search.
– Voice notes in pages are recorded by the app; on the iPhone and iPad they become text on the device itself.
– On-device AI (iPhone, iPad, optional): writing assistant and summaries with Apple Intelligence without the text leaving the device; Apple's Writing Tools in the editor.
– Calendars in Apple Calendar with one configuration profile instead of typing CalDAV credentials.
– App lock: if you like, Flowplan only unlocks with Face ID, Touch ID, a fingerprint or the device code.

– Back: swiping from the left edge (iOS) or the back gesture or button (Android) first closes what is open (menu, dialog, sidebar) and then goes up a level: from a settings section to the overview, from a record to its database, from a page to the previous page.
– Exports and downloads go to the system's share menu (e.g. "Save to Files").
– Without a connection: the app opens the profile's offline copy, on iPhone and iPad too – see Offline in the app for iPhone and iPad.

– iPad and tablets: every orientation, Split View, Slide Over and Stage Manager, several windows, a hardware keyboard with the shortcuts listed when you hold ⌘, the trackpad, and Handoff to the Mac – see iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff. With the Apple Pencil you write in notebooks and drawing blocks, draw on whiteboards and write on PDFs (see Annotate PDFs) with pressure while fingers move the board and a resting hand leaves no marks; double-tap and squeeze switch the tool, Scribble writes into any text field (see Whiteboards). The app recognises your handwriting on the device: search finds it, and Convert to text turns selected strokes into text (see Recognising handwriting).

– iPhone Duo: open or close it while you work – the page stays as it is (no reload, the same place, the text you are typing) and lays itself out anew: the phone layout with the bottom bar on the closed display and on the open one held upright, the sidebar on the open display held sideways. Content stays clear of the status bar and camera at the side of the closed display. On the open display you can use several windows as on the iPad (see below); the closed display has one. Full screen on iPhone Duo needs an app built for iOS 27.1 or later.
Also:

– On first start they ask for the address and suggest https://app.flowplan.org. They only accept real Flowplan instances that do not redirect to another site. More instances are saved as profiles. Sign out and remove the profile in the app settings (via Settings → Notifications → Open app settings) signs the app out of the active profile's instance and removes it there.

– Managed devices (MDM/EMM): through managed app configuration (iOS Managed App Configuration or Android app restrictions), the key server presets the address of your own instance; the app suggests it on first start.

– Sign in with a passkey and Sign in with SSO open the system's sign-in sheet (iOS) or a browser tab (Android); after Sign in to the app the app takes over the sign-in. E-mail and password work directly in the app. Signing in through the browser as well as notifications and widgets (the app interface) need Flowplan 0.4.0 or newer.
– Links to other sites open in the browser; without a connection the app shows a page of its own and reconnects by itself.
– Flowplan appears in other apps' Share menu – as Flowplan on iPhone and iPad, as Save to Flowplan on Android, see Share from other apps.

en.heading: Buttons on notifications
paragraphs: Long-press a notification (or pull it down) for its buttons. They do their work in the background; the app does not open.
Notification Buttons
A task is due (a task assigned to you is due today, a date reminder of a record) Done ticks it off; Tomorrow moves its date to tomorrow – the time of day stays, a date further ahead moves one day on
Comment, reply, mention in a comment Reply – type the answer right in the notification; it goes into the thread (or comments on the page) under your name. Mark as read
Everything else Mark as read
– Each button also marks the notification as read; the number on the app icon follows.
– Done, Tomorrow and Reply need the phone unlocked; Mark as read works on the lock screen.

– Done on a record uses the database's “done” state (a status option such as Done, or a checkbox Done); databases without one only offer Mark as read. If the task changed meanwhile, nothing is ticked off – a notification says so, and a tap opens the page.
– Your rights apply as in the browser, and the change shows in the activity, versions and automations like any other.

– Done, Tomorrow and Reply only appear when the notification brings its text along – without it, nobody could tell which task a button acts on. Through the push relay that is the default, because the text is end-to-end encrypted (operators can turn it off with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=off); older app versions through Expo only get it with MOBILE_PUSH_CONTENT=on. Otherwise there is Mark as read only.

Reminders without push: if your instance does not send push notifications to the app (switched off by the operators, or a test build without push), the app reminds you of your tasks itself – at 09:00 on the day a task is due, as long as notifications are allowed for Flowplan. It uses the tasks the app knows from its summary (the next eight).

en.heading: Widgets
paragraphs: Each widget shows one thing and has settings of its own. A widget you just added works right away with sensible defaults; small sizes show less. A tap opens the task or page in the app.
– Change the settings: iPhone/iPad (iOS 17 or later): long-press the widget → Edit Widget. Android: long-press the widget → Settings (you can skip this step when adding it).
– The lists to choose from (databases, views, properties, calendars, forms …) come straight from your Flowplan instance.
Widget What it shows Settings
Quick capture Buttons for note, task, voice memo, photo Where to save (default: your capture inbox), which buttons
Tasks Open tasks – check them off right in the widget My tasks, records of a database (with view) or to-dos of a page; all open, due today or overdue; number
Today Appointments and tasks due Calendars, range (today, 3 days, week), tasks due on/off
Page and favorites Your favorites, or one page / database view Page, view, up to two properties
Database counter One number (count, sum, average) with its last 14 days Database, view, value, group, history
Journal and habits Whether today is written, your streak; habits to check off Journal, habit database
Time this week Hours this week and today; start/stop the timer Which timer "Start" starts
Mentions Who mentioned you or gave you a task; mark as read Mentions and/or new tasks, unread only
Form responses New responses to a form Form
Flowplan Tasks due at a glance With or without the inbox, running timer on/off
Flowplan Inbox Number of unread notifications –
Flowplan Instance, Live, Storage Administrators only: state, one live number, storage What to show or which metric
Good to know:
– Counter history: Flowplan keeps the value of every day. Days before the widget was set up are estimated and drawn lighter and dashed.
– Privacy: widgets only show what you may see in Flowplan. Pages behind a journal PIN or end-to-end encrypted only show their state in a widget, never content.
– Signed out? When your session ends (e.g. a short SSO session), every widget shows Open Flowplan to sign in. Its settings stay; after signing in, the widgets fill again at once.
– Profiles: widgets belong to the active profile. Switching removes what the previous profile showed; on Android every widget keeps its settings per profile.

– Colours on Android: from Android 12 all widgets take the system colours (Material You, from the wallpaper or the chosen theme), light and dark. Red, amber and green keep their meaning. After a new wallpaper the widgets follow with their next update.
– Check off today's tasks: add the Tasks widget and choose Due today in its settings.
– Updates: when you change something in Flowplan, when the app comes to the foreground, and in the background about every 30 minutes (iOS decides how often).

– Requirements: the configurable widgets, the Live Activities other than the timer, and Siri and Shortcuts need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. Flowplan, Flowplan Inbox and the running timer work from 0.4.0.

en.heading: Widgets for administrators
paragraphs: People who administer the instance (members of the admin group, OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP, default flowplan-admins) get three more widgets in the app for iPhone, iPad and Android. Each shows one thing big; on the iPhone you choose which in the widget's settings.
Widget Sizes (iOS) Setting (default first) Tapping opens

Flowplan Instance small, medium, lock screen Show: state (All fine, notices or problems with the most important one), last backup, or version with available update Administration (Monitoring when there are notices or problems)

Flowplan Live small, medium, large, lock screen Metric: active now, requests/min, error rate (1 h) or sign-ins today; from medium up the other numbers small and the requests of the last 24 hours as a chart Administration → Monitoring
Flowplan Storage small, medium, lock screen (ring) Metric: disk used, database and files, or fullest workspace (quota) Administration → Storage
– Everyone else sees Administrators only in these widgets; without a sign-in they say Open Flowplan to sign in.

– Like the other widgets they read their data with the app's device token (GET /api/mobile/admin-summary). The instance checks on every call that the person of the session the device is bound to is an administrator right now – leaving the admin group, signing out or removing the device under Signed-in devices stops it. API tokens never get this data.
– Only numbers and states are sent – no names, e-mail addresses or workspace names.
– With the statistics switched off (FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off or in the administration under Monitoring → Statistics), Flowplan Live says "Statistics switched off"; state and storage stay.
– Older instances without this endpoint show Administrators only.

en.heading: Live Activities and ongoing notifications
paragraphs: On iPhone what is running appears on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, on Android as a notification (a Live Update on Android 16):
What runs Shows Button
Timer a running clock –
Focus e.g. 25 minutes of focus, then the break End
Meeting now the time left Open notes – creates the meeting note in your journal if there is none yet
Imports and exports their progress –
Voice memo recording Stop recording
Incident of the instance administrators only, only while it lasts –
Meetings, imports/exports and incidents can be switched off in the app settings under Live Activities; the timer, focus and voice memos always appear while they run.

If you start or stop the timer or focus elsewhere – in the browser, on another device – or focus moves on to the break, the instance updates the Live Activity on the iPhone by push through the push relay, even when the app is not open. By default this push holds only times and the phase; the Live Activity already knows the title and link from when it started on the device.

en.heading: Capture, Siri, Control Center
paragraphs: Every way leads to the app's capture screen: type a note or task, record a voice memo (keeps recording with the screen locked; transcribed when your instance can) or take/choose a photo.
Way What it offers
Quick capture widget Note, task, voice memo, photo – into the place chosen in the widget

Siri and Shortcuts (English, German, French) "Add a note to Flowplan" (into your capture inbox), "Add a task to Flowplan", "What's on today in Flowplan", "What's due today in Flowplan", "Open a page in Flowplan", "Search Flowplan", "Start the timer in Flowplan", "Stop the timer in Flowplan", "Record a voice memo in Flowplan", "Start focus in Flowplan"
Control Center and the Action button (iOS 18) New note, Quick capture, Today's tasks (shows how many are due), Voice memo, Start focus, Timer (a switch)
Long-press the app icon (iPhone, iPad) Inbox, My tasks, Search, New note, Switch profile. The iPhone shows the first four of them, Switch profile when signed out.

Long-press the app icon (Android) New note and Quick capture (always there, even before the first sign-in), then the pages you opened last, Inbox, My tasks, Search, Voice memo and Switch profile. Most launchers show four of them; every shortcut can be dragged to the home screen. Shortcuts to pages of another profile are greyed out until that profile is active again.

Android Quick Settings "New note" and "Quick capture" tiles (also from the lock screen). From Android 13, App settings → Widgets → Add “Quick capture” to Quick Settings adds the tile with one tap; otherwise use the pencil of Quick Settings.

Quick capture (tile and shortcut on Android) opens a compact window: choose where it goes – the inbox (your default capture database, see Capture into a database) or another page or database, with search –, type title and text, take or choose photos if you like, Save.
What Siri does without opening the app:

– Add a task: Siri asks for the task; in the Shortcuts app you can also set a due date and the list or database it goes to (otherwise your capture default). In a database the due date goes into its first date property.
– What's due today: Siri reads out how many tasks are due today and overdue and the first three, and shows the list.

– Search Flowplan: searches pages, records and comments in all your workspaces and shows the best hits; in a shortcut, the hits can be passed on (e.g. to Open a page). The action Search in the app opens Flowplan's own search with the text instead.
– Open a page: Siri asks which page – say part of its title – and opens it in the app. In Shortcuts you pick the page from a list.

Siri, Shortcuts and the controls use the active profile. Pages of end-to-end encrypted spaces do not appear (not even their titles). Adding tasks, what's due, opening pages, searching, the new controls and focus filters need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer.

en.heading: Focus filters
paragraphs: On the iPhone and iPad, a Focus (Settings → Focus → e.g. Work → Add filter → Flowplan) can choose:

– Profile or workspace: a profile ("all workspaces") or one workspace of a profile. When the Focus starts, the app switches to that profile and opens the workspace; when it ends, it goes back to the profile you had before – unless you switched yourself in the meantime.

– Hide notifications from other workspaces: while the Focus is on, your instance does not send this phone push notifications from other workspaces – or none at all if the Focus belongs to another profile. They still arrive in the inbox. If the Focus is never switched off, the rule ends by itself after a day.
Workspaces appear in the list once the app has been signed in to that profile; open the app on the profile once if one is missing.

en.heading: Share from other apps
paragraphs: In any app that can share (browser, Photos or gallery, Files, mail, scanner …), Share → Flowplan (iPhone, iPad) or Share → Save to Flowplan (Android) opens a small window with title, text, link and files.
– What works: text, links, photos and PDFs – several files at once too (at most 10). Other file types are not taken.

– Where to: the inbox, your default capture database, is preselected (set it in the browser with Use as default for capturing, see Capture into a database). Save to (iPhone, iPad) or Change (Android) lists every page and database you may write to, with search.

– What you get: in a database (the inbox included) a record – the link in the first URL property (if there is one), the files in the first files property and in the record itself. On a page a sub page with text, link, photos and PDFs.

On iPhone and iPad you stay in the app you share from. Flowplan remembers the last choice of where to save per profile. The sheet uses the sign-in of the app: open Flowplan once and sign in, otherwise it asks you to. Photos in HEIC become JPEG.

On Android the window lists under Not taken what it cannot take (other file types, more than 10 files). PDFs get a preview of their first page in the record. You can change the title; left empty it is the first line of the text, the link's address or the first file name. After Save, Back to the app returns to the app you shared from; Open shows the result in Flowplan. Not signed in yet? Text and links then go to the instance's preview as in the browser and continue after signing in.
The share sheet on iPhone and iPad as well as photos and PDFs on Android need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. Up to 0.6.0, Android takes only text and links, through the instance's preview.

en.heading: Scan documents and Spotlight (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: Scan documents. In a page, type / and choose Scan document (only in the iPhone and iPad app). The camera finds the edges and straightens each page; take as many pages as you like. Flowplan recognises the text on the device (German, English, French) and adds one PDF at the end of the page – or of the record you are in. The PDF carries the text invisibly, so you can select and search it in any PDF viewer, and Flowplan's search finds the scan by its text right away. The link flowplan://scan (e.g. in a shortcut) opens the scanner with the choice of inbox, page or database. The PDF does not stay on the phone after saving.

Spotlight. The app puts the titles of your most recently changed pages (up to 500, with where they are and a line of their content) and your open tasks into the phone's search. A tap on a result opens it in Flowplan. Nothing of end-to-end encrypted spaces, pages behind a journal PIN or journal days goes there; signing out or switching profiles empties it. The index stays on the phone.
The scanner and Spotlight need a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer.

en.heading: Voice notes in pages
paragraphs: In the app, Voice note (/voice) in a document records with the phone's microphone – up to 30 minutes, also with the screen locked. Insert puts the recording into the page as audio:

– Insert as text (iPhone and iPad): the spoken words become text on the device with Apple's speech recognition – the recording does not leave the phone for it. The text follows below the audio as a Transcript with timestamps. The app asks once for permission to use speech recognition. It works for the languages the device can recognise by itself (set by the device's language; most major languages, depending on the iOS version).
– Where the device cannot (Android, other languages), your instance's speech recognition turns it into text if it is set up (Voice notes); otherwise the audio stays on its own.
– Then summarise with AI puts a summary below the text when the AI is available to you.
This needs a Flowplan server 0.7.0 or newer. In the browser, /voice records as before.

en.heading: On-device AI and Writing Tools (iPhone and iPad)
paragraphs: Optional: on an iPhone or iPad with iOS/iPadOS 26 or later that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence switched on (Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri), the writing assistant and the summary of open pages run with Apple's language model on the device. The text does not leave the device, also in encrypted spaces; the instance needs no AI provider for it. Results carry the label On this device. This needs a Flowplan server newer than 0.7.0 (currently the beta image).

– Switch it off: Settings → AI → On this device (Apple) → Off – Flowplan then never asks the device. It also shows whether Apple Intelligence on this device is available, turned off in Settings or not supported. Administrators can switch it off for the whole instance.
– Server AI stays: questions to the workspace, AI in databases and AI actions keep running through the instance when it is set up; it also takes over texts that are too long.
– Older devices and iOS versions (from iOS 16.4) use the app as before, just without this path.
– Writing Tools: Apple's Writing Tools (proofread, rewrite, summarise) work right in the editor – select text and choose Writing Tools in the text menu (from iOS 18 with Apple Intelligence).
More: on-device AI.

en.heading: Calendars in Apple Calendar
paragraphs: Settings → Calendars & issues → Calendars on iPhone, iPad and Mac: choose calendar views and tap Set up in Apple Calendar. The app opens a configuration profile in Safari; confirm the download, then install it under Settings → Profile Downloaded (on the Mac: System Settings → Profiles). Each view becomes a CalDAV account in Apple Calendar, in both directions – see Sync both ways. On a computer the page shows a QR code instead; scan it with the iPhone's camera. The link works once and for ten minutes.

en.heading: iPad: windows, keyboard and Handoff
paragraphs: – Several windows: in a page's menu (right-click or long-press it in the sidebar), Open in new window gives the page a window of its own – side by side in Split View, in Slide Over or in Stage Manager. On iPhone Duo this works on the open display; on the closed one the menu item is not there. Links that would open a new tab do the same. Long-press the app icon → Show All Windows lists them. The first window holds the app settings, notifications and widgets; the others show a page and come back with it after a restart. All windows use the active profile and the app lock.

– Hardware keyboard: hold ⌘ and the iPad lists Flowplan's shortcuts – search ⌘ K, new page ⌘ N, quick capture ⌘ ⌥ N, the overview ⌘ / and the others with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, including your own. A shortcut works in the window in front. The editor's shortcuts (bold, undo …) work as in the browser.
– Trackpad and mouse: the pointer hovers over buttons and links as in Safari.

– Handoff: the page in front is offered to your Mac and your other devices (same Apple Account, Handoff on under Settings → General → AirPlay & Continuity). On the Mac it opens in the desktop app, without it in the browser. Pages from the Mac or another device open in the app on the profile of their instance; pages of an instance without a profile open in Safari. Pages behind the app lock are not offered while it is locked.

en.heading: Profiles in the mobile apps
paragraphs: The apps for iPhone, iPad and Android also keep several instances as profiles:
– Switch: tap a profile under Profiles in the app settings, or long-press the app icon → Switch profile (on the iPhone while signed out). The same list is a tap away from the offline page.
– Add: App settings → Add profile, enter the address and, if you like, a name. If the address already has a profile, the app simply switches to it – there is one profile per instance.
– Rename: tap Rename next to a profile in the app settings.
– Remove: Sign out and remove the profile applies to the active profile; the next profile then becomes active.

Notifications, widgets, Live Activities, the number on the app icon and the running timer always belong to the active profile. On a switch the app unregisters the device from the previous instance's notifications; the sign-in there stays, so you are still signed in when you switch back. What the app keeps for a profile (the device token for widgets, the last summary) is stored separately in the keychain or Keystore and never goes to another instance. An address set up before becomes the first profile after the update.

en.heading: What the app keeps on the instance
paragraphs: After signing in, the app registers with the instance: the entry belongs to that sign-in; signing in again on the device moves it to the new session. It disappears with signing out, removing it under Signed-in devices or deleting the account. With its device token, widgets, Live Activities and Shortcuts read in the background only what you may see in Flowplan – in small answers of at most ten items per widget – and run their buttons (check off a task or habit, start/stop the timer, mark as read, save what you captured) – as do the buttons on notifications, which name only the notification: what they act on comes from the instance. The share sheet and the scanner save with it as well, and Spotlight reads your page titles and open tasks with it. For notifications the app leaves a token of the push relay (the instance stores it only encrypted) and a public key; the private key stays in the Keychain or Keystore. Notifications thus arrive end-to-end encrypted: the relay, Apple and Google do not see their content, only the app decrypts it. Older app versions get them through Expo's push service – there, as with Web Push, they only say that something new is in the inbox. Operators can turn notifications off or send their text through Expo as well, see Configuration. A focus filter that hides notifications leaves a rule for this device there: which workspace may still notify it, for at most a day.

en.heading: Light and dark
paragraphs: Flowplan follows your device's light or dark mode by itself – also when it changes while Flowplan is open (for example automatically in the evening). Under Settings → Appearance & language → Appearance you choose a fixed Light or Dark instead; Automatic follows the device again. The choice applies per device. Sign-in, public pages and forms, the website and this documentation follow the device as well, the apps also with their own screens and widgets.
Health check, metrics, the storage overview and the most common causes when something does not run.

en.heading: Health check
paragraphs: GET /api/health answers without sign-in with 200, or with 503 when there are problems, and tells nothing about the instance:
{"service":"flowplan","status":"ok"}

With 503 it says "status":"error". Docker/Podman health checks, Kubernetes probes, Coolify, Gatus and uptime monitors only need the status code; the desktop and mobile apps recognise a Flowplan instance by "service":"flowplan".
The details come only with the token from FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN (Authorization: Bearer , as for /api/metrics) or for signed-in instance administrators:
– checks.database: database reachable and writable,
– checks.storage: upload directory writable,
– searchBacklog: search index backlog,
– failedPushDeliveries: failed push deliveries,
– objectStorage: with S3 pending (files still to upload) and retrying, otherwise "off",
– uptimeSeconds: the server's uptime.
– version, commit, builtAt: which version from which commit runs here (empty when the image doesn't carry them) – for example to check whether a deployment is current.
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN" https://flowplan.example.com/api/health
Personal API tokens do not unlock the details.

en.heading: Administration → Monitoring
paragraphs: Administration → Monitoring shows the instance live – refreshed every 15 seconds, paused while the tab is in the background:

– Health: database, file storage (with disk usage), S3 mirror, backup, e-mail, AI provider (reachable and response time, checked at most every five minutes), push relay (reachable, checked at most every minute, see Push notifications), background workers and update. Each tile leads to the section in charge.
– Key figures: active now, requests per minute (with error rate and p95 response time), sign-ins today, storage with its change over 7 days.

– Charts: Requests & errors (5xx) – 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days –, Active people per hour (7 days), Sign-ins successful and failed per day (14 days), Refused requests, Storage by kind and the largest workspaces, Deliveries (webhooks, push, e-mail) per day and AI usage (tokens per day and per feature). Every chart shows its values on hover, tap or with the arrow keys and has As a table.
– Queues: what is waiting to be processed right now – search index, mail queue, push delivery, AI fields and AI search index, S3 upload, webhooks retrying.
– Events: errors, warnings and notes of the last 14 days, filterable.
– Quick actions: Back up now, Check AI provider, Check alerts, Test alert, the way to Maintenance & notices and the activity log as CSV.
– Below: Background workers, Instance in numbers (size of the database and uploads, versions, uptime, demos …), Alerts by webhook and Statistics.
In detail:

– Refused requests: failed sign-ins, requests a limit refused with 429 (sign-in attempts, invitations, AI, MCP, forms …) and anonymous uploads over the daily budget (forms, share links) – per day over the last 14 days. A rise points to attacks or limits that are too tight. The counters are kept for 35 days and cleaned up daily.
– Background workers: last run and last error of backup, Markdown export, AI background work, calendar and issue sync and LDAP sync; “off” means not set up.

– Storage: usage by kind and the largest workspaces with bars against the quota (yellow from 80 %, red from 95 %). Quotas are set under Administration → Workspaces and Administration → Limits & retention.

– Deliveries: delivered webhooks, push messages and e-mails per day; what is waiting, given up and the latest errors are under Queues. Only the host of a webhook address is shown, never its path or token.

en.heading: Statistics
paragraphs: For the charts, Flowplan counts requests, errors and response times per minute, active people per hour, storage per day and AI tokens per feature – numbers only, without IP addresses, paths, user agents or names. Who was active is held in memory for the running hour only, so that each person counts once. Successful sign-ins are counted with their time (without the person). AI tokens come from the provider where it reports them, otherwise they are estimated (four characters per token).
Resolution Kept for
Minutes 48 hours
Hours 35 days
Days (storage, AI tokens) 400 days

Switch the statistics off under Administration → Monitoring → Statistics (Collect usage statistics) or for the whole instance with FLOWPLAN_METRICS=off (see Configuration); the switch is then locked. Delete statistics removes all counted requests, active people, storage history, AI tokens and successful sign-ins; the counters of refused requests stay.

en.heading: Alerts by webhook
paragraphs: Under Administration → Monitoring → Alerts by webhook, enter an https:// address (with FLOWPLAN_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true also http:// and internal addresses) and choose the events:
Event When
Backup failed The last scheduled backup ended with an error.
Storage > 90 % A workspace with a quota is more than 90 % full.
Worker error A worker that is set up reported an error in the last 24 hours.
Many failed sign-ins 50 or more failed sign-ins within an hour.
Flowplan checks every ten minutes and sends at most one message per event and day as a POST with JSON:
{ "event": "ops.storage_high", "title": "Speicher > 90 %", "detail": "Agency: 93 %", "instance": "Flowplan", "url": "https://flowplan.example.org", "at": "2026-10-22T08:10:00.000Z" }
The title is in German, as alerts are sent outside of a request; match on event.

The header X-Flowplan-Signature: sha256= is made with the signing secret shown, X-Flowplan-Event names the event. Send test sends ops.test right away, Check now checks out of turn, New secret creates a new signing secret. The latest alerts sent are listed below with their status code. An empty address turns alerts off.

en.heading: Maintenance & notices
paragraphs: Administration → Maintenance & notices holds two banners. The notice for everyone – e.g. “The new filing applies from Monday” – stays until you clear the field. A maintenance notice with text, start and end appears to everyone signed in as a banner at the top of the window from saving on – before the start as “Scheduled maintenance”, during it as “Maintenance in progress”, in each person's time zone and language. After the end it disappears by itself, also in windows already open (they check every five minutes). Everyone can hide the notice for themselves. Remove notice withdraws it at once. Saving and removing are in the activity log.

en.heading: Storage overview
paragraphs: Administration → Storage & backup shows in the cards Backups, Usage and Content:
– whether the S3 storage is reachable, how long the check took and how many files are still waiting,
– what is local and what is in the bucket: files by kind (images, videos, documents …) and how the database is split,
– how many workspaces, pages, databases, records, whiteboards, files, accounts and comments there are.

en.heading: Prometheus
paragraphs: With FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN (at least 16 characters), /api/metrics delivers metrics: sizes, queues, search backlog, storage and quota per workspace, flowplan_object_storage_pending and flowplan_build_info with version and commit.
scrape_configs:
- job_name: flowplan
metrics_path: /api/metrics
authorization:
credentials: <FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN>
static_configs:
- targets: ["flowplan:3000"]
Without a token the endpoint is switched off. The same token unlocks the details of /api/health (see above).

en.heading: Check after the first start
paragraphs: – /api/health returns 200.
– Signing in works and lands back in Flowplan.
– The first account (with SSO: a member of the admin group) sees Administration.
– Upload a file, restart the container, open the file again – then the volume is mounted correctly.
– With S3: objectStorage.pending drops to 0; the bucket contains flowplan/uploads/ and flowplan/db/; the log shows lines from litestream on start.

en.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Symptom Cause and fix
Sign-in ends with an error about the redirect URI The URI at the provider ≠ APP_URL + /api/auth/callback.
"Invalid request origin" when saving APP_URL differs from the address in use.

No administration visible With SSO the group is missing in the token: check OIDC_SCOPES, OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM, OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP and sign in again. For e-mail accounts an administrator grants the right under Users.
Everything is empty after a restart The volume is not mounted on /app/data.
SQLITE_READONLY or EACCES in the log The host folder does not belong to UID 1000.
Container "degraded" in Coolify The health check port is empty (= 80); enter 3000.
404 through the front proxy No route at the inner proxy: set the host header, turn off TLS to the target, the container must be healthy.

objectStorage.retrying: true The bucket is unreachable or the keys are wrong. Uploads are retried with growing intervals, nothing gets lost locally. Check the endpoint from the container (typos, service only bound to an internal IP).
