The container does not start, the log shows litestream Endpoint, bucket or keys for the database backup are wrong; to narrow it down use FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off.
Push does not arrive WEB_PUSH_SUBJECT is missing, the keys have changed or outgoing HTTPS is blocked.
High CPU load after uploads Text recognition of scanned PDFs; if needed FLOWPLAN_OCR=0.

Other people's changes or live cursors arrive late The proxy buffers server-sent events (/api/documents/live, /api/whiteboards/…/cursors); turn buffering off. Without the channel, Flowplan keeps syncing every few seconds.

en.heading: Desktop apps
paragraphs: The desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux is a slim window around a Flowplan instance. All data stays on the server; new Flowplan features arrive with the server and need no app update. The app has its own repository: flowplan-desktop.

Offline use: works in the desktop app as in the browser, including the AppImage on Linux. Turn it on in the app itself under Settings → Offline & devices, because the app, the browser and the installed web app store separately. Without a connection the app opens the copy from the instance's service worker, also when another page of the instance fails to load; the app's own offline page only appears without a copy. If the option is missing, the address is not HTTPS with a valid certificate (the service worker needs a secure connection; http://localhost works for tests). See Work without a connection.

en.heading: Download
paragraphs: flowplan.org/download detects the system and downloads the latest version; every file is listed below. The same files are in the latest release:
System File Architecture
macOS 12 or newer Flowplan--mac.dmg Apple Silicon and Intel in one app
Windows 10 or newer Flowplan--windows-setup.exe, the .zip without installing x64 and ARM in one installer
Linux Flowplan--linux-.AppImage, or the .tar.gz x64 and ARM

On first start the app always asks for the instance's address, suggesting https://app.flowplan.org (HTTPS, http://localhost for local tests); more instances are added as profiles (see below). For managed installations --server= or the environment variable FLOWPLAN_SERVER suggests their own address instead – the first start still asks to confirm it. The app checks that Flowplan really runs there (/api/health answers with "service": "flowplan") and refuses addresses that redirect to another site.

Signing in with passkeys and SSO: passkeys, and providers that ask for one, only work in a real browser. The app therefore opens the sign-in in the default browser: it creates a random secret, opens /api/auth/desktop with its hash, after signing in you confirm Sign in to the app, and the browser hands a one-time code back to the app via flowplan://sign-in. The code is valid for one minute, once, and only together with the secret that never leaves the app. If the browser asks whether it may open Flowplan, that is this step.

From version 1.0.6 the Mac app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple; macOS opens it without asking. Only versions up to 1.0.5 were unsigned: there macOS blocks the first launch (from macOS 15 allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, up to macOS 14 right-click → Open; if macOS says "damaged", xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Flowplan.app helps). Self-built apps without a certificate behave the same, see flowplan-desktop → Signing. Windows shows SmartScreen (More info → Run anyway), and an AppImage has to be made executable first (chmod +x).

en.heading: Profiles
paragraphs: The desktop app can keep several instances as profiles (how to use them: Several instances). Under the hood:

– Every profile has its own Electron session (persist:profile-): cookies, service worker, offline copy, IndexedDB and cache are separate, also for two profiles on the same instance. Permissions (notifications, microphone) go only to the active profile's instance, and a sign-in started in the browser is dropped on a switch.

– The profiles live in config.json in the app's user data folder (profiles, activeProfile). An address from version 1.0.4 or older becomes the first profile automatically on first start and keeps its session; server still mirrors the active profile, so an older version finds an address after a downgrade.

– --profile= starts the app with a saved profile or switches a running app to it, for example from a Linux launcher. New addresses are not accepted this way; only --server= or FLOWPLAN_SERVER suggest one on first start, as before.
– Removing a profile signs it out of the instance and empties its session on this computer.

en.heading: Updates
paragraphs: The app checks for a newer release 15 seconds after starting, then every six hours and via Nach Updates suchen … in the menu:
Installed as What happens

Windows installer Downloads in the background, with its progress in a small notice in the window and on the taskbar button; then the notice, the menu and the notification area offer Restart, otherwise it installs when the app quits.
Linux AppImage The same – the AppImage replaces itself.
macOS (1.0.6 and later, signed) The same.

macOS up to 1.0.5 (unsigned), Windows ZIP, Linux .tar.gz A notice in the window names the new version and leads to the download page (up to 1.0.8 this was a dialog). macOS only lets signed apps replace themselves – so from 1.0.5 or older download 1.0.6 once; after that the app updates itself.

From the version after 1.0.8 no dialog interrupts any more: the answer to Check for Updates… also appears as a notice in the window. Without a connection the check stays quiet and tries again later. FLOWPLAN_UPDATE_URL on the computer running the app makes it fetch updates from another source – a folder with the same files (latest*.yml and the installers), for example a mirror inside a company network. Not to be confused with the server's variable of the same name, which points the instance's release check at a mirror (see Configuration).

en.heading: Settings, links and launch at login
paragraphs: – The app's settings (notification area icon, open at login, the quick capture shortcut, the spell checker's languages) are in config.json under settings, the pages in windows of their own per profile under pageWindows. The app checks both when reading; anything unknown is dropped.

– flowplan://open?instance=&page= opens a page (see flowplan-desktop → Links). An instance without a profile is only added after asking and the same check as on setup. On Linux this needs the registered desktop file, like the sign-in through the browser.
– Open at login registers a login item on macOS and Windows; on Linux the app writes ~/.config/autostart/flowplan.desktop (or under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME).

– Quick capture and dropped files go to the profile's own instance with its sign-in, through the same endpoints as the web app (capture.record, /api/upload, the Markdown import, /api/import/source); nothing is set up on the server for it.

en.heading: Signing and new versions
paragraphs: New versions are made in the flowplan-desktop repository via Actions → Release → Run workflow: the version goes up, the apps are built and attached for all three systems, and the release is published only once everything is there. Installed apps find it within six hours.

The apps are signed as soon as the secrets CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD (macOS, plus APPLE_ID, APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD, APPLE_TEAM_ID for notarization) or WIN_CSC_LINK/WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD (Windows) are set there; a signed Mac app then updates itself like on Windows. To build yourself: in the repository run npm run dist:mac, dist:win or dist:linux.
Everything in Flowplan is a page in a tree. Spaces structure the tree, workspaces keep teams apart.

en.heading: Structure
paragraphs: Level What it is
Workspace A separate world with its own members, groups, templates and storage quota. Switch with the name at the top of the sidebar.
Space A section in the sidebar, e.g. "Teamspace" or "Private". Open to all members or private.
Page Document, database, whiteboard, journal or dashboard. Pages can have sub-pages at any depth.

en.heading: Page types
paragraphs: – Document: text made of blocks – headings, lists, tasks, tables, code, formulas, diagrams, embeds. See Documents and the editor.
– Database: records with properties, shown as a table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, list, feed, chart or form. See Databases.
– Whiteboard: an infinite canvas with sticky notes, shapes, connectors, pen and frames. See Whiteboards.
– Journal: one page per day, open tasks move along. See Journal.
– Dashboard: tiles with metrics, charts, database views, tasks due and notes. See Dashboards.

en.heading: Page actions
paragraphs: The … menu at the top right of every page offers:
Action Effect
Change icon, change cover Emoji, symbol or your own image; upload a cover image or choose an existing one and set its position.
Full width The content uses the whole window width.
Change font Default, serif or mono for this page.
Lock page Protects against accidental changes until someone unlocks it.
Duplicate A copy including sub-pages, databases and files; internal links point to the copies.
Move Below another page, into another space or workspace.
Save as template See Templates.
Export, print / PDF See Import, export and versions.
Present Show a document as full-screen slides, see Present.
Open a page beside it … Open a second page on the right in the split view.
Owner and review … Who looks after the page and when it should be checked again, see Owner and review date.
Version history Compare and restore earlier states.
Move to trash Removes the page with its sub-pages; restorable.

en.heading: Right-click in the sidebar
paragraphs: Right-clicking a page in the page tree or under favourites – a long press on a phone – opens its actions directly: Open in new tab, Open in split view, Copy link, Add to favourites, Share, Add sub-page, Change icon, Duplicate, Move, Export, Lock page and Move to trash. Actions with a dialog open the page first.

en.heading: Filter pages
paragraphs: The Filter pages field above the page tree hides everything that does not match; parent pages of the hits stay visible and expanded. Esc clears the filter. Templates, media, trash, settings and administration sit as a toolbar at the bottom of the sidebar.

en.heading: Split view
paragraphs: Two pages side by side – say notes on the left and the task database on the right. A page opens on the right with:
– Open in split view in the right-click menu of a page in the page tree,
– ⌘-click (Windows/Linux: Ctrl-click) on a page in the page tree, under favourites or on a page link in the text,
– dragging a page from the page tree to the right edge of the window (a drop area appears there),
– ⌘ ⌥ S or Open a page beside it … in the … menu: the quick search opens the chosen page on the right.

Each half has its own header with the title and ×. The × on the left closes the left page and the right one moves into the main view; the arrow on the right brings the right page into the main view. Documents can be edited in both halves; databases, whiteboards and dashboards work as usual.

Drag the divider between the halves with the mouse; with the keyboard, tab to it, then ← / → (with ⇧ in large steps), Home / End for the narrowest and widest position, Enter or a double-click for half and half. The device remembers the width.
Dragging a page from the page tree into a document in the other half inserts a link to it there; selected text and blocks can be dragged between the two documents (they are copied).
The right page is part of the address (?split=…): reloading and bookmarks keep the split view. Windows up to 1024 pixels wide and phones do not have it – there, the same ways open the page as usual.
[!NOTE] Since ⌘/Ctrl-click in the page tree now opens the split view, a multiple selection starts with ⇧-click or the tick icon of the space; after that, ⌘/Ctrl-click adds more pages too.

en.heading: Arrange and move
paragraphs: – Reorder pages in the sidebar by drag and drop, or drag them onto another page to nest them.
– Select pages (the tick icon on a space) or ⇧-click marks several pages that can be moved or deleted together.

– Moving to another workspace takes sub-pages, database records and files along. Shares with groups or people who are not members there are dropped. Databases with relations to databases staying behind have to be detached first.
[!NOTE] Pages keep their address when moved. Links to the page keep working as long as the reader has access in the new workspace.

en.heading: Owner and review date
paragraphs: So that guides, policies and knowledge pages do not go stale unnoticed, every page can have an owner and a review date. Set both under … → Owner and review … (edit rights needed):
– Owner: a member of the workspace (not a guest) who can read the page.
– Next review on: a fixed date, once, or
– Then every … days: a rhythm such as 30, 90, 180 days or yearly. Without a date it starts today.

Once the review date has come, the page shows the hint “This page is waiting for a review (owner: …)” at the top. Reviewed moves the date on by the rhythm, counted from today; a one-off date disappears. The owner gets a reminder on the due day (““Title” is waiting for your review”) – once per review date, in the inbox and, depending on the settings, as push or e-mail (kind “Date reminders”).
[!NOTE] Through the API, the commands page.owner and page.review set owner and review date. A restore archive keeps review date and rhythm but not the owner, who belongs to the old workspace.

en.heading: Aliases
paragraphs: Under … → Aliases … a page gets further names, such as abbreviations ("PAC" for "Chauffage"). Up to 10 aliases of up to 100 characters each; Enter or a comma separates them, duplicates are dropped. Everyone with edit rights may change them.

@ mentions, the quick search and Unlinked mentions find the page by its aliases like by its title; hits show "Title · alias". When you pick a hit found by an alias in an @ mention, the alias becomes the link text. The Markdown export writes aliases as frontmatter (aliases: [PAC]) at the top of the page – only for pages that have some. Records use the property type Aliases; a page that becomes a record takes its aliases there, and the other way round.
[!NOTE] Through the API, the command page.aliases ({ pageId, aliases: [...] }) sets the aliases of a page; an empty list removes them. A restore archive keeps them.

en.heading: Favourites and "Linked from"
paragraphs: The star in the header puts a page under Favourites in the sidebar – personal, others do not see your favourites. At the bottom of every page, Linked from shows which pages and database records refer to it.

en.heading: Manage spaces
paragraphs: Via … next to a space → Edit space … or Settings → Spaces:
– rename it, give it an emoji or symbol and one of nine colours,
– switch the visibility between open (all members) and private,
– Duplicate space: an independent copy of all active pages, records and attachments; comments, versions and shares are not copied,
– Git export (only for the owner of the space, when the administration has switched it on): push the space into a Git repository daily or weekly, see Git export of a space,
– move it to the trash. The last active space stays until there is another one.

en.heading: Order of spaces
paragraphs: Workspace owners decide in which order the spaces appear in the sidebar – the same for every member:
– Drag: grab a space by its header (name and symbol) and drop it above or below another space. A blue line shows where it lands.
– Keyboard and phone: … next to the space → Move up or Move down. Screen readers announce the new position.
– Settings → Spaces lists the spaces in the same order, with arrows to move them.
Other members see the new order within a few seconds, without reloading. Wherever spaces are offered for choice – moving, sharing, the browser extension, record to page – the same order applies.
– New spaces go to the end, a duplicated space right after its original.
– A space restored from the trash returns to its old place.
– A restore archive keeps the order of its spaces; on import they go to the end. Older archives without an order keep their previous one.
– Spaces you cannot see – private spaces of others, encrypted spaces without the key – keep their place. Their names appear nowhere; reordering changes nothing about visibility.

[!NOTE] Through the API the command space.reorder ({ workspaceId, order: [spaceIds] }) sets the order of the spaces you see in the sidebar; only workspace owners may do this. The answer lists the visible spaces in their new order.

en.heading: Collapse and expand spaces
paragraphs: A click on a space's name collapses its pages or expands them again. Each device remembers this for itself. Opening a page in a collapsed space expands it by itself; while filtering the page tree, every space with matches stays open.

en.heading: Trash
paragraphs: Deleted pages and spaces end up in the Trash at the bottom of the sidebar. There they can be restored or deleted permanently. Publications, share links and forms are switched off when deleting and are not switched on again automatically when restoring.

Right after deleting, Flowplan shows a notice at the bottom such as “‘Notes’ moved to the trash” with Undo – for about six seconds, longer while the pointer or the focus rests on it. Undo or ⌘ Z (outside text fields) brings the page back with its sub-pages and opens it again. The same goes for moving pages in the page tree and for several pages at once.

en.heading: Graph of links
paragraphs: The network icon at the bottom of the sidebar (or > graph in the quick search) shows all pages as dots and their links as lines. Database records appear as dots of their own once they link or are linked; a click opens the record. Large dots have many connections; colours tell documents, databases, records, whiteboards and journals apart.
– Drag to pan, scroll or use two fingers to zoom, click to open a page.
– Hovering highlights a page and its neighbours; Highlight marks pages by title.
– Connect sub-pages also shows the page hierarchy (dashed), Pages without links shows or hides single pages.

– Journal days controls the days of journals: hide, one dot per month (default; the dot gathers the links of all days of the month, a click opens the journal) or show each day. The line at the top counts pages and journal days separately.
– Links to pages and records (also from a record's text), embedded whiteboards, linked databases and synced blocks count as connections. The graph only shows what you may see.

en.heading: Unlinked mentions
paragraphs: Below Linked from at the end of a page, Unlinked mentions lists documents and records in which the title of this page appears without being linked (titles of four characters or more), or one of its aliases as a whole word (two characters or more); the alias found is shown in grey next to the hit. Link turns the first mention there into a link to this page, by the title first, else by an alias – the text stays as written. An open record shows the same for its title and aliases below its properties.

Block extensions bring custom block types into the editor: a poll, a counter, a chart from a database, your team's own widget. An extension is a static web page with a manifest. Flowplan shows it isolated in a frame and only talks to it through messages.

en.heading: For owners: register an extension
paragraphs: – Your administrators allow the address: either through PLUGIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (configuration) or with the switch Block extensions from any HTTPS address under Administration → Extensions & domains.

– Under Settings → Block extensions enter the address at Address of the extension, e.g. https://plugins.example.org/poll/, and choose Register. Flowplan loads flowplan-plugin.json from there, checks it and shows the extension as a card of its own: which blocks it brings and what it may do, below that the switches Active and Also show on published pages. It is removed with the trash icon at the top of its card.
– In the editor its blocks appear in the / menu under Extensions.
Per extension there is:
– Active – when off, its blocks only show their text.
– Also show on published pages – without this switch its blocks appear on published pages as text only.
– Databases it may read – only when it requests database access.
– Settings – as the manifest describes them. Everyone who sees the block also sees the settings: do not enter passwords.
Registering again reloads the manifest (new version, new block types). Removing it leaves the blocks in the documents; they then show their text.

en.heading: What an extension may do – and what not
paragraphs: The frame has sandbox="allow-scripts" and never allow-same-origin, so the extension runs in an anonymous origin of its own:
– It reads neither Flowplan's cookies nor its storage and cannot change the page around it.
– It knows neither the name nor the e-mail address of the person reading.
– Forms, pop-ups and redirecting the whole page are blocked.
– Every message is checked: sender (exactly this frame), shape (zod schema), the nonce from the handshake. More than 60 messages per second are dropped.
– Height: the extension asks for a height; Flowplan keeps it between 40 px and the manifest's maxHeight (at most 2000 px).
Permissions a manifest can request:
Permission Meaning
read:page Title of the page the block is on.
read:selection The text selected in the editor.
write:block Store its own data in the block (JSON, at most 64 KB) – only for people with edit rights.
read:database: Read records of exactly this database (ID of the database page).
read:database Read records of the databases an owner picks when registering.

Database queries always run with the rights of the person reading: private records and properties with a read rule stay hidden. Published pages never query databases, and blocks there are always read-only.
The text an extension hands over with its data goes into search and the Markdown export. In the export a link to the extension takes the frame's place.

en.heading: For developers: build an extension
paragraphs: An extension is a set of static files served over HTTPS. A complete example (counter and poll) lives in the repository under examples/plugin-hello/.

en.heading: The manifest
paragraphs: flowplan-plugin.json next to the entry page:
"name": "Hello Flowplan",
"description": "A counter and a small poll",
"entry": "index.html",
"blocks": [
{ "type": "counter", "label": "Counter", "icon": "🔢", "description": "A number to count up" },
{ "type": "poll", "label": "Poll", "icon": "📊", "entry": "poll.html" }
"permissions": ["read:page", "write:block"],
"size": { "height": 160, "maxHeight": 600 },
"settings": {
"step": { "type": "number", "label": "Counter step", "default": 1 }
Field Rule
name 1–60 characters.
version 1.2.3, optionally with a suffix (1.2.3-beta.1).
entry Relative path of the page in the frame (default index.html); no .., no other address.
blocks 1–20 block types: type of lowercase letters, digits and -; label; optionally icon (emoji), description and an entry of its own.
permissions See above.
size Initial height and maxHeight in pixels (40–2000).
settings Up to 20 settings: string, number or boolean with label and default.
The manifest must not redirect to another address and may be at most 64 KB.

en.heading: Security headers
paragraphs: Serve the page with a strict Content Security Policy, for example:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'
connect-src 'none' makes sure block data does not leave the frame. If the extension needs a server of its own, name it there explicitly.

en.heading: The message protocol
paragraphs: All messages are objects with protocol: "flowplan-plugin/1". After loading, Flowplan sends:
{ protocol: "flowplan-plugin/1", type: "init", nonce, blockType, readOnly, permissions, settings }
From then on every message of the extension carries this nonce. Answer with ready first; Flowplan then sends the stored data as data.
From the extension Fields Answer
ready – data with the stored data
resize height – (the height is capped)
getData id response with result = data
setData id, data, optionally text (search text, up to 2000 characters) response; errors read-only, permission:write:block or too-large
getContext id response with theme, locale, readOnly, blockType, page.title (with read:page), selection (with read:selection)
query id, databaseId, optionally limit (1–200) response with fields and rows; errors public or permission:read:database:
Answers look like { protocol, nonce, type: "response", id, ok: true, result } or { …, ok: false, error }. When others change the data (simultaneous editing, undo), data arrives again.
A minimal example:
const PROTOCOL = "flowplan-plugin/1";
let nonce = null;
const send = (message) => parent.postMessage({ protocol: PROTOCOL, nonce, ...message }, "*");
addEventListener("message", (event) => {
if (event.source !== parent || event.data?.protocol !== PROTOCOL) return;
const message = event.data;
if (message.type === "init" && !nonce) {
nonce = message.nonce;
send({ type: "ready" });
} else if (message.nonce === nonce && message.type === "data") {
document.body.textContent = JSON.stringify(message.data);
send({ type: "resize", height: document.documentElement.scrollHeight });
Messages to Flowplan go out with the target "*": the frame has no origin of its own that Flowplan could name. Flowplan recognises senders by the frame and the nonce.

en.heading: Try it
paragraphs: – Serve examples/plugin-hello/ over HTTPS (for example behind your reverse proxy).
– Set PLUGIN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://plugins.example.org and restart Flowplan.
– As an owner register https://plugins.example.org/plugin-hello/ and type /counter in the editor.
Tools for teams that work with tickets – all optional: a database behaves as before until you set one of them up.
Most of them sit in the … menu on the right of a database's toolbar: record templates, Automations, Workflow and done, Time report and Git connection.

en.heading: Ticket numbers
paragraphs: A property of the type ID (ticket number) shows a running number for every record, such as WEB-123.
– You choose the prefix when adding the property; it is unique in the workspace.
– Numbers are never handed out twice, not even after deleting. A restored record keeps its number.
– In text, WEB-123 is highlighted in every document: hovering shows title and status, ⌘/Ctrl-click opens the record. This also works for text written before the ID property existed.
– Search finds records by their number, and Git commits can refer to them (see below).

en.heading: Subtasks and epics
paragraphs: The type Parent record (subtasks) lets records sit below another record of the same database – for example epic → story → task. Flowplan refuses loops.
– In the record, the Subtasks section lists everything below it with its state; you add new subtasks right there.
– In tables, View → Show subtasks as a tree indents records and lets you fold them.
– Subtask progress is a property of its own: it shows the share of done work across all levels as a bar.
– On boards, Swimlanes by with the parent property gives epic swimlanes.

en.heading: When is a record done?
paragraphs: Sprints, progress, overdue records and “My tasks” need to know when a record is done. Flowplan detects it:
– from a status select with an option like “Done” or “Erledigt”,
– otherwise from a “Done” checkbox.
Set it under … → Workflow and done when it should be different.

en.heading: Workflows
paragraphs: In the same dialog, switch on Set allowed changes and required properties:
– Allowed changes: in the “from (row) to (column)” table, untick changes such as “Open → Done”. A record then has to be “In progress” first.
– Required properties: a status needs certain properties – e.g. “Done only with a solution”.
– Owners only: some statuses can only be set by people with the owner role on the database.
The rules apply everywhere: table and board, bulk edits, guests and the Git connection. A change that does not fit is refused with an explanation.

en.heading: Automations
paragraphs: … → Automations takes care of recurring steps in the form When … only if … then …:
– When: a record is created, a record arrives through a form, a property changes (optionally to a certain value), a date has passed or it is time according to a schedule (see Scheduled automations).
– Only if (optional): conditions such as “Priority is High” or “Assignee is empty”.
– Then: set properties or notify.
– Values for properties can be fixed, or today, now, the person who triggered it or the creator.
– You can notify the person in a person property, the creator, the person who triggered it or a specific member.
Suggestions add the usual rules in one click:
– “When Status → Done, set a date”,
– “When the due date has passed, notify”,
– “Assign new form records”.
Each rule can be switched off on its own.

[!NOTE] Rules run on the server, however a record changes. What a rule changes does not trigger further rules, so rules cannot loop. Flowplan checks overdue records every few minutes; each rule fires once per record and date. Notifications appear as “Database automations” and can be switched off in the settings.

en.heading: Scheduled automations
paragraphs: With the trigger it is time (schedule) a rule creates a new record regularly, for weekly reports, monthly closings or maintenance:

– When: daily or every N days, weekly or every N weeks on a weekday, or monthly or every N months on a day (the 31st becomes the last day in shorter months), each at a time in your time zone. Examples: “Every Monday at 09:00”, “Monthly on day 1”, “Every 3 days”.
– Then: Create a record from a record template (properties and text) or empty. Date fields can be set relative to the run, e.g. “Due: +3 days”; 0 means the same day.
The suggestion “Create a record every Monday at 09:00” sets this up with the default template.

[!NOTE] A scheduled rule runs once per date – also after a restart – and only from the moment it was saved. Dates on which the server was not running are not made up one by one; the latest missed one runs once. The rule creates records on behalf of the person who last changed it; if they lose edit rights or the database is locked, the rule rests. Switching it on or off does not change the person.
Repeating tasks, whose next record only appears once the previous one is done, are set in the record, see Repeating tasks.

en.heading: WIP limits
paragraphs: On a board, View → WIP limits sets a maximum per column, e.g. “In progress: 3”.
– The column header then shows 2/3.
– When it holds more, the column is marked.
– With lock, the column takes no further records – wherever they come from.

en.heading: Sprints
paragraphs: A view of the type Sprints (backlog and planning) plans work in time boxes. Set up sprints adds the “Sprint” property and the first sprint the first time.
– Planning: drag records from the backlog into a sprint – or use Move to, also on phones.
– A sprint has a name, start, end and goal; + Sprint adds the next one.
– Start and Complete: when completing, choose where unfinished records go – the next sprint or back to the backlog.
– Measure size in: number of records or a number property such as story points.
– Burndown: the running sprint shows the work left per day against the ideal line.
– Velocity: closed sprints show what was committed and what was completed.

en.heading: Time tracking
paragraphs: A property of the type Time tracking adds up the time worked on a record. Optionally it shows an estimate from a number property in hours next to it.
– In the record: Start and Stop – each person has at most one running timer, a new one stops the old one.
– Add time: a duration as 45, 1:30 or 1.5h, with a date and a note.
– Correcting: you delete your own entries; owners can correct everyone's.

– … → Time report: the time report of this database, switchable to the whole workspace (see Time reports and billing). The report across all databases is also under Settings → Time; there the filters carry their labels above the report, two side by side on phones.

en.heading: Time reports and billing
paragraphs: The time report sums up the time entries of a database or of the whole workspace.
– Period: This week (from Monday), This month, Last month or a custom period with start and end date (at most three years). The server's time zone applies.

– Filters: person, database (in the workspace), project, billing status and billable yes/no. Project is the record a record's first relation points to (not the parent relation of subtasks) – such as the project of a task. Records without a relation are listed under No project.

– Group by person, project, record, database, day or week. The totals come first (total, open, billed, not billable and – with hourly rates – the amount), then a bar chart and a table per group. Clicking a bar filters by that person, project or database.
– Time entries: the single entries with date, person, record, project, note, duration and billing status (the first 1000; the export contains all).

– Export: CSV (commas, decimal points) for spreadsheets and scripts, CSV for Excel with semicolons, decimal commas and a BOM, as a German Excel opens it correctly with a double click. Cells a spreadsheet would run as a formula start with an apostrophe.
– Print outputs totals, chart and table (also save as PDF); expanded time entries come along.

Who sees what: everyone sees their own time entries and the entries of others on records they may read. If the permissions of the property (who may read it, see Property visibility) hide the time property from someone, they only see their own time there. Own time on a record that has become private since appears without a title as “Record without access”.

Billing status: every time entry is open, billed or not billable. Whoever may edit the record and the time property changes the status – one by one in the list of time entries, or with Mark as billed for all open entries of the current selection. Entries that are not billable stay as they are, as do running timers. Every change is in the activity log (time.billing).

Hourly rates (optional): workspace owners set a rate per person and/or per project under Hourly rates, plus the currency (e.g. EUR, CHF). A project's rate takes precedence over the person's. Members with edit rights in the workspace see amounts; readers and guests see hours only.

Through the API: GET /api/time-reports with page or workspace and the same filters (format=csv or format=excel for the files), POST /api/time-reports with { "action": "billing", "status": "billed", "filter": { … } }.

en.heading: Git connection
paragraphs: … → Git connection connects the database to GitHub, GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo:
– Set up Git connection creates a webhook address and a secret.
– In the repository, add a webhook with both:
– content type JSON,
– events for pushes and pull or merge requests. The exact steps are in the dialog.

– Commits and pull requests that mention a ticket number of this database like WEB-123 appear in the record under Development. Numbers of other databases are left alone – they have their own connection.
– “closes WEB-123” (also fixes, resolves) marks the record done. This happens once the commit is on the default branch or the pull request is merged – through the database's workflow and automations.
Every request is checked against the secret. Only people who may edit the database see the address and the secret. New address and secret invalidates the old ones.

en.heading: Sync GitHub and GitLab issues
paragraphs: A database can keep itself in step with the issues of a GitHub or GitLab repository – both ways or only one. Unlike the Git connection, which only links commits and pull requests, records and issues are created and updated on both sides here.
Setting up the connection (workspace owners and administrators):
– Settings → Calendars & issues → Connect GitHub or GitLab.

– Choose the provider; for an own server enter its address (empty for github.com or gitlab.com), the repository (owner/name) or project (group/project) and an access token that may read and write issues – on GitHub a fine-grained token with Issues: Read and write, on GitLab a token with the api scope.
– Test connection makes one call with the token; Save stores the token encrypted. It is never shown again.
– Optional People: one login = e-mail of a member per line. Assignees are matched through it.

– For immediate updates, add the shown webhook address with the secret in the repository – on GitHub with content type JSON and the events Issues and Issue comments, on GitLab as Secret token with Issues events and Comments. Without a webhook, Flowplan syncs every 10 minutes.

The sync acts as the person who set up the connection: they need edit rights on the database, and records they may not read are skipped. If they are no longer an owner of the workspace, the connection pauses until someone saves the token again.
Mapping a database: … → Sync issues in the database. There you choose the connection, repository and direction (both ways, only issues → database, only database → issues) and map properties:
Issue Property
Title Title
Description (Markdown) a text property or the record's document
Open/closed and labels a select – per option "open" or "closed", optionally with a label (e.g. Doing → open + in progress)
Labels a multi-select (only labels that exist as options)
Assignee a person (through the connection's people list)
Milestone due date a date (an existing milestone with that date is set)
Number and address number/text or URL – read-only

Two switches handle comments: issue comments appear as record comments (with name and link), and record comments go out as issue comments. Also take over existing issues fetches all existing issues on the first run; otherwise only what changes after saving. New records become issues once the mapping is saved – older records stay as they are.

Conflicts: if both the record and the issue changed since the last sync, the later change wins. The decision is written to the audit log. Each record is linked to at most one issue; the record then shows a chip like GitHub #123 with a link.

Status: the dialog shows the last pull and push, conflicts, skipped records and errors; Sync now starts a run right away. When the provider reports a rate limit, Flowplan waits for the time it gives. A repository can only be connected to one database. Disconnect ends the sync; records and issues stay.
Administrators allow own servers (GitHub Enterprise, self-hosted GitLab) with ISSUE_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

en.heading: Records from all databases
paragraphs: My tasks → Records from databases shows records from every database of the workspace in one list. By default these are the open ones assigned to you – through any person property.
– You can filter by due date, database and text.
– Save as view turns a filter into a personal view of its own, e.g. “All my open tickets in all projects”.

en.heading: Import from Jira and Trello
paragraphs: Settings → Import & export → Import → Jira or Trello takes a Jira CSV export (all fields) or a Trello JSON export.
It becomes a new database with a table and a board. It brings over:
– status or list, priority, type, labels, dates and story points,
– assignees – as a person property when they are all members,
– checklists, and parent issues as subtasks,
– descriptions as content and comments as comments,
– attachments as links (the files stay at Jira or Trello).
Relations connect databases, rollups calculate across linked records, formulas calculate values from the properties of the same record.

en.heading: Edit properties
paragraphs: A click on the column header or View and properties opens the property dialog: name, type (one of {{facts.fieldTypes}} property types), options and format. Changing the type keeps existing values as far as they fit. Number formats cover currencies, percent, decimal places and thousands separators and also apply to formulas with a numeric result; date fields show short, long or ISO dates and optionally times; Remove date below the field clears it again.

en.heading: Aliases
paragraphs: The property type Aliases (other names) holds further names of a record, such as "PAC" and "Pompe à chaleur" for the record "Chauffage". A database has at most one such property. In the record you enter the names separated by commas; up to 10 aliases of up to 100 characters each count, surrounding spaces and duplicate names (ignoring case) are dropped.
Aliases work like the title:
– @ mentions and the quick search also find the record by an alias and then show the real title with the alias in grey: "Chauffage · PAC". In the search, aliases weigh as much as the title.
– Unlinked mentions also look for every alias – as a whole word, from two characters, ignoring case. Link keeps the text as written: "PAC" becomes a link to "Chauffage" that still reads "PAC".
– The Markdown export writes them as aliases: into the frontmatter, the Markdown import reads aliases: and alias: back (Frontmatter).

Filters ("contains", "is"), sorting, formulas (as a list, like multi-select), CSV and the other exports treat aliases as a list of texts. An alias may be used by several records; then both appear. Only people who may read a record find it by its aliases.
Pages keep their aliases under … → Aliases … – see Pages and spaces.

en.heading: Property visibility
paragraphs: Single properties such as "Salary" or "Internal note" can be limited to certain people. In the property dialog, the Visibility section sets who may read the property and who may edit it:
Choice Read Edit
Everyone with access (default for reading) Everyone who may read the database –
Editors and owners (default for editing) Edit and owner roles Edit and owner roles
Owners only Owners of the database Owners of the database
Selected groups Members of these groups Members of these groups with edit rights
– Only owners of the database change the visibility; they always see and edit everything themselves.

– Restricted properties show a lock in the column header. Whoever may not read a property does not get the column at all; cells someone may only read are read-only and say on hover who may edit them ("Editable only by …").
– The rules only narrow page and record permissions: whoever may only view the database does not edit a property for "selected groups" either.
– Everyone with access always sees the title property (the first one).

– The server enforces the rules everywhere: in the database itself, in linked views, dashboards, whiteboard cards, exports (Markdown, CSV, JSON, Word, EPUB, print), versions, through the API and the MCP server, for the AI and in calendar subscriptions. It refuses changes to properties someone may not edit – in the record, through bulk editing, import, API, AI or CalDAV – with a message.
– Restricted properties are never public: publications, links with their own permissions, forms, the customer portal and webhooks leave them out, even when a link allows editing.
– Full-text search and the AI's semantic search do not index restricted properties, for anyone.

– Formulas, rollups, AI properties, progress and time that read a hidden property count as hidden for that person as well – their result would otherwise give the value away. A formula with a computed prop() name depends on every property. A rollup is hidden when the person may not read the property in the target database.

– Whoever does not see a property can neither lose nor delete it when changing the schema. Versions of a database with restricted properties are restored by owners only, and records with hidden properties cannot be turned into a page or moved to another database (copying leaves the hidden values out).
Filters and sorting of a view that use a hidden property work on empty values for that person; the condition itself (such as the value compared with) stays stored in the view.

en.heading: Relations
paragraphs: – Add property → Relation and choose the target database.
– Optionally in both directions: the target database gets a counterpart property, and changes are kept in sync on both sides.
– In the cell, search for records and link them; several links can be removed one by one or cleared together.
Relations appear as links in the record. The database search also finds records by the names of linked records, and relation filters offer these names directly.

en.heading: Rollups
paragraphs: – Create a relation first.
– Add property → Rollup, then choose the relation and a property of the target database.

– Choose a calculation – 22 are available, depending on the type: original values, unique values, count, empty/not empty (also as a percentage), sum, average, median, minimum, maximum, range, checked/unchecked, earliest and latest date, date range.
Number rollups appear as a number, progress bar, progress ring or rating, with an adjustable target value. Values from databases someone may not read are not loaded for that person.

en.heading: AI properties
paragraphs: When AI is switched on, a property can take its value from an instruction to the AI – such as a summary or a category from other properties. Everything about it under AI in databases.

en.heading: Formulas
paragraphs: Choose the type Formula in the property dialog. The editor offers 58 functions with search, categories, signatures and examples, suggestions while you type and a live preview on a record of your choice.
round(prop("Effort") * prop("Hourly rate"), 2)
if(prop("Done"), "✓", concat(format(dateBetween(prop("Due"), today(), "days")), " days"))
– References with prop("Name") stay valid when the property is renamed.
– Syntax errors show their position and prevent saving.
– Numeric results are available in filters, sorting, charts and column calculations.
– Date functions calculate in UTC unless a zone is given; now() and today() update every minute.
– Formulas do not run JavaScript; length, nesting and result size are limited.

en.heading: Function groups
paragraphs: Group Examples
Logic if, ifs, coalesce, and, or, not, empty
Numbers sum, average, min, max, round, ceil, floor, abs, mod, pow, sqrt
Text concat, length, contains, replace, replaceAll, trim, slice, lower, upper, format, toNumber
Date now, today, parseDate, formatDate, dateAdd, dateSubtract, dateBetween, year, month, day, hour, timestamp
Lists list, count, at, first, last, join, split, unique, sort, reverse
The formula editor shows the complete list.
The quick search finds content right down into file attachments. The inbox and push notifications tell you when someone needs you.

en.heading: Quick search
paragraphs: ⌘ K (Windows/Linux Ctrl K) or Search in the sidebar.
It searches:
– page titles and aliases as well as document text,
– database records and their content,
– comments,
– file names,
– the text of PDF attachments (up to 50 MB, the first 100,000 characters),
– scanned PDFs and images with text recognition (German and English, French on request via FLOWPLAN_OCR_LANGS),
– Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument files.

Hits can be filtered by type and space. Journal days come after all other hits; Without journal days leaves them out completely and stays on for the next search. File text is indexed in the background and can be found after a few seconds. The search only shows what you may read. Enter opens the first hit.

Aliases of pages and records weigh as much as the title. When the search only matches an alias, the hit shows the real title with the alias in grey, e.g. "Chauffage · PAC". The same applies in the @ mention dialog.

en.heading: Commands
paragraphs: The same quick search also runs commands: if the input starts with >, only commands appear, such as > new database, > tasks, > dark or > focus; Enter runs the first one. Matching commands also appear above the search hits without >. With a page open there are page commands as well: favourite, follow, comments, export, print/PDF, version history, share and focus mode.

en.heading: Saved searches
paragraphs: Save frequent searches including their filters with Save search. Saved searches are personal and appear when you open the search.

en.heading: Inbox
paragraphs: The Inbox collects:
– mentions,
– comments and replies to your posts,
– date reminders,
– comments and records from guests via share links,
– pages and workspaces shared with you,
– changes on pages you follow (you follow your own pages when creating them; the bell at the top right toggles following),
– messages from automations.

By default, what concerns you directly – mentions, shared pages, comments, reminders – arrives in the inbox, as push and by e-mail. Guest comments come without e-mail. Changes on pages you follow and automations only land in the inbox, so that not every small edit triggers a push message or e-mail. Settings → Notifications changes this per kind and channel; Reset to defaults restores the starting point.
Unread items are marked and can be filtered. A click opens the spot, for text comments the thread directly.

en.heading: E-mail
paragraphs: If a mail server is set up on the instance, unread notifications arrive by e-mail as a digest after ten minutes – one mail for everything that has piled up, each notification at most once. Under Settings → Notifications, the E-mail column can be switched on and off per kind. Invitations to a workspace and pages shared with you arrive by e-mail right away.

en.heading: Weekly digest
paragraphs: Under Settings → Notifications → Weekly digest you subscribe to an e-mail that arrives every Monday at 7 am in your time zone (your browser's time zone is saved when you switch it on):
– Changed in pages you follow – with the workspace and who changed it (changes of the last seven days, by others only),
– Overdue tasks and Open tasks – as in My tasks, across all workspaces.

With a short AI summary of the changes (only shown when AI is on for you) puts a few bullet points before the list. The AI only reads pages it may read for you, with your AI provider. If AI is off or the request fails, the e-mail comes as a plain list. If there is nothing to report in a week, no e-mail is sent. The digest needs a mail server to be set up.

en.heading: Push notifications
paragraphs: Under Settings → Notifications:
– Enable push – the browser asks for permission. This applies per device.
– In the card Notification kinds, set the switches Inbox, Push and E-mail per kind – every change is saved at once. On a phone every kind is a card of its own with three labelled switches.
– Use Send test notification to check that everything arrives (see below).
Push notifications open the page concerned. No document content appears on the lock screen.
[!NOTE] iPhone and iPad (iOS 16.4 or later): open Flowplan in Safari over HTTPS, Add to Home Screen and start it from that icon. Only there can push be enabled.
Signing out, the end of a session or a locked account end the push subscription; enable it again after the next sign-in if needed.

In the apps for iPhone, iPad and Android, notifications come through the app: it asks for permission after the first sign-in, and the number of unread ones shows on the app icon. Notification kinds apply there as well. These notifications are end-to-end encrypted and therefore show their text – the relay, Apple and Google cannot read it, see Push relay.

en.heading: Test notification
paragraphs: Settings → Notifications → Send test notification immediately sends a notification "Test notification – everything works." to all your push targets: every browser with push enabled and every app with notifications allowed. It takes the same way as every notification – Web Push, the push relay or Expo – but leaves nothing in the inbox. Tapping it opens these settings.
After at most ten seconds, each device is listed with the channel it went through (Relay · end-to-end encrypted, Expo or Web Push) and what happened:
– Delivered – handed to Apple, Google or the browser's push service. If nothing shows up anyway, check the device: are notifications allowed for Flowplan? An active Focus is mentioned.
– Registration expired – open the app once, it registers again. For a browser whose subscription expired, enable push there again.
– Notifications turned off – allow them in the app or in the device's system settings.

– Push relay not set up, unreachable or instance not verified – this concerns the instance, not your device; the message gives the reason (e.g. PUSH_RELAY=off, APP_URL without HTTPS, /.well-known/flowplan-push not reachable). See Configuration.
– No devices registered – enable push above or open the app and allow notifications.

The test only goes to your own devices, regardless of Notification kinds and Focus filters – the device's own permission and Focus still apply. At most five tests in ten minutes. The result never shows tokens or keys; administrators also see a diagnostics line with the relay address, whether /.well-known/flowplan-push is enabled and the instance's address (APP_URL).

The desktop app has no Web Push. It asks for new notifications itself and shows them as system notifications, with the unread count on the app icon. There, Settings → Notifications shows a switch for the app's notifications instead of Enable push; Do Not Disturb and All Profiles are in the app's Notifications menu. Notification kinds apply here too: only kinds with push pop up.
Share at the top right of every page handles three things: who in the workspace may access it, named links for outsiders and publishing on the web.

en.heading: Access in the workspace
paragraphs: Pages inherit the permissions of their space and parent pages (Inherited). In addition, individual people or groups can be given permissions:
Role May
View Read and comment
Edit Change content, records and views
Private spaces and pages are only visible to the people they are shared with. Guests only see what has been explicitly shared with them (see Workspaces, members and permissions).

en.heading: Share a page with a person
paragraphs: A page or database can be shared with someone who is not in the workspace – without taking them into the whole workspace. Share → People with access to this page: enter an e-mail address (members are suggested), choose View or Edit, Add.

– The person already has an account on this instance (with a confirmed address): they have access to the page and its sub-pages right away and get a notification in the inbox ("… shared “Page” with you") and – when the instance sends e-mail – right away an e-mail with a link to the page. Settings → Notifications → Pages shared with you turns the e-mail off. If they are not in the workspace yet, they join as a guest and see only what is shared with them.

– No account yet: they get an invitation by e-mail (when set up) and are listed as "Invited". Once they create an account with this address, the page is there. The same goes for an account whose address is not confirmed yet – then only the invitation link (Settings → Members → Pending invitations → Copy link) opens the page.
– Guests do not see the list of people with access; only those who may share see e-mail addresses. Each person sends at most a few dozen invitations an hour, and each address gets only a few e-mails.
– In the list, roles can be changed and people removed. A guest without any shared page left is no longer in the workspace either.
– Owners of the workspace and owners of the page's space may share. Everyone else only sees the list.

en.heading: Links with their own permissions
paragraphs: Under Links with their own permissions you create as many named links as you like, e.g. "Feedback from the customer":
Link permission Visitors may
Read look at the page
Read and comment also comment; comments carry a guest note
Read, comment and edit also change the title, text and visible properties of existing records
– Links work without an account and can be revoked one by one.
– With edit links, guests write along live: changes by members and other guests appear right away, and cursors are visible both ways – guests appear as "Guest · ".
– Optionally they also apply to the sub-pages that exist right now; new sub-pages are not added automatically.
– Edit links cannot change permissions, members, private relations or files properties. Before every guest edit, Flowplan saves the previous content.

en.heading: Password and expiry date
paragraphs: Links with their own permissions and publications can have a password and an expiry date – when creating them or later via Password and expiry date in the share dialog. The list shows "Password" or "expires on …".
– Visitors enter the password once per device. It is valid for up to 12 hours and only for this link; a new password signs all visitors out.
– Ten wrong attempts within 15 minutes block that address for the link.

– Editing links have daily budgets: per link, guests upload at most 200 MB of files per day (20 files per 10 minutes) and send at most 100 MB of changes per day; a document does not grow beyond 3 MB of text through a link. For the whole instance FLOWPLAN_ANONYMOUS_UPLOAD_MB applies on top (Configuration).
– After the expiry date the link only shows "expired" – no content, no files, no live updates.
– You can remove the password or extend the date at any time.
– Password-protected publications cannot be copied into other workspaces.
– The password is stored only as a hash and never shown again.

en.heading: Publish on the web
paragraphs: Enable public link makes the page readable for everyone with the link.
– Also publish the current sub-pages; new sub-pages can be added to the selection later.
– Visitors may copy it into their workspace – only what the publication shows.

– Databases appear with their views – table, board, gallery, list, feed, calendar, timeline and chart (also with series and more values) –, records and record documents. A view is only published if all properties it needs are public. Person properties, relations, formulas, rollups and internal comments stay private.
– Files linked in published pages are public; other uploads are not.
– Switching it off, deleting or moving a page out of the published tree revokes access immediately, including to files.

en.heading: Appearance
paragraphs: Below the public link you set the look of the publication: logo and favicon (an HTTPS address or an uploaded file the publication shows), accent colour, footer text and hide “Published with Flowplan”.

en.heading: Custom domain
paragraphs: When the administration switched it on (Custom domains for publications), a publication can also be shown under your domain, such as docs.example.org:
– Enter the domain under Custom domain.

– At your DNS provider create the TXT record shown: name _flowplan-verify.docs.example.org, value flowplan-verify-…. Alternatively the domain serves the file https://docs.example.org/.well-known/flowplan-verify.txt with this value.
– Point the domain at the Flowplan instance with a CNAME (or A/AAAA) record.
– Choose Check now. The reverse proxy obtains the HTTPS certificate – see Custom domains for publications.

Under the domain there are short addresses (/ for the start page, / for sub-pages), a sitemap.xml and robots.txt of its own, and search engines may index the pages; the /share/… link names them as the canonical address. The domain shows only this publication: no sign-in, no app, no API apart from the publication's read access, no cookies, and the pages cannot be embedded in other sites.
Publications with a password cannot be shown under a custom domain. When the publication ends, the domain answers with 404.
[!WARNING] Embedded videos and external images load content from their provider when viewed. This also applies to published pages.

en.heading: Forms
paragraphs: Forms have a link of their own, see Forms.

Flowplan signs people in with e-mail and password, optionally with passkeys. In addition – or instead – sign-in can go through an OpenID Connect provider (single sign-on), whose groups decide who administers the instance.

en.heading: E-mail and password
paragraphs: Without further setup, the sign-in page shows a form for e-mail and password.
– The first account of a new instance administers it: the sign-in page then offers Create account right away. This account sees the Administration.

– Further accounts are created when the administrators open sign-ups under Instance → Allow sign-ups with e-mail and password – or for addresses with an invitation. Workspaces someone was invited to appear as soon as the address is confirmed via the e-mail link.

– Confirming the e-mail address: if the instance sends e-mail (SMTP_* set), a new account signs in only after the address has been confirmed with the link from the e-mail – the link signs in right away. Trying earlier shows a notice and sends the link again (at most every five minutes); Send the link again also works after signing up. Without e-mail every account counts as confirmed immediately, as does the instance's first account. Admins can confirm an address by hand under Administration → Users → Manage; resetting the password via a link confirms it too. If the address already has an account, signing up shows the same as for a new address, and the account's owner gets a note by e-mail instead – so the page does not reveal which addresses have an account.
– Passwords have at least 10 characters and are stored with scrypt. After 8 failed attempts for an address (or 30 from one IP address) there is a 15-minute pause.

– Forgot password: with e-mail delivery set up, the sign-in page sends a link that is valid for two hours. Without e-mail, the administrators create a link to hand over under Users → Reset link. After a reset all previous sessions are ended.
– Admin right: under Users, the administrators pass it on (Make admin) or take it away; someone always has to administer the instance.

– Everyone changes their name and password under Settings → Account & security (card Profile, or Change password … in Sign-in & security). The name is saved when you leave the field. After a password change all other sessions end; the current one stays signed in.
– Sign-ups and "Forgot password" are limited per address and network address (at most one reset e-mail every five minutes per account).
FLOWPLAN_LOCAL_LOGIN=false turns off e-mail, password and passkeys – then only single sign-on remains.

en.heading: Passkeys
paragraphs: With a passkey you sign in with your fingerprint, face recognition or device PIN, without a password. Passkeys are created under Settings → Account & security → Add a passkey; afterwards Sign in with a passkey on the sign-in page is all it takes.

Under Settings → Account & security, the card Sign-in & security lists password, two-factor sign-in, passkeys and the signed-in devices, each with its state (“Off”, “On · 8 codes left”, “2 passkeys”). Delete account is at the very bottom, in the Danger zone. Addresses such as /#settings/account/passkeys or /#settings/account/two-factor open a card directly.
– Passkeys exist for accounts with e-mail and password. SSO accounts sign in with their provider, which may offer passkeys itself.
– Passkeys belong to the domain in APP_URL. They need HTTPS (or http://localhost during development); a bare IP address does not work. Whoever changes the domain creates the passkeys anew.
– A passkey can be removed in the settings at any time.
– In the desktop app, Sign in with a passkey and Sign in with SSO open the sign-in in the default browser and hand it back to the app afterwards (Desktop apps).

en.heading: Two-factor sign-in
paragraphs: Accounts with e-mail and password can add an authenticator app, such as Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
– Settings → Account & security → Two-factor sign-in → Set up an authenticator app.
– Scan the QR code with the app – or type the key shown.
– Confirm with the current six-digit code.
– Keep the ten recovery codes safe. They are shown only once, and each works exactly once.
When signing in, Flowplan asks for the code from the app (or a recovery code) after the password.
– A code counts only once; codes from the previous and the next 30-second window are accepted, so a slightly wrong clock doesn't matter.
– Too many wrong codes block sign-in for 15 minutes.

– Passkeys are enough on their own: signing in with a passkey needs no code – even with the app turned on. Whoever wants a code as well turns on Also ask for a code after the passkey under Settings → Account & security → Two-factor sign-in → Manage. Turning it off needs the password or a current code.
– SSO accounts get their second factor from the provider; API tokens are not affected.
– Turning it off and new recovery codes need the password or a current code.
– Forgot password does not skip the second step.
– Lost your phone and your codes? An administrator can reset two-factor sign-in (Administration → Users).

Admins can require two-factor sign-in for all local accounts or only for admins (Administration → Sign-in & SSO). Accounts without an app and without a passkey then set up a second factor right after signing in, before using Flowplan; accounts with a passkey but no app sign in with the passkey.

[!IMPORTANT] The apps' keys are stored encrypted – with FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, otherwise FLOWPLAN_SECRETS_KEY, otherwise with the generated file secrets.key in the data folder (Configuration). Be sure to back up this file or the key: the instance backup deliberately leaves it out. Without it, only the recovery codes work after a restore.

en.heading: Single sign-on with OIDC
paragraphs: Optional. With OIDC_ISSUER set, the sign-in page shows Sign in with SSO; new people are created on their first sign-in. E-mail accounts and SSO accounts can exist side by side.

en.heading: Create a client at the provider
paragraphs: Register a confidential web client:
Setting Value
Redirect URI https://flowplan.example.com/api/auth/callback
Flow Authorization code with PKCE (S256)
Scopes openid profile email and the scope for groups (often groups)
Groups must be in the signed ID token or in the UserInfo answer
The redirect URI is always APP_URL plus /api/auth/callback.

en.heading: Variables
paragraphs: APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com
OIDC_ISSUER=https://id.example.com/realms/company
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=flowplan
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=secret
OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email groups
OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM=groups
OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP=flowplan-admins
SESSION_HOURS=8
Variable Meaning
OIDC_ISSUER The issuer URL; Flowplan reads the discovery from it (/.well-known/openid-configuration).
OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM The claim with the groups, also as a path such as realm_access.roles.
OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP Members of this group see the Administration. The name is compared exactly.
OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUP If set, only members of this group may sign in.
OIDC_PROMPT_CREATE true: Sign up opens the provider's registration directly (prompt=create).

OIDC_PICTURE Take the profile picture from the picture claim (on by default, off turns it off). The image must be at a public HTTPS address; internal addresses are not fetched – not even via redirects.
SESSION_HOURS How long a session is valid in hours, as long as "Stay signed in" is not used (see Stay signed in).

en.heading: Group names with common providers
paragraphs: – Keycloak: add the "Group Membership" mapper to the client, token claim name groups, turn off "Full group path" – otherwise the group is called /flowplan-admins. For realm roles use OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM=realm_access.roles instead.
– Authentik: the profile scope already delivers groups with the group names.
– Zitadel: roles are under urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:roles; create a claim of your own with an action or enter the path.
– Entra ID: configure the groups claim in the token. Entra delivers object IDs by default; then enter the admin group's ID as OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.

en.heading: Map SSO groups to workspaces
paragraphs: Groups from the identity provider (the claim in OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM) can give membership and groups in workspaces – so you manage access centrally in the provider.
– Admins map groups – for any workspace centrally under Administration → Sign-in & SSO → Map SSO groups centrally, or, where they are owners, under Settings → Groups & permissions → SSO groups.

– Owners who aren't admins see their workspace's mappings there but can't change them. A mapping brings people of the whole instance into a workspace and shows their addresses there – that is the administration's decision.
– A mapping gives a role (View, Edit, Owner), a workspace group (for page permissions) or both.
At every SSO sign-in Flowplan applies them:
– Matching people are added; with several matching groups the highest role wins. Guests stay at "Edit" at most.
– Whoever no longer has the SSO group loses what the mapping gave.

– The mapping always wins. If a mapping matches a person, Flowplan sets the role and groups to what the mapping says – even if the member was added or changed by hand. From then on the membership is managed through SSO.
– Members and group memberships that no mapping matches and that never came from SSO stay untouched.
– The last owner of a workspace always stays.
– Changed mappings apply right away to everyone with an active SSO session, otherwise at the next sign-in (with "Stay signed in" and SESSION_GROUPS_HOURS set, at the latest after that).
– Accounts with e-mail and password are not affected.

Note: changes by hand while SSO is active. If an owner changes the role or a group of a member who comes from an SSO group (marked "via SSO group …" in the member list), the change lasts only until that person's next SSO sign-in or the next change of the mappings. Then the mapping sets the role and groups again. Flowplan says so right after the change. For a lasting difference, the administration changes the mapping – or the person's groups in the identity provider.
In the member list and the group dialog, such members show "via SSO group “X”".

en.heading: User provisioning (SCIM)
paragraphs: With SCIM 2.0 your identity provider creates accounts in Flowplan, keeps name and address up to date and deactivates accounts as soon as someone leaves – without the person having to sign in first. Flowplan speaks SCIM 2.0 as in RFC 7643/7644 (users and groups, filters, PATCH).
Setting up
– Administration → Sign-in & SSO → SCIM tokens: Create token. The token starts with fpscim_ and is shown only once; only its hash is stored. You can revoke it at any time.
– At the provider, enter the SCIM base URL /api/scim/v2 and the token as bearer token.
– Assign people and groups to the app at the provider, or turn on "Push Groups".
What Flowplan does with it

– Accounts: a new SCIM account is an SSO account. If an account with the same e-mail address exists, it is linked instead of duplicated. At the first OIDC sign-in the person takes over the prepared account – by the externalId (= the provider's sub) or a verified e-mail address.

– Deactivating: active: false disables the account as in the administration – all sessions end at once, API tokens stop working. active: true enables it again. Deleting (DELETE) deactivates and unlinks; the content and the account itself stay, final deletion is still done in the administration. The last admin account with a password cannot be deactivated over SCIM.

– Groups: SCIM groups do not create groups in Flowplan. Their display name counts like an SSO group from the token: the SSO group mappings give the role and workspace groups, and all rules from there apply (the mapping always wins, the last owner stays). Membership changes take effect at once, not only at the next sign-in. A person's OIDC groups and SCIM groups are combined.
– Accounts with e-mail and password can be linked and deactivated, but mappings do not change their memberships.
– The last SCIM requests with their status are listed in the administration – useful when the provider reports errors.
Not supported: bulk, sorting, /Me and password changes (Flowplan stores no password for SCIM accounts).

en.heading: SCIM with common providers
paragraphs: – Okta: app integration (SAML or OIDC) → Provisioning → "SCIM connector base URL" = /api/scim/v2, "Unique identifier field for users" = userName, authentication mode HTTP Header with the token. Under "To App" turn on Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users; add groups under Push Groups.

– Microsoft Entra ID: enterprise application → Provisioning → mode Automatic, "Tenant URL" = /api/scim/v2, "Secret Token" = the token, Test connection. Keep userPrincipalName → userName and objectId → externalId in the attribute mappings; set the scope to "Sync only assigned users and groups". Entra works in cycles of about 40 minutes.

– Authentik: Applications → Providers → create a SCIM provider, URL /api/scim/v2, enter the token; attach the provider to the Flowplan application as backchannel provider. Groups are sent with their names.
– Keycloak: Keycloak has no SCIM client of its own; install a SCIM extension (e.g. "keycloak-scim") or use LDAP or OIDC groups.

en.heading: Sign-in with LDAP
paragraphs: With LDAP_URL set, the password field of the sign-in page checks names against an LDAP directory (OpenLDAP, 389 DS, Active Directory, …). The field is then called E-mail address or user name.

– Accounts with e-mail and password keep signing in with their Flowplan password. Every other name is searched with the search account (LDAP_BIND_DN) and LDAP_USER_FILTER below LDAP_BASE_DN, and the password is checked by binding as that person. Empty passwords are never sent; the name is escaped as in RFC 4515, so * or ) in a name do not change the filter.

– An LDAP account is a directory account like an SSO account: the first time it is created by its DN or linked to an existing SSO/SCIM account with the same address. An account with e-mail and password of the same address is never taken over.

– Groups come from LDAP_GROUP_ATTRIBUTE (default memberOf): Flowplan takes the group's name (the first RDN, usually the CN, e.g. flowplan-admins) and the full DN. Either can be used in the SSO group mappings and as OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP.

– Hourly sync: Flowplan reads all LDAP accounts again – groups, name, address. Whoever is missing from the directory or locked there (Active Directory userAccountControl, 389 DS nsAccountLock, OpenLDAP ppolicy pwdAccountLockedTime) is disabled; once they are back, they are enabled again. Accounts disabled by an admin stay disabled. A run that would disable more than half of the accounts (at least five) stops – that is more likely a wrong configuration.
– Two-factor sign-in applies as for passwords: LDAP accounts can set up an authenticator app, and the instance's policy ("admins" or "everyone") applies to them too.
– Administration → Sign-in & SSO → LDAP directory shows the status, Test connection and Sync now with the last result.
Variable Default Meaning
LDAP_URL empty ldap://host:389 or ldaps://host:636. Without it, no LDAP.
LDAP_BIND_DN / LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD empty Search account. Without it, the search is anonymous.
LDAP_BASE_DN – Where people are searched, e.g. ou=people,dc=example,dc=org.
LDAP_USER_FILTER (\ (uid={user})(mail={user})) {user} is replaced by the escaped name. Active Directory: (\ (sAMAccountName={user})(userPrincipalName={user})(mail={user})).
LDAP_GROUP_ATTRIBUTE memberOf Attribute with the person's groups.
LDAP_TLS_CA empty CA certificate for ldaps:// or StartTLS (file path or PEM text). Certificates are always verified.
LDAP_STARTTLS false true: encrypt ldap:// with StartTLS.
LDAP_TIMEOUT_MS 8000 Time limit per LDAP operation.

en.heading: Examples
paragraphs: OpenLDAP (with the memberof overlay):
LDAP_URL=ldaps://ldap.example.org LDAP_BIND_DN=cn=flowplan,ou=services,dc=example,dc=org LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD=… LDAP_BASE_DN=ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
Active Directory:

LDAP_URL=ldaps://dc1.corp.example.com LDAP_BIND_DN=CN=svc-flowplan,OU=Service,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com LDAP_BASE_DN=OU=Staff,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com LDAP_USER_FILTER=(&(objectCategory=person)( (sAMAccountName={user})(userPrincipalName={user})(mail={user})))
Keycloak as the source: Keycloak itself is no LDAP server – connect Flowplan to the same directory Keycloak uses through "User Federation", or use OIDC.

Authentik: create an LDAP outpost (provider "LDAP", base DN e.g. dc=ldap,dc=goauthentik,dc=io), a service account with "Search full LDAP directory" as LDAP_BIND_DN (cn=,ou=users,), LDAP_USER_FILTER=( (cn={user})(mail={user})). Groups are in memberOf.

en.heading: Stay signed in
paragraphs: Normally a session ends SESSION_HOURS after signing in (default 8 hours). With SESSION_REMEMBER=true the sign-in page shows Stay signed in – for password, passkey and SSO. When ticked, the session lives on while Flowplan is used:

– It ends SESSION_IDLE_HOURS after it was last used (default 168 = 7 days) and at the latest SESSION_MAX_DAYS after signing in (default 30). Then you sign in again – this limits how long a stolen cookie is good for.

– SSO sessions extend the same way, up to SESSION_MAX_DAYS. Group changes at the provider follow through SCIM, the LDAP sync or the next sign-in. Only when SESSION_GROUPS_HOURS is set does an SSO session end after that many hours already: signing in at the provider again fetches the current groups, so OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUP and OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP apply by then at the latest, even without SCIM.
– A disabled account loses access immediately, as before.
– The desktop and mobile apps stay signed in once the option is on; they always ask for it.

– When the same person signs in again on a device (for example because the session ran out), the app's registration survives – notifications, widgets, Live Activities and Shortcuts move over to the new session. Only an explicit Sign out (in the app or under Signed-in devices) removes it.

Without SESSION_REMEMBER every session – the apps' too, and with them their widgets – ends SESSION_HOURS after signing in (default 8 hours). If you use the apps or their widgets, set SESSION_REMEMBER=true. Turning the option off later stops the extending; running sessions then end at their next expiry.
Settings → Account & security → Signed-in devices lists all your own sessions with device, last use and end; Sign out ends a single one, Sign out all other devices all but the current one.

en.heading: Security
paragraphs: With OIDC, Flowplan checks the discovery, issuer, audience, signature, PKCE, state and nonce. Sessions are random tokens, stored hashed in SQLite; cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure with HTTPS. Groups or roles are never taken from browser data.
– An account deactivated in the administration loses all sessions immediately; open live connections are closed within 15 seconds at the latest, as they are when read access is withdrawn.

– Every page carries a content security policy: scripts only run with a nonce that is new for every request, frames only come from the supported players (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma, CodePen). The reverse proxy sets HSTS (usually active with Traefik/Coolify).
– Sessions can be revoked individually in the administration.
– Invitations to an e-mail address are only assigned after a sign-in with a confirmed address (email_verified=true with OIDC, the confirmation link for e-mail accounts).

en.heading: Common errors
paragraphs: Symptom Cause
An error about the redirect URI The URI entered at the provider does not exactly match APP_URL + /api/auth/callback.
