No administration visible The group is missing in the token: check the scope, OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM and the exact group name, then sign in again.
"Invalid request origin" APP_URL differs from the address in use (e.g. http instead of https).
Sign-in refused OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUP is set and the person is not a member.
"Create account" is missing Sign-ups are closed: open them in the administration or invite the person.
A passkey cannot be created APP_URL is not an HTTPS domain (an IP address or http:// other than localhost).
All data lives in one directory. With S3 storage, files are mirrored and the database is backed up continuously – the container then holds nothing irreplaceable anymore.

en.heading: What is where
paragraphs: Path in /app/data Content
flowplan.sqlite (+ -wal, -shm) All content, accounts, sessions, settings
uploads/ Uploaded files
web-push-keys.json Push keys, unless set via the environment
ocr/ Language data for text recognition, recreated when needed

en.heading: Turn on S3 storage
paragraphs: With S3_BUCKET and credentials (see Configuration):

– Files: every uploaded file goes into the bucket right after saving, and deleted files are removed there. uploads/ stays the working copy. If a file is missing there – a new host, a lost volume –, Flowplan fetches it from the bucket: right away when requested, all others in the background.
– Database: Litestream transfers changes to the SQLite file to /db about every second. If the container starts without a database, Litestream first restores it from the bucket.

On the first start with S3, Flowplan uploads all existing files. Administration → Storage & backup shows the progress, the connection and the split between local and S3 (cards Backups and Usage); with FLOWPLAN_METRICS_TOKEN, or signed in as an administrator, /api/health shows it under objectStorage.pending.
MinIO, Garage, SeaweedFS, AWS S3 and other S3-compatible services are suitable.

en.heading: Garage
paragraphs: Garage creates neither the bucket nor the keys by itself:
garage status                                  # read the node ID
garage layout assign -z dc1 -c 10G <node ID>
garage layout apply --version 1
garage bucket create flowplan
garage key create flowplan
garage bucket allow --read --write --owner flowplan --key flowplan
garage key info flowplan --show-secret         # key ID and secret
S3_REGION must match the value s3_region in garage.toml.

en.heading: SeaweedFS
paragraphs: Start the S3 service so that it listens on all interfaces (-ip.bind=0.0.0.0), otherwise other containers cannot reach it. The endpoint is the S3 port, 8333 by default.

[!NOTE] Why no Postgres and no Redis? Flowplan works in one process directly on SQLite – faster and simpler for one instance per organisation. Sessions, presence and live sync run through the database and the process itself; Redis would have nothing to do.

en.heading: Backups
paragraphs: – Instance backup in Flowplan (recommended): Administration → Storage & backup → Whole instance → Download downloads the database and files consistently while running.
– S3 with Litestream: a continuous backup; an earlier point in time can be restored (below).
– Scheduled backup: a consistent copy of the database every day or every hour, with S3 in the bucket under backups/, otherwise in the data folder – encrypted when a key is set (Encryption).
– A volume backup on the host or in Coolify. For a consistent copy, stop the container first.
– By hand while running:
sqlite3 /app/data/flowplan.sqlite "VACUUM INTO '/backup/flowplan.sqlite'"
Back up uploads/ and web-push-keys.json as well.
The content archive under Settings → Import & export → Export → Workspace as ZIP backs up a workspace but does not replace an instance backup with accounts and permissions.

en.heading: Encryption
paragraphs: On request, Flowplan encrypts everything it sends out of the server with a key only the server knows (AES-256-GCM). Whoever gets hold of the bucket or a backup – the storage provider, someone with leaked credentials, a bucket made public by mistake – sees only unreadable data.
What Encrypted
Files in the bucket (/uploads/) yes
Scheduled backups (flowplan-….sqlite.enc) yes, in the bucket and in the data folder
Markdown exports (….zip.enc) yes, in the bucket and in the data folder
Downloaded instance backup (….zip.enc) yes
Litestream replica of the database (/db/) no – see Litestream
Git export no – readable Markdown is what it is for
Data folder on the server (flowplan.sqlite, uploads/) no – use the host's disk encryption for that

en.heading: Turn it on
paragraphs: Create a key, set it as an environment variable and restart:
openssl rand -base64 32
# or without openssl:
docker run --rm ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan node /app/decrypt.mjs --new-key
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<32 bytes, base64>
# or as a Docker secret:
FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/flowplan-key

Administration → Encryption then shows “Encryption on” with the key ID (the first bytes of a hash, not the key itself). A malformed key shows up there as an error; backups then fail instead of being stored unencrypted.
[!CAUTION] Without the key, encrypted backups and files are lost – for you too. Keep it apart from the backups (password manager, vault), not in the same bucket and not only on the same server.

en.heading: Existing data
paragraphs: There is no migration step, and nothing is rewritten at startup. Flowplan recognises encrypted data by its first bytes, so unencrypted and encrypted data sit side by side without problems:
– From the moment you turn it on, new files and every new backup and export are encrypted.

– Files already in the bucket stay readable and unencrypted for now. Administration counts them; Encrypt existing objects uploads them once more in the background, this time encrypted, replacing the old object. The app keeps running normally meanwhile.
– Older backups and exports are not rewritten. Over time they drop out of retention (Backups kept), or you can delete them by hand.
– Restore works with both: an unencrypted instance backup can still be uploaded, and an encrypted one is decrypted first.
– If the bucket has versioning, older unencrypted versions of the objects remain. Remove them with a lifecycle rule or by hand.
Turning it off works too: move the key to FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS. Then nothing new is encrypted, but what is already encrypted stays readable.

en.heading: Change the key
paragraphs: – Set the new key as FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY and move the old one to FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS (several separated by commas), then restart.
– Under Administration → Encryption, choose Encrypt existing objects. All files in the bucket are re-encrypted with the new key.
– Keep the old key until the last backup encrypted with it has dropped out of retention.
Every encrypted file names the ID of its key. If that key is missing, Flowplan says exactly that instead of silently returning broken data.

en.heading: Litestream and encryption
paragraphs: Litestream (0.5) cannot encrypt the database replica itself. With a key set, Administration therefore warns that an unencrypted copy is kept under /db/. Two ways out:

– Encrypted backups only (recommended for a bucket you do not trust): set FLOWPLAN_LITESTREAM=off, turn on Hourly instead of daily under Administration → Storage & backup → Backups, and keep more copies (e.g. 72). Then delete the folder /db/ in the bucket. The price: in the worst case you lose the last hour instead of the last seconds, and on a new host you restore the database from the newest backup (below).

– Server-side encryption at the provider (SSE-C): set LITESTREAM_SSE_C_KEY to a key of its own (32 bytes, base64). The provider encrypts the replica and receives the key with every request to do so. That protects against leaked disks or buckets, not against the provider itself. It only works over https and only with providers that support SSE-C (check first). Empty the folder /db/ before turning it on, because a replica made of unencrypted and SSE-C parts cannot be restored.

en.heading: Emergency: decrypt without a running instance
paragraphs: decrypt.mjs needs only Node.js – no database and no running server. It is in the Docker image at /app/decrypt.mjs and in the source at scripts/decrypt.mjs:
# in the folder with the backup
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u)" -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work -e FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY='<key>' \
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan node /app/decrypt.mjs flowplan-2026-10-19-03-00.sqlite.enc
# → flowplan-2026-10-19-03-00.sqlite

The same works for Markdown exports (.zip.enc becomes .zip), for the instance backup and for single objects from uploads/ in the bucket (output .decrypted). Add earlier keys through FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS; --key-file reads the key from a file. The output only appears once the checksum is correct.
The format is openly documented: FPE1 (4 bytes) · key ID (8 bytes) · IV (12 bytes) · data · GCM tag (16 bytes). The first 12 bytes are authenticated as well.

en.heading: More protection
paragraphs: Encryption covers what leaves the server. On the server itself, the database and files are unencrypted, because Flowplan has to read them to show them. To cover that as well:
– Disk encryption on the host (LUKS, an encrypted volume at your provider). You can add it at any time, independently of Flowplan.
– The format carries a version (FPE1) and a key ID. A later switch to another method or key therefore goes the same way as above, without making old backups unreadable.
– Encrypting the running database (SQLCipher) is deliberately not part of this; see the reasoning in issue #32.

– For individual confidential content there are encrypted spaces: they are encrypted in the browser already, so the database, the uploads folder and the backups on the server hold only ciphertext – independently of FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

en.heading: Markdown export and Git
paragraphs: A readable copy outside Flowplan – for emergencies when the instance is down, or as an archive in a Git repository. Administration → Markdown & Git export chooses pages and databases; with every scheduled backup (and with Back up now) each becomes a Markdown ZIP with its sub-pages, comments and earlier versions:

– with S3 in the bucket under /exports/, otherwise in the data folder under exports/; as many are kept as backups (Backups kept). With FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY the ZIPs are encrypted (.zip.enc), the push to Git is not;
– the export reads with the permissions of the person who saved the selection – private records and journals with a PIN stay out;

– file names and paths in the ZIP contain ids, so they stay the same between runs (clean Git diff). Records start with YAML frontmatter, comments are in .comments.md, earlier versions under .versions/.

en.heading: Push into a Git repository
paragraphs: [!IMPORTANT] The instance Git export (EXPORT_GIT_*) is deprecated. It keeps working but is replaced by the Git export of a space, which space owners set up themselves; the administration shows a notice about it. The scheduled Markdown export to S3 or the data folder stays as it is.
With these variables Flowplan pushes every export into a repository itself (Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab) – every page in a folder of its own, one commit per run with changes:
Variable Meaning
EXPORT_GIT_URL https:// address of the repository, without credentials.
EXPORT_GIT_TOKEN Token with write access to that repository. Only in the environment, never in the database or a backup.
EXPORT_GIT_USERNAME User name for the token (default flowplan; GitLab: oauth2).
EXPORT_GIT_BRANCH Branch, default main. An empty repository gets it on the first run.
EXPORT_GIT_AUTHOR, EXPORT_GIT_EMAIL Author of the commits.
EXPORT_GIT_IMPORT true: changes made in the repository since the last run are taken over before exporting.
With EXPORT_GIT_IMPORT=true, changed files are handled like this:
– Records (records//…md) are updated by flowplan.id in the frontmatter; new files become new records.
– Document pages (index.md, pages/…-.md) get the file's text; the previous state stays as a version.

– Journal days (/2026/10/2026-10-27.md) are found by their journal (the folder) and the date; flowplan.id in the frontmatter only counts when it names a day of the same journal. Repositories from older versions, where days were still pages/-.md, keep working: changes to those files are still taken over before the export, then the export writes the days to the new paths and removes the old files. No day is created twice; a renamed journal keeps its days because the folder is matched by its id.
– Database tables, comments and versions are copies and are not read back.

Markdown does not know every Flowplan block (such as columns). Whiteboards are in the repository as SVG images; an embedded board carries an invisible marker (``) that makes it an embed again when changes are taken over from Git – please leave the image and link below it in place. If you edit pages with other such blocks in Git, the previous state is in the version history. The administration shows the state of the last push (commit, changes taken over, errors).

en.heading: Git export of a space
paragraphs: Instead of one repository for the whole instance, the owner of a space sets up a repository for that space themselves: Manage space → Git export (via … next to the space or Settings → Spaces). The administration only switches the feature on:
Variable Default Meaning
SPACE_GIT_EXPORT empty true turns on the Git export of spaces. Without it, space owners don't see it and exports already set up don't run.
SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Git servers, comma-separated, e.g. git.example.org,codeberg.org. When set, only these are allowed; without it, any public https:// server.

SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE empty true also allows internal addresses for the servers listed in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS – for example a Forgejo on the same host that the container reaches via --add-host git.example.org:host-gateway. Only works together with the list; every other server stays limited to public addresses.
In the space, the owner enters:
– the repository address (https://, without credentials), branch (default main), user name and an access token with write access (GitLab: user name oauth2);
– the frequency: daily or weekly, plus Run now;
– optionally comments and earlier versions (.comments.md, .versions/).
What happens:

– The repository gets the Markdown export of the space – every top-level page in a folder of its own (-/), plus index.md and README.txt. Other files in the repository (such as LICENSE or CI files) stay untouched.
– One commit per run, and only when something changed; pages no longer in the space are deleted in the same commit.
– The export reads with the owner's permissions: private records of others and journals with a PIN stay out.
– Export only: Flowplan does not take over changes made in the repository.
– The settings show the last run (commit, files changed, error) and when the next one is due. A failed run is retried after an hour.
Security:

– Flowplan stores the token only encrypted (like the other stored secrets, bound to the space). After saving, the interface only shows whether one is stored; it is not in exports, and in the instance backup only encrypted. A new repository address needs the token again.

– Every address is resolved and checked: internal addresses (localhost, private networks) cannot be reached, redirects are not followed. The only exception: servers the administration lists in SPACE_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS when SPACE_GIT_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true is set as well – for example a Git server on the same host. Even then it stays HTTPS, with the pinned address and no redirects.

– The export ends, and token and working copy (git-export/spaces// in the data folder) are deleted, when the owner turns it off, leaves the workspace, becomes a guest or deletes their account – or when the space gets a new owner or moves to the trash.
Administration → Markdown & Git export shows how many spaces use the Git export and their last errors – without addresses or content.

en.heading: Restore
paragraphs: – From an instance backup: upload it under Administration → Storage & backup → Restore from backup (at the very end). Flowplan checks it and applies it on the next restart; the previous state stays as pre-restore-… in the data directory.

– From a scheduled backup, with the app stopped: decrypt an encrypted one first, then move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside and put the backup in place as /app/data/flowplan.sqlite. With S3, the files follow from the bucket.
– On a new host with S3: start a new installation with the same S3_* variables and an empty volume. Litestream restores the database, the files follow in the background.
– An earlier point in time, with the app stopped:
litestream restore -config /etc/litestream.yml \
-timestamp 2026-09-26T12:00:00Z -o /app/data/flowplan.sqlite
Move the existing flowplan.sqlite with -wal and -shm aside first.

en.heading: Quotas
paragraphs: FLOWPLAN_WORKSPACE_QUOTA_MB or Administration → Limits & retention sets a default quota per workspace; under Administration → Workspaces it can be overridden per workspace. Uploads, copies, templates and imports beyond the quota are refused.
Templates are saved pages – documents, databases or whole page trees – from which new pages are created. On top of that there are record templates within a database.

en.heading: Starter templates
paragraphs: Templates in the sidebar shows {{facts.templates}} built-in templates in {{facts.templateCategories word}} categories, each with example records and fitting views:
Category Templates
Projects Project planning, product roadmap, sprint board, project brief
Meetings Meeting notes, meeting note, 1:1 conversation, retrospective, meeting minutes
Knowledge & documentation Team wiki, how-to guide, decision log, FAQ
Planning & goals OKRs, quarterly planning, content calendar, budget planning
Personal To-do list, reading list, habit tracker, travel planning
Other Contacts & customers, job applications, inventory, event planning
A click asks for a title and space and creates the page. Dates in the examples are set relative to today.

en.heading: Your own templates
paragraphs: – On a page, choose Page actions → Save as template.
– Choose a name, category and visibility:
– Only me,
– Workspace: all members of this workspace,
– All workspaces of the instance,
– Public gallery (administrators only): visible even without an account.

Templates store their own copies of the files and stay usable even if the source page is deleted. Database templates contain views, records with their content, record templates and the form design. Templates can be renamed, made private or shared and moved to the trash.

en.heading: Record templates
paragraphs: In a database, Record templates opens the templates for records: property values and content are applied to every new record. One template can be the default, so that New uses it automatically.

en.heading: Public template gallery
paragraphs: Under /templates, the built-in templates and all templates with the visibility Public gallery are available even without an account, filtered by category, each with a preview. Use in my workspace takes the template over after signing in. Only administrators can add their own templates to the gallery.

en.heading: Whiteboard templates
paragraphs: On a whiteboard, Templates inserts a retrospective, a kanban board, a mind map, a SWOT analysis or a flowchart at the current spot.
A database can have as many views as you like. Every view shows the same records with its own layout, filters, sorting and groups.
New view: + next to the view tabs, then choose one of the {{facts.views word}} layouts. View and properties controls which properties are visible and in which order.

A right-click on a view tab opens its menu: Rename, Duplicate, Settings …, Set as default view, Move left, Move right and Delete view (the records are kept; the last view cannot be deleted). Tabs can also be reordered by dragging, and a double-click renames them.

Default view: the view that appears first when the database is opened – the board instead of the table, for example. Without it, the first view opens. A small star in the tab marks it; it can also be set in the view settings (handy on a phone).

en.heading: Table
paragraphs: – Edit cells directly; open records as a page via their title.
– Move columns by drag and drop, resize them at their edges.
– Choose a calculation below every column.
– Grouped tables fold groups and show summaries per group.

en.heading: Board
paragraphs: The kanban view groups cards into columns, for example by status, select, person or relation.
– Move cards between and within columns by drag and drop: the card lifts, the target column opens a gap, and on release the card settles in. This changes the grouping property.
– New at the foot of a column creates a record right in that group.
– Reorder, hide or collapse columns; "No group" collects records without a value.

– Add group to the right of the columns creates your own status, such as "Waiting for customer": it is saved as a new option of the grouping select property and appears right away as a column of its own.
– Sub-groups also split the board into rows (swimlanes).
– With multi-select and relations, a card can appear in several columns; moving it only replaces the respective assignment.
– Cards can be dragged on touch devices too.

en.heading: Calendar
paragraphs: Month, week and day view by a date field.
– Week and day show an hourly grid with an all-day row and overlaps placed side by side.
– Move appointments in 15-minute steps, extend or shorten them at their edges.
– A click on an hour creates an appointment, All day + an all-day record.
– Every view has its own time zone; without a setting the browser's applies.
– Keyboard: Alt + ↑/↓ moves by 15 minutes, Alt + ←/→ by one day.

en.heading: Subscribe to a calendar
paragraphs: Subscribe in the calendar view creates your personal link for Apple Calendar, Google Calendar or Outlook. It shows the records of this view with its filters – only what you may see – and recurrences as series. The link is secret and shown only once; Create new link invalidates the old one, End subscription switches it off. If you lose access to the database, the link returns nothing anymore.

en.heading: Sync both ways (CalDAV)
paragraphs: In the same dialog, Set up access sets up sync with Apple Calendar, Thunderbird or DAVx⁵ (Android). Events you add, move, rename or delete there land in the database.
– Credentials: you get a server, a username and a password that is shown only once.

– Apple: Set up in Apple Calendar (in the app, in Safari or on a Mac) downloads a configuration profile with the account – install it under Settings → Profile Downloaded. Several calendars at once: Settings → Calendars & issues → Calendars on iPhone, iPad and Mac. By hand: Add account → Other → CalDAV account, type “Manual”.
– Thunderbird and DAVx⁵: they take the calendar address directly.

– Several devices: each profile gets its own access, so a calendar set up on the Mac keeps working when you install the profile on the iPhone. End access or Create new password ends all accesses to this calendar, those of profiles included.
– Permissions: your own rights apply – whoever can only read the database cannot change anything from the calendar. Workflow and automations apply as for any change.
Google Calendar does not support CalDAV accounts; use the calendar sync below for it.

en.heading: Sync with Google Calendar or Outlook
paragraphs: Calendar sync keeps a view with a date and a calendar in Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook / 365 in step both ways – personally, with your own account.
– Settings → Calendars & issues → Connect calendar → Connect Google Calendar or Connect Microsoft Outlook / 365. You sign in with the provider and allow access to your calendars.
– In the database, open the calendar icon next to … (Calendar sync), pick the view, the account and the calendar, and Connect.
What is synced:
– Title ↔ event title.

– Date ↔ start and end: a date without a time becomes an all-day event, a date with a time a timed event. The view decides which date properties are start and end; the time zone of the calendar view applies to dates without their own time zone.
– The record's document ↔ description, as plain text. The description ends with a link back to the record.
– New, changed, deleted – both ways. Events deleted in the calendar move their records to the database's trash.
Good to know:
– Flowplan syncs every ten minutes and only fetches changes; Sync now in the dialog syncs right away.
– Conflicts: when both sides change the same event, the later change wins. The audit log records every conflict.
– Permissions: only records you may see and edit go to the calendar and are changed by it. Workflow and automations apply as for any change.
– Range: events from 90 days back to one year ahead. Recurring events from the calendar arrive as single records; a recurring record goes to the calendar with its first date.
– Disconnect under Settings → Calendars & issues ends every sync of that connection. You can also revoke access in your Google or Microsoft account.
– An administrator sets up the providers once, see Configuration.

en.heading: Sprints
paragraphs: Backlog, sprints with goal and period, burndown and velocity – see Projects, tickets and sprints.

en.heading: Timeline
paragraphs: Bars from a start to an end date field, on a scale of week, month, quarter or year.
– Move bars or drag their edges; the calendar icon opens a date dialog, also for unscheduled records.
– Today jumps to the current date; weekends can be highlighted.
– Keyboard: Alt + ←/→ moves by one day, with ⇧ it changes the end, with Ctrl the start.

en.heading: Dependencies (Gantt)
paragraphs: Records can wait for each other – for example "Print" only after "Proofreading":
– In the timeline's bar, choose a relation of the database to itself under Dependencies – or Set up dependencies creates a "Dependencies" property.
– Link by dragging: drag from the round handle at the end of a bar onto another bar – that one then waits for the first. Links that would create a circle are refused.
– Arrows connect the bars; if a record starts before its predecessor ends, the arrow is red. While dragging, the timeline already warns which record would be too early.

– Move successors along: moving a record moves every record that waits for it, directly or indirectly, by the same number of days – in one step. What counts is the side the link is attached to: the record's end for "End → start" and "End → end", its start for "Start → start" and "Start → end".
– Resolve all conflicts moves every record that starts too early behind its predecessor.
– Highlight critical path marks the records and arrows without slack: if one of them is delayed, the end of the whole plan moves.
In embedded views (linked databases), linking by dragging and Resolve all conflicts are not available – open the database itself for that.

en.heading: Gallery
paragraphs: Cards with a preview image and selected properties. The image comes from the record's content, its cover or a files property, filling the card or fitted in.

en.heading: List
paragraphs: Compact rows with the title and a few properties, good for long collections.

en.heading: Feed
paragraphs: Records including their document content one below the other, like a blog or a log. The title, Open record or the comment count opens the full record. More records load in steps of 20.

en.heading: Chart
paragraphs: Configure chart chooses columns, bars, line or donut, the grouping and the calculation – count, sum, average, minimum, maximum. Date values can be summarised by day, week, month or year. A click on a data point shows the records behind it; Export as CSV exports all values.
– Series split every group by another property, side by side or stacked.

– More values put up to four additional calculations next to the main value, such as "sum of costs" next to "sum of revenue" per month. Every value becomes a series of its own with a legend; series and more values cannot be combined.

en.heading: Form
paragraphs: Collects records through a form, also from people without an account. See Forms.

en.heading: Linked databases
paragraphs: In a document, /db shows a view of an existing database. The embed has its own views, filters and sorting; records and their changes still belong to the source. The source name in the header opens the full database.
Reading it requires access to both the document and the source. The embed grants no additional permissions; Remove only deletes the block.
An infinite canvas for brainstorming, processes and workshops: sticky notes, shapes, connectors, pen, frames and tables – together and live.

en.heading: Tools
paragraphs: Tool Key What for
Select V Select, move, scale and rotate elements; drag a rectangle to select several
Hand H Move the canvas (also with space + drag or two fingers)
Sticky note N Coloured notes with text
Text T Free text
Shape R Rectangle, rounded, ellipse, diamond, triangle, hexagon, star, arrow, cloud
Connector L Straight, curved or elbowed; sticks to elements and follows them
Pen P Draw freehand
Eraser X Delete drawn strokes: just move over them
Frame F Group areas – and slides for presenting
Table G A simple table on the canvas
Comment C Pin a comment to a spot
Stamp E A quick reaction (👍 ❤️ ⭐ ✅ ❓ 🔥 💡 🎉) on an element; once more takes it back
Laser pointer K Point without changing anything: everyone sees a red trail that fades shortly
Also in the toolbar: Insert image, Emoji or sticker, Link page (a card linking to a Flowplan page), Shape library, Timeline, Embed (video, web page or PDF, see below) and Templates (see Templates).

en.heading: Style elements
paragraphs: Selected elements show a bar with colour, font size, bold, alignment, line width and style, Bring forward/Send backward, Duplicate (⌘ D) and Delete (Del). Sticky notes and text can also be hidden – like a spoiler in a document, revealed with a click.
A double click edits an element's text. Copy and paste work within and between whiteboards. Italic and Underline apply to the whole text of an element, like Bold.

en.heading: Group
paragraphs: Select several elements and press ⌘ G (or Group in the bar): from then on they behave like one. A click selects the whole group, and it is moved, scaled at the corners, duplicated, copied, locked and deleted together. Groups can be combined into larger groups.

– A double click on a grouped element enters the group: a dashed outline shows it, and clicks now select single elements inside (in nested groups, the next level). Esc or a click elsewhere leaves the group.
– ⇧ ⌘ G or Ungroup dissolves the outermost group of the selection.
– Copies of a group are a new group of their own. Like every change, grouping is shared live and can be undone with ⌘ Z.

en.heading: Lists, links and tags
paragraphs: Sticky notes, shapes and texts know a few formats right in the text:
You write Result
- item Bulleted list (the Bulleted list and Numbered list buttons in the bar set it for the marked lines)
1. item Numbered list; Enter continues the list, an empty line ends it
bold, italic, underline Emphasise single words – while typing with ⌘ B, ⌘ I, ⌘ U
text Link – Insert a link into the text in the bar puts it around the marked text

Links may only point to https://, http:// and mailto: or to an element of the same board (see below); other addresses stay plain text. Web links open in a new tab. In addition, every element can carry a link of its own (chain icon in the bar); a small icon at its corner leads there.
Tags on sticky notes show as coloured chips along the bottom edge – a tag always has the same colour. In the board search, Only notes tagged highlights all notes with that tag and dims the rest.

en.heading: Links to frames and elements
paragraphs: Copy link to this element (in the bar of a selected element or in the frames panel) copies an address like …/#page=…&item=…. Whoever opens it sees the board zoomed to the element and selected – provided they may read the board.
Inside the board, links to elements fly there: in an element's link field or in the text as To the goal. If the element is gone, a note says so.

en.heading: Mind maps
paragraphs: Select a sticky note, shape or text and press Tab: a connected branch appears on the right, ready to be labelled. Tab on the new branch branches further, ⌥ Enter adds a sibling. The mind map arranges itself: branches sit to the right of their parent, evenly spaced and centred. Arrange mind map in an element's bar rearranges the whole tree. Typing on a selected sticky note starts writing right away.

en.heading: Diagrams: shape libraries
paragraphs: Shape library in the toolbar (or More shapes … in the shape menu) opens a searchable side panel – a sheet from the bottom on phones. A click or Enter puts the shape in the middle of the view, or drag it where you want it; arrow keys move between the shapes. Search works in English and German (“decision”, “Raute”, “gateway” …).
Library Shapes

Flowchart Process, decision, start/end, data, document(s), predefined process, manual input and operation, database, preparation, delay, display, connector, off-page connector, internal storage, merge, loop limit, annotation
BPMN Start, intermediate, end, timer and message events, task, subprocess, user and service task, exclusive, parallel and inclusive gateway, data object, data store, pool, lane, group
UML Class (with compartments), interface, enumeration, actor, use case, component, package, note, lifelines, activation, initial and final node, state, decision, fork, node, combined fragment
ER diagram Entity with attribute rows, weak entity, relationship, (key, multivalued) attribute
Org chart Person, team, open position
Network Server, database server, internet, firewall, router, switch, laptop, workstation, smartphone, tablet, user, Wi-Fi, printer, web
Cloud architecture Compute, object storage, managed database, queue, function, CDN, load balancer, container, API gateway, cache, monitoring, secrets, virtual network, events

Wireframes Browser, smartphone and tablet frames, dialog, buttons, input and search field, checkbox, radio button, toggle, dropdown, tabs, navigation bar, card, list, image and icon placeholders, avatar, text, slider, progress bar

All shapes are vector graphics, take fill, line colour and width from the bar, can be connected and look the same in the SVG, PNG and Markdown exports. A double click edits the text; in classes and entities a line -- separates the compartments (name, attributes, methods). The cloud icons are neutral icons drawn for Flowplan – no logos or icon sets of AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.

Line ends: for selected connectors you choose the start and end separately: arrow, open arrow, triangle (inheritance), diamond (aggregation), filled diamond (composition), circle, dot, cross and the crow's-foot ends for ER diagrams (one, exactly one, zero or one, many, one or many, zero or many).

en.heading: Arrange automatically
paragraphs: Select several connected shapes → Arrange automatically → Top to bottom or Left to right. Flowplan arranges the diagram in layers (with as few crossings as it can), the top left corner stays where it was and connectors stay attached. One ⌘ Z undoes it all at once. Locked elements stay put.

en.heading: Import Mermaid and PlantUML
paragraphs: Simply paste Mermaid or PlantUML text onto the board (⌘ V), drop a .mmd or .puml file on it or choose Import Mermaid/PlantUML … in the menu at the bottom right. It becomes editable shapes and connectors, laid out automatically:
– Mermaid: flowchart/graph (with shapes, labels, subgraphs as frames), sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram (with crow's feet), stateDiagram, mindmap.
– PlantUML: activity diagrams (start, :action;, if/else, while, fork …), sequence, class, use case and component diagrams and @startmindmap.

Everything is read on your device – no PlantUML server, no Java. The dialog shows beforehand what was detected. Lines Flowplan does not understand are skipped and listed with their line numbers; pure styling (style, skinparam, themes) is ignored silently. Limits: 100,000 characters, 400 shapes, 800 connectors, 40 participants in a sequence diagram, files up to 200 KB.
Copy as Mermaid (in the export menu) copies the selected shapes with their connectors – or the whole board – to the clipboard as a Mermaid flowchart, for example for a Mermaid diagram in a document.

en.heading: Wireframes and clickable prototypes
paragraphs: Sketch screens with the wireframe shapes, ideally one frame per screen (with the smartphone frame inside, for example). Select an element – a button, a shape, a sticky note – and set On click → frame in the bar, or On click → back. A small arrow badge on the element shows the link.

Play prototype (shown once there are frames) shows the selected frame – or the first one – full screen. Clicks on linked elements change the screen; a click elsewhere or the Show clickable areas button briefly highlights everything clickable. Back (←), Restart (Home) and Esc to close. Linked elements can be reached with the keyboard too (Tab, Enter).
When copying, duplicating and pasting, links point to the frames copied along; archives and exports keep them.

en.heading: Timelines (roadmaps)
paragraphs: Timeline in the toolbar (or in the shape library under “Planning”) adds a roadmap with a time scale, lanes and bars. While the timeline is selected, move bars right on the board – into another lane, too – and drag their ends to change the start or end. A red line marks today.

A double click or Edit timeline opens the settings: title, scale (weeks, months, quarters), period (up to about three years), today marker, lanes and bars with title, lane, dates and colour (up to 40 lanes and 400 bars).

As the source you can choose a database instead of own bars: records with a date become bars (start, optional end), a select property provides the lanes. The timeline is live: it shows the current state, and anyone who may edit the records moves a record's dates by moving its bar (a time of day is kept). Everyone sees only the records they may read in the database; the records are not stored in the board and therefore do not appear in the board's exports or search.

en.heading: Align, stack and sort
paragraphs: – When moving, edges and centres snap to other elements; orange guides show to which. ⌥ while dragging turns snapping off.
– Snap to grid (grid button at the bottom) snaps elements without neighbours to the 24-point grid.
– Select several elements → Arrange: align left, centre, right, top, middle or bottom, distribute evenly or stack as a row or column.
– For workshops: Group by colour, Group by person (with headings), Sort by votes or Arrange as a grid.

en.heading: Pen and shape recognition
paragraphs: With a tablet pen (such as an Apple Pencil) the stroke width follows the pressure. Choose the colour in the pen menu; with Recognise shapes, drawn lines, rectangles, circles, triangles and diamonds turn into clean shapes (⌥ on release keeps the stroke).

Once you have drawn with a pen on a device, only the pen draws: fingers move and zoom the board, a resting hand leaves no strokes. A hand resting on the screen while the pen draws neither cuts nor moves the stroke. Draw with the pen only in the pen menu switches this off – fingers then draw too, except the hand holding the pen: a touch while the pen draws or hovers, or within a moment after lifting it, moves the board instead. A pen touching down lightly does not start the stroke thick, and the width follows the pressure smoothly. Writing with Scribble in an open text on the board may run past its edges; the text stays open. A hovering Apple Pencil (iPad Pro, iPad Air M2 and later) shows where the stroke starts; the eraser end of a pen erases like the Eraser. In the iPad app, double-tapping or squeezing the Apple Pencil switches to the eraser and back, to the previous tool or to the pen, as set on the iPad. The same applies when marking up images in documents.

en.heading: Images, icons and records
paragraphs: – Images and icons (magnifier in the toolbar) searches freely licensed images on Openverse; chosen images are uploaded to the server, and the credit shows as a tooltip on the image. There is also the icon library in ten colours.

– Crop (in the bar of an image): choose the part with the mouse, a finger or the arrow keys (⇧ resizes). The image itself stays unchanged – Show the whole image undoes the crop at any time, and exports show the cropped part too.

– GIFs: when the instance has a key for GIPHY or Tenor (see Configuration), Images and icons gets a GIFs tab. The search runs through the server; a chosen GIF is stored on the server like the Openverse images (up to 8 MB), and afterwards the board loads nothing from the provider. Without a key the tab is hidden.
– Link page → Record from "…" places a database record as a card. The card shows the title and up to three properties and stays up to date when the record changes; a double click opens it.
Cards of linked documents that are tall enough show the first lines of the page as a small preview.

en.heading: Embed videos, web pages and PDFs
paragraphs: Embed in the toolbar (on phones under More tools) takes a link:

– Videos and web pages from YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, Figma and CodePen – the same list as for embeds in documents. Other addresses are refused. The board first shows only a preview with the provider; the content loads only after a click on Load, in an isolated frame (sandbox), and Close embed unloads it again. YouTube runs through youtube-nocookie.com.

– PDFs: Upload PDF … or drag a PDF file onto the board. The file is stored in the page and counts towards the storage quota; the board shows one page as a preview, with arrows to page through. A double click opens the PDF viewer.
Exports show a card with the provider and link instead of the player.

en.heading: Sticky notes as database records
paragraphs: Turn a brainstorm into a backlog: select notes → As records in database … (database icon) in the bar. Without a selection the dialog takes the notes in view, with a selected frame the notes in it. This works without any AI.
– Choose the target database – you are offered databases you may add records to.

– Mapping: the note's first line becomes the title, further lines the record's content. Optionally the colour becomes a select property (one option per note colour; options with the same name such as "Yellow" or "Red" are preselected) and the note's author a person property.

– Replace with cards swaps the notes for record cards in the same place – connectors then attach to the card. Keep and link leaves the notes and places the cards next to them, joined by a dashed line.

The cards are live: when someone changes the record in the database, the board shows it at once. Others see the new cards like any edit; one ⌘ Z takes the change to the board back in one step (the records stay in the database).
– At most 500 notes at once; the server creates them in batches of 100, progress shows how far it got, Cancel stops – whatever was created already goes onto the board.
– Trying again after an error creates nothing twice.
– Values are checked like every edit: locked properties, existing options, only members as people.

– Split with AI (when AI is available to you): the AI reads the notes' text and fills further properties – such as assignee, due date or priority. A preview first shows the values per note, anything that does not fit is listed with the reason; records are only created after that.
– In the API the command is whiteboard.toRecords.

en.heading: AI on the whiteboard
paragraphs: When AI is on for you, AI in the toolbar (on phones under More tools) opens these features. Without AI the button is missing and everything else works as usual; on boards the AI may not read, the entries are greyed out with the reason.

– Group by theme (AI) – also in the Arrange menu once two notes are selected: the AI finds themes in the selected notes (without a selection: those in view) and arranges them in labelled columns, like Group by colour. Notes without text and those that fit nowhere go under "Other".

– Summarise as a page – reads the board (or the selection or selected frame) and creates a page next to it: summary, themes, Decisions, Open questions and Action items, with a link back to the board. With Take over action items they become real tasks with person and due date where the board names them – they appear in My tasks. Frames become sections; the AI reads large boards in parts, and the page says what was left out beyond the limit of 2,000 elements.

– Create with AI … – a mind map or a flowchart from a description, such as "how a holiday request is approved". It appears in the middle of the view (or to the right of it when something is already there) as normal shapes and connectors; the mind map uses the layout of Arrange mind map. At most 60 and 40 nodes respectively.

Every action shows its progress and can be cancelled; an error shows in the dialog with Try again. The result is an ordinary change to the board: everyone sees it live, and one ⌘ Z takes it all back. Hidden notes stay hidden from the AI; it reads linked pages and records only when it may read them.

en.heading: Navigate
paragraphs: – Zoom with ⌘ + scroll wheel, trackpad gestures or the buttons at the bottom right.
– Show everything (⇧ 1) fits the view to all elements, ⇧ 2 to the selection – with a smooth camera move that any input stops at once.
– Undo ⌘ Z, redo ⇧ ⌘ Z.

– Minimap (map icon at the bottom right, on narrow boards in the View and actions menu): a small overview of all elements with the visible part. Click or drag to go there; with the focus on the minimap the arrow keys move the view. The browser remembers whether it is open.

– Search the board (⌘ F on the board, or the magnifier at the bottom): searches sticky notes, shapes, texts, tables, frames, comments, embeds and page and record cards. Enter and ⇧ Enter (or the arrows) jump to the next or previous match, which is highlighted; Esc closes the search.

en.heading: Work together
paragraphs: – Live cursors: you see the others' pointers with names in real time, as in Miro. Someone working outside your viewport appears as a marker at the edge; a click on it jumps there.
– Changes appear for everyone within seconds, also after a time without a connection.

– A timer for workshop phases, visible to everyone. If you like, background music plays along (Calm, Focus or Lo-fi): choose it in the timer window under Music while the timer runs. It starts and stops with the timer for everyone; volume and mute are up to each person via the speaker icon in the timer. If the browser blocks sound because nothing on the page has been clicked yet, Sound on appears. The music is generated in the browser, without audio files or external services.

– Voting: set the votes per person and start; everyone puts dots on elements, and the result shows the ranking. Anonymous voting shows everyone only their own votes until the vote ends – so nobody influences the others.

– Follow me (person icon at the bottom): everyone else sees your viewport and follows you as you pan and zoom. Whoever pans or zooms themselves stops following and can return with Follow. End lifts it for everyone.
– Comments on spots of the canvas, with replies and mentions.

– Private mode (crossed-out eye icon) for silent brainstorming: anyone who may edit the whiteboard starts it for the whole whiteboard or just one frame. While it runs, everyone sees only their own new notes and elements in that area (outlined, “only you”); of the others' contributions only the number shows, as hidden placeholders – no text, no names. Reveal shows all contributions to everyone at once and ends the mode; anyone with edit rights can do this, even if the facilitator has left. Private content is stored separately on the server and, until it is revealed, reaches neither the others' browsers nor search, exports, previews, the API or AI features. Reloading, a second tab or joining later are no problem; changes made without a connection are sent afterwards.

– Estimate (planning poker): select notes or record cards – or a frame, then everything in it – and choose Estimate. Decks: Fibonacci (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?, ☕), T-shirt sizes (XS–XL) or your own values. Everyone picks a card hidden; you only see who has already estimated. Reveal cards shows the distribution, average, median and whether there is a consensus. Apply result writes the value onto the note as a label – for record cards into a number, select or text property of the record (with the usual permissions). Then Next element or Estimate again.

– Bring everyone here: everyone else jumps once to your current view – unlike “Follow me”, they move freely again afterwards. With a frame selected, the magnet icon brings everyone to this frame. The others see a notice (“Mara brought everyone here”) and return to where they were with Back.

en.heading: Frames panel
paragraphs: Frames (bottom right, or in the View and actions menu) lists all frames with a small preview – on phones as a sheet from the bottom.
– A click on the preview flies to the frame; the name can be renamed right there.
– Dragging the grip (or ⌥ + arrow keys) changes the order – it is the order of the presentation and is saved with the board. Until someone sorts, reading order applies (top to bottom, left to right).
– Hide from the presentation (eye icon) skips a frame when presenting without deleting it.
– Speaker notes per frame, shown only in the presentation.
– Also: Copy link to this element, Export frame and Present from here.

en.heading: Present
paragraphs: As soon as there are frames, Present appears. The frames are shown one after another in the order of the frames panel, filling the screen; hidden frames are left out, and everything outside the current frame fades away. Arrow keys or the buttons page through, End presentation or Esc closes.
– Speaker notes shows the notes of the frame.
– Presenter view opens the same second window as for documents: the current and the next slide, the notes and the elapsed time. Both windows stay in step – you can move on in either of them.

en.heading: Templates
paragraphs: Templates opens a searchable gallery with previews, sorted by category:
Category Templates
Retrospectives Retrospective, 4L retrospective, starfish retrospective
Planning Kanban, user story map, sprint planning, project timeline, Eisenhower matrix, impact/effort matrix
Strategy OKRs, SWOT analysis, lean canvas, business model canvas, customer journey
Ideas Empathy map, brainstorm, mind map
Diagrams Flowchart, decision tree, org chart
Meetings Meeting agenda, icebreaker
A template lands in the middle of the view and is ordinary board content afterwards.

Own templates: Save as template turns the whole board or the selection into a template – For the workspace or Only for me. Comments, votes and stamps stay out; images and PDFs remain files of the workspace. Own templates are in the Own templates tab; the person who saved one and owners can delete it. At most 500 templates per workspace.

en.heading: Import Excalidraw and draw.io
paragraphs: Use Import … at the bottom right – or drop the file onto the board – to bring in drawings from:
– Excalidraw (.excalidraw),
– draw.io / diagrams.net (.drawio, .xml, also compressed and with several pages) and draw.io SVG exports with an embedded diagram.

Shapes, texts, arrows with their connections and labels, freehand strokes, frames, colours, stroke widths, dashes and rotations become whiteboard items. Several draw.io pages are placed side by side, each in a frame of its own. What Flowplan doesn't know (stencils, embeds, external images) becomes a note with its text. Embedded pictures (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are stored as files of the page and count towards the storage quota.
– Dropping such a file into a document creates a new whiteboard below it and embeds it right away.
– In the ZIP import (see Import) .excalidraw and .drawio files become whiteboard pages.
– Limits: 20 MB per file (30 MB unpacked), 3,000 elements, 50 pages. Flowplan fetches nothing from the internet during import; texts are taken over as plain text.

en.heading: Embed and export
paragraphs: – With /board in a document, a whiteboard becomes part of a page; the button at the top right opens it large.
– Export as PNG or Export as SVG saves the whiteboard as an image.

– Export … (PNG, SVG, PDF) opens the export dialog: what (Whole board, Selection or a single frame), the format and, for PNG, the Resolution 1×, 2× or 4×. As a PDF the board comes Everything on one page or with One page per frame in presentation order (hidden frames left out). The export is made in the browser; the server sees nothing of it.
– In the Markdown export, every whiteboard comes along as an SVG automatically.
– The text on the board is searchable and appears in exports.
– Copy as Mermaid takes shapes and connectors along as a Mermaid flowchart (see above).
A workspace belongs to a team: its own members, groups, spaces and templates. Permissions work from the workspace via the space down to the single page and the single record.

en.heading: Workspaces
paragraphs: – Create: the name at the top of the sidebar → Create workspace. The administrators decide whether everyone may do this.
– Switch: via the same name; everyone can be a member of several workspaces.
– Settings → General: change the name and icon (Name & icon). Leaving and deleting are at the end in the Danger zone; when a button is greyed out, the text above it says why.

When leaving, a last owner has to make someone else an owner first under Settings → Members; your own spaces are handed over to a remaining owner of your choice. Deleting is only possible once you have another workspace; it removes all content, templates, files and shares for all members and cannot be undone. Both are confirmed with the workspace's name.

en.heading: Roles
paragraphs: Role May
Owner Everything, plus managing members, groups, spaces (including their order in the sidebar) and the workspace itself
Edit Create and change pages, comment, share
View Read and comment
Guest Only explicitly shared pages and spaces, with view or edit access

en.heading: Invite members
paragraphs: Settings → Members → Invite member opens a sheet (from the bottom on phones): e-mail address, role and – if needed – Invite as a guest. If e-mail is set up on the instance, the person gets an invitation. They create an account with this address – even if sign-ups are otherwise closed – or sign in with SSO; the workspace appears as soon as the address is confirmed. Without e-mail, afterwards copy the invitation link under Pending invitations (Copy link) and send it to them yourself.

Only confirmed addresses: an existing account takes over an invitation on its own only when its address provably belongs to it – confirmed with the e-mail link, by an administrator or by the SSO provider. Otherwise (for instance on an instance without e-mail, where any address can sign up) only the invitation link counts: whoever opens it and signs in or signs up accepts the invitation. So give the link only to the person invited.

Where the invitation arrives: open invitations are listed under Settings → Members → Pending invitations – with role, guest status and shared pages, when and by whom they were invited. There they can be sent again (with e-mail) or withdrawn. The invited person finds the workspace in the workspace switcher at the top left and a notification in the inbox – right away with a new account, with an existing one the next time they open Flowplan (with single sign-on, at the next sign-in). A single page can also be shared without the whole workspace: Share a page with a person.
Existing members can be turned into guests with Make guest and back with Make member.

en.heading: Guests
paragraphs: Guests are people outside the team, such as customers or freelancers. They only see pages and spaces shared with them, including sub-pages, and cannot create pages, invite anyone or change settings. They do not see the workspace's templates, only their own. For people without any account there are links with their own permissions instead.

en.heading: Groups
paragraphs: Settings → Groups & permissions: under Groups create a group such as "Design" or "Sales" and tick members with Manage (with a search when there are many). Under Access to spaces set each space's visibility and below it View or Edit per group; single pages get a group through Share. New members of a group get its permissions right away.
With single sign-on, groups from the identity provider can maintain members and groups automatically – see Map SSO groups.

en.heading: How permissions work together
paragraphs: – The space sets the basis: open to all members or private for the people it is shared with.
– Pages inherit the permissions of their space and parent pages; under Share, people or groups are added.
– Records of a database can be made read-only or private (see Databases).
– Properties of a database can be made visible or editable only for editors, owners or selected groups (see Property visibility).
– Linked databases, mentions and links never grant additional permissions: whoever may not read the source does not see it embedded either.
Owners of a workspace also manage other members' spaces, but do not get read access to their private pages that way.

Encrypted spaces go one step further: there, not only the permission on the server decides but the key. Whoever has not been given the space key reads nothing – not even workspace owners or the administrators. See Encrypted spaces.

en.heading: Storage quota
paragraphs: Every workspace can have a quota. Uploads, copies, templates and imports beyond it are refused. Administrators see the usage under Administration → Workspaces.
